This document is GENERATED (by generate.py, from the shipped tree) — it is the pack's own map of itself. Everything else in the pack is a shipped file reproduced verbatim.
## What this pack is

Navi's development library: the source, guides, changelog and config surface of the Apex build she is running, as retrievable knowledge. It exists so she can answer questions about her own system from the shipped truth — and author chips in the house idiom, from the code that actually ships.
## The version lock

- Generated from: the shipped Apex **v0.6.9** tree (VERSION file: `0.6.9 edge`). - Build stamps: **2026-11-19.41** / seq **41** — the same stamps the running bridge reports about itself. - Regeneration rule: this pack is regenerated from the shipped tree at every release and its version moves with the build
A library that does not match the running build teaches dead APIs, so an out-of-date copy of this pack should be updated, not trusted.
## Quick facts — canonical values, straight from the tree
Which port does the bridge serve on? The bridge serves on port 8675 (BRIDGE_PORT in bridge.py). The llamafile model server endpoint is http://localhost:8080/v1.
Where does Apex install on a machine? Apex installs into ~/.local/share/navi-apex — the install home (DEFAULT_HOME in install.sh). A legacy /opt/navi-apex install is migrated into that home.

Which ports does the Mesh door listen on? The Mesh door's canonical port is 8765; the shipped default listen ports add 8443, 2475 — one door, one certificate, one fingerprint on every port (MESH_DEFAULT_EXTRA_PORTS in bridge.py).

How does Navi discover knowledge packs and chips? Knowledge packs are GitHub repos carrying the navi-rag topic (the catalog search is `topic:navi-rag`); chips are GitHub repos carrying the navi-chips topic.
How is a chip stored? A chip's entire codebase rides inside its PNG image in a tEXt chunk with the keyword "navi-chip" (JSON: name, description, code, output). Share the image and you share the chip.

How large can a knowledge pack be? A knowledge pack holds at most 40 documents, and a document body is capped at 200000 characters at install. The pack index is feature-hashed term vectors of 256 dimensions; retrieval keeps chunks scoring at least 0.18 against the question.
Which build is this library locked to? This pack is version-locked to Apex v0.6.9, build stamps 2026-11-19.41, seq 41.

#!/usr/bin/env python3 """Navi bridge — serves the Apex dashboard and gives it real local powers.

Stdlib only. Endpoints: GET / the dashboard (app/index.html) GET /api/status backend, model, version, llamafile reachability GET /api/update/check -> the Updater's real check: the newest GitHub release on the install's channel (stable = latest full release; edge = newest incl

pre-releases; ?channel= overrides the saved choice) compared against the VERSION file, with the running version's own release page riding along for the panel's dropdown; a check that cannot complete answers ok: False with the reason POST /api/settings/updater-channel {channel} -> persists the Updater's Stable / Edge channel choice in the config's updater block POST /api/update/apply -> starts the end-to-end apply: a worker downloads the latest release's package zip (unwrapping a gzip-wrapped payload first), verifies it is an Apex package, stages it under updates/<tag>/package, then hands the install to a detached helper (written into updates/<tag>/) that outlives this bridge, runs the staged installer (never --fresh), relaunches the app through start.sh, and records the outcome in config/update-result.json GET /api/update/result -> the apply's live record: the step it is on while it runs, and afterwards either the confirmed version before → after or the failed step, its reason, and the manual fallback (staged folder + install command) GET /api/commands the commands actually installed on this machine (a scan of PATH) — feeds command autocomplete GET /api/persona Navi's Soul and Memory documents (config files) POST /api/persona saves edits to those documents POST /api/chat {messages:[...], sudo, operator_name} -> proxies to the llamafile server, with Navi's persona as the system prompt POST /api/shell {command:"...", sudo} -> runs it, returns output
Commands run from the operator's home directory; elevated commands ride sudo mode (below)

POST /api/sudo/arm {password} -> warms sudo's own timestamp once (sudo -v) and enables sudo mode; the password is never stored, logged or synced POST /api/sudo/disarm -> disables sudo mode and kills the timestamp (sudo -k), instantly and totally GET /api/sudo/audit -> the append-only record of the elevated commands Navi has run (never rides Sync) POST /api/shell/session/open|input|close, GET /api/shell/session/state -> the per-chat interactive shell sessions (CLI Mode, below) GET /api/github -> GitHub account state: repo/issues URLs, whether an OAuth client id is configured, sign-in state, backup settings, last backup/import records (Settings → GitHub & Backup reads it) GET /api/github/pulse -> the project pulse for AlexKollar/ Apex (description, stars/forks/watchers, latest release, recent commits, open-issue count, last push), live, no auth GET /api/github/issues -> the repo's current open issues, live from the public API, no auth POST /api/github/client-id {client_id} -> stores the OAuth App client id (a config value, not a secret) POST /api/github/settings {backup_repo, backup_private, backup_items, backup_interval_days} POST /api/github/signin/start -> Device Flow: asks GitHub for a user code the operator enters in their browser POST /api/github/signin/poll -> one poll of the token endpoint; on success the token is stored locally only POST /api/github/signout -> deletes the local token file POST /api/github/backup {dashboard} -> writes the ready-to-fly essentials to the operator's backup repo POST /api/github/import/preview {dashboard} -> what an import would change, per essential; writes nothing POST /api/github/import/apply -> restores the backup's essentials (only ever called after a preview + confirm) GET /api/sync -> Quick Sync state: the Operator sign-in, the last round's verdict and when it ran (Build 3, issue #176) POST /api/sync/run {openChatId} -> one full Quick Sync round: pull, converge, push — chats and Case Files both ways, over the backup repo, riding the Operator identity GET /api/chips/catalog -> the Navi User Repo (NUR) list: a live GitHub search for repos tagged navi-chips, each with its latest release, merged with the installs recorded in chips/installed.json GET /api/chips/readme?repo=<owner/name> -> a chip repo's README as raw Markdown (the NUR flip cards) GET /api/chips/file?name=<file> -> a chip .png from chips/ POST /api/chips/install {full_name} -> downloads the chip's .py source from the repo at its latest release (or default branch), forges it into a chip in chips/, and records the install in chips/installed.json — the chip joins the folder: pill row, /chip, workflows, execution POST /api/chips/update {full_name} -> moves an install to the repo's latest release / push when newer and re-downloads its chip to match POST /api/chips/delete {full_name} -> removes the install record and the chip's chip file with it POST /api/chips/create {name, description, code, output, files} -> Chip Studio: forges a .png chip into chips/ and registers it as a local install; files is the chip's full file set ([{path, content}] — root.py is the entry, the rest are modules it can import) and rides in the chip beside code GET /api/chips/source?name=<chip file> -> a chip's code and full file set for the Studio editor (local chips) POST /api/chips/save {file, name, description, code, output, files} -> saves the edited file set back into the chip POST /api/chips/run {query} -> executes a chip's chip code (its run() against a stub of navi_internal) and returns the output; /api/chat runs chips the same way when a message invokes one GET /api/rag/catalog -> the RAG tab's Packs list: a live GitHub search for repos tagged navi-rag, merged with the packs recorded in rag-packs/installed.json GET /api/rag/readme?repo=<owner/name> -> a pack repo's README as raw Markdown (the pack flip cards) GET /api/rag/packs -> {packs}: the pack folders on this machine, with documents, chunk counts, and active flags GET /api/rag/pack-source?slug=<folder> -> a pack's name, description, and documents with bodies, for reopening it in RAG Studio POST /api/rag/update-pack {slug, name, description, documents} -> RAG Studio saving an edit into the pack's own folder (documents added/removed), the index rebuilt locally; a GitHub-installed pack is marked locally_edited and its catalog update then refuses rather than overwriting the edits POST /api/rag/install {full_name} -> downloads the pack's .md/.txt/.pdf documents from the repo at its latest release (or default branch), builds its index in rag-packs/<slug>/, and records the install POST /api/rag/update {full_name} -> moves an install to the repo's latest release / push when newer, re-downloading the documents and rebuilding the index (the active flag survives) POST /api/rag/delete {full_name} -> removes the install record and the pack's folder (documents + index) with it POST /api/rag/toggle {full_name, active} -> only active packs feed retrieval in /api/chat POST /api/rag/forge {name, description, documents|source_dir} -> RAG Studio: packages documents (picked files sent as text — PDFs as base64, their text extracted here — or a folder on this machine's disk) into a local pack in rag-packs/, index built, active and ready to use POST /api/rag/export {slug, version} -> builds a GitHub-ready repo ZIP of the pack in rag-exports/: a generated README.md (the pack's GitHub page — installs skip a root README, so it is never indexed), a navi-rag.json manifest, the pack's built index.json (reference copy — installs rebuild it locally from the documents), the documents under documents/, and a .gitignore GET /api/rag/export-file?name=<zip> -> downloads an exported pack repo ZIP from rag-exports/ POST /api/chips/export {file, version} -> builds a GitHub-ready repo ZIP of a local chip in chips-exports/: a generated README.md, a navi-chip.json manifest, the chip's files at the root (root.py entry + importable modules), the chip .png, and a .gitignore GET /api/chips/export-file?name=<zip> -> downloads an exported chip repo ZIP from chips-exports/ POST /api/downloads/save {filename, dataBase64} -> writes a download the dashboard fetched inside the desktop shell (chip .png, export ZIP) into ~/Downloads under a sanitized basename — the shell's webview cannot save files itself GET /api/workflows -> {chips, workflows}: the local chips and the saved chains (chips/workflows.json) POST /api/workflows/create|delete|run -> manage and run chains; a run feeds each chip's output into the next GET /api/voice her voice: settings, engine availability, and the live call state (see Voice, below) POST /api/voice/settings {enabled, stt_model, tts_engine, tts_voice, rate, pitch} -> saves the voice section of navi.config.json POST /api/voice/test {text} -> synthesizes one line and returns it as base64 WAV for the dashboard to play — the "hear her voice" check POST /api/voice/stt {audio_b64} -> one push-to-talk clip in, its transcript out (faster-whisper) POST /api/voice/tts {text} -> one line in, base64 WAV out (Kokoro or Piper) — the call panel speaks her replies sentence by sentence through this POST /api/voice/call/start|turn|end -> the call session: turns are recorded as they happen (voice/state.json) and a finished call is archived to voice/calls.json GET /api/voice/calls -> past calls, newest first /api/chat also accepts "speak": true — the bridge then speaks the reply aloud on this machine as well as returning it (typed chat with a voice)

POST /api/llamafile/connect -> drives the dashboard's status element ("Running" / "Disconnected. Click to Connect."). In app-load startup mode (config "startup": "on-ui-launch") connecting means starting: if the server isn't answering, the bridge launches navi.llamafile from the install location itself and waits for it to answer. In boot mode the bridge only probes — the system service owns the server
A failed start returns the reason (and the server's log tail) instead of a bare probe failure, and the server's output is kept in navi.llamafile.log beside the binary.

Persona: Navi is a partner, not a command executor — conversational, warm, genuinely trying to connect with her operator while doing exact CLI work. Her persona is operator-modifiable, Soul/Memory style: the bridge builds her system prompt from config/soul.md (who she is) and config/memory.md (what she carries), editable in Settings or as plain files. No shards, nothing locked.

Chat CLI access: when a chat message asks for a directory listing ("show me the contents of /path"), the bridge runs ls itself and hands the model the real output to present — the model never guesses.

Command-line fallback: when the llamafile server is not answering, there is no model to proxy to, so /api/chat treats the message as a plain command line — it runs it as a shell command and returns the system output, flagged mode="command-line" so the UI can say so.

Sudo mode (v0.3.0e — Build 3, #209): the operator arms it in Settings with one masked password prompt. The bridge feeds the password once to "sudo -v" and forgets it — never stored, logged or synced; what persists is a single boolean in navi.config.json

While sudo's own credential timestamp lives, elevated commands run as "sudo -n <cmd>" (never prompt); when it lapses the state reads EXPIRED and elevated commands refuse honestly until the operator re-warms. Disarming flips the boolean and runs "sudo -k", so it is instant and total

Every elevated command Navi runs is appended to config/sudo-audit.jsonl (timestamp, command as run, chat served, exit status), surfaced read-only in Settings, and deliberately NOT part of the Sync set

This replaced the parked pre-Build-3 design (a persistent root shell held by the bridge, the password re-sent by the page with every request): the shell was the credential, held root indefinitely, and had no expiry semantics

One cost is accepted knowingly: on machines whose sudo PAM stack tries a fingerprint reader before the password, each fresh "sudo -n" still runs PAM — but "-n" fails fast instead of waiting out the reader, and the arm's one "sudo -v" pays the full conversation once per timestamp window.

CLI Mode shell sessions (Build 3, #209): each chat can hold ONE standing interactive session — a real shell on a PTY, born on first interactive need (the operator opens it, or Navi drives one through a [[shell]] block in her reply), surviving messages and window reloads, closed explicitly or after 30 idle minutes (the thread says so either way)

Output streams into the thread as events badged by author (operator / Navi); a program that takes the alternate screen gets a real terminal grid on the desktop and an honestly-named streamed degradation on mobile. Sessions are local to the seat's bridge and die with it — the thread keeps the record and names the death rather than faking continuity
Elevation never rides the PTY: a session runs under its own session id, so sudo inside it prompts in-terminal.

Voice: Navi can be called and spoken with, and the whole loop is local — she hears through faster-whisper (Whisper on CTranslate2, int8 on CPU) and speaks through Kokoro (an 82M-parameter voice model built for CPU; Piper is the lighter fallback)

The bridge itself stays stdlib-only: the speech engines are optional dependencies (requirements-voice.txt, installed into voice/venv by the installers when the operator says yes) that the bridge imports lazily, only when a voice endpoint is actually used
Until they are importable, /api/voice reports each engine unavailable with the exact step that fixes it — there is no simulated audio path anywhere in the shipped app

Models download once, on first use, into voice/models/ (the STT cache and the Piper voices live there; Kokoro's weights ride inside its package), and that folder is on the same keep-list as the chips and the persona: updates, reinstalls, and --fresh installs never remove it

A call is not a separate mode: its turns go through the same /api/chat as typed chat — persona, CLI access, chips and all — the dashboard records each turn with the bridge, and a finished call lands in voice/calls.json and in the conversation.

Working directory: commands run from the operator's home directory, never from whatever directory the bridge happened to inherit — a bridge started from a folder that later vanished made every command fail with "getcwd() failed". shell_cwd() guarantees a real directory and the bridge repairs its own cwd at startup the same way.

Stale bridges: this bridge serves the dashboard HTML fresh from disk on every request, so after a reinstall the UI is the new build even when the process answering is an OLD bridge that was never restarted — its in-memory code still lacks newer endpoints (sudo auth 404s), sends chat the way the old build did (the llamafile 400s), and runs the old shell code

Three defenses: (1) /api/status reports this build's stamp (BRIDGE_BUILD) and the dashboard warns loudly when the answering bridge's stamp differs from its own; (2) at startup the bridge probes the port — the same build already answering means exit quietly, an older build answering means claim the pid file (bridge.pid) and wait for the port: a bridge from this build onward watches the pid file and this file's mtime and exits with code 75 when replaced, and the launchers relaunch on 75, so updates take over on their own; (3) the installers stop a bridge running from the install directory before replacing files — and since build .91 that stop is a proof, not a gesture: the bridge is found by pid file, by the process holding this port, and by working directory, waited on until it is gone and the port is free, escalated to a forced end if it will not go politely, and the install aborts with the holder named (and the exact kill command printed) if the port cannot be cleared — because a fire-and-forget stop once stranded an update behind a frozen bridge that only a reboot could clear

When this bridge starts against an incumbent that answers nothing, it resolves the holder from the socket itself (port_holder_pid) and names that pid in its messages, pid file or no pid file. The model string sent to the llamafile is read from the server itself (GET /v1/models) rather than assumed, and a server rejection surfaces its own error text.

Wrong server on the port: the bridge is not the only thing that has ever served http://localhost:8675 — the operator's own earlier UI for Navi did too, and if that program is still running it holds the port and answers the browser with its own page while this bridge cannot even bind

Three defenses for that: (1) every response carries no-store cache headers, so no page — ours or a predecessor's — is ever replayed from the browser's cache at this address; (2) the dashboard this bridge serves is stamped with this build and this install folder (an HTML comment at the top of the page), so view- source settles which program served it; (3) at startup the bridge identifies what actually holds the port — probe_port_holder() reads the incumbent's own page title — and the launchers open the browser only when /api/status answers with this build's stamp, naming the incumbent instead of landing the operator on the wrong UI

""" import atexit import base64 import binascii import datetime import gzip import hashlib import hmac import http.client import importlib.util import io import ipaddress import calendar import json import math import os import re import secrets import select import socket import shutil import ssl import struct import uuid import subprocess import sys import tempfile import threading import time import urllib.error import urllib.parse import urllib.request import zipfile import zlib from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
# Guardian (Build 14, #156): the system-monitor engine lives in # its own stdlib module beside this bridge (it never imports the # bridge; the bridge imports it)

The try/except is for benches # and partial copies that carry bridge.py alone — a real install # always ships guardian.py next to bridge.py (the packager and # the installer both carry it), and GUARDIAN below falls back to # an inert stub only when the module truly is not there. try: import guardian as guardian_mod except Exception: guardian_mod = None

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) CONFIG_PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "config", "navi.config.json") SOUL_PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "config", "soul.md") MEMORY_PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "config", "memory.md") # The app's version lives in exactly one place: the VERSION file at # the top of the install folder — one line of plain text (e.g. # "0.1.0 alpha")

The bridge reads it and reports it on /api/status; the # dashboard displays that value in the side menu and the status # column, and an update checker compares this same file against the # latest release. Installers write it with each build; nothing else # stores the version. VERSION_PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "VERSION")
# The release this bridge shipped in, baked at export — the fallback # when the VERSION file itself is missing (an install made by a # pre-.47 installer, which never copied the file, say)

It outranks # anything the preserved config remembers: that config is carried # across installs and written only when missing, so its recorded # version belongs to whichever build installed first — the stale # 1.0.0 placeholder that used to flash in the dashboard's menu # footer and then "revert" the freshly baked number. This constant # is exactly as old as the code answering, never older
SHIPPED_VERSION = "0.6.9" SHIPPED_VERSION_STATUS = "edge"

# This build's stamp — the dashboard baked into the same package # carries the identical value and compares it against /api/status. BRIDGE_BUILD = "2026-11-19.41" # Edge build sequence (build .86): this package is its Edge # version's publication number SHIPPED_BUILD_SEQ — 0.3.0e # Build 3. The Updater's third comparison tier reads it. SHIPPED_BUILD_SEQ = 41 # The one port this build's bridge binds

Deliberately NOT read from # navi.config.json: the launchers poll this port, so a config carried # across from an older package build (which recorded the old port) # must never be able to pin the bridge to a different address than # its own launcher polls. BRIDGE_PORT = 8675 PID_PATH = os.path.join(ROOT, "bridge.pid")

def shell_cwd(): # The one directory commands are allowed to run from by default: # the operator's home — a real directory that exists. The bridge's # inherited cwd is not trustworthy (a launcher started from a # folder that was later moved or wiped leaves every child process # with a dead getcwd), so never inherit it blindly
home = os.path.expanduser("~") if home and os.path.isdir(home): return home if os.path.isdir(ROOT): return ROOT return os.sep

# --- Local server (build .59; fluid activation .61) --------------- # Settings -> System's toggle: OFF (the default) the bridge binds # 127.0.0.1:8675 exactly as it always has; ON it binds 0.0.0.0:8675 # at launch, so a phone or tablet on the same network can open the # dashboard. The flag is read once, here at startup — a bind is # never hot-swapped

Build .61 makes the flip itself do the # restarting: saving the toggle records a restart request in the # config block and this process exits with code 75, the handshake # the launcher's supervise_bridge loop already relaunches on (the # same one an install takeover uses)

The relaunched bridge reads # the saved flag, binds accordingly, and reconciles the recorded # request against its own actual bind (ACTIVE_BIND_HOST): a match # marks the restart confirmed; a mismatch marks it failed at the # verify step, in plain words, with the live state named

The # Settings row reads all of it from the bridge that actually # answers, so it never lies about which state is live, and a # restart that never completes is reported by the dashboard's # confirmation polling as a named failure — never a silent # pending

While the public bind is active, any request from a # NON-loopback address must carry the access code's acceptance # cookie before anything beyond the gate page is served — # dashboard and API alike. Loopback is never gated, so every # internal caller that polls 127.0.0.1 (launchers, the shell, # status probes) works unchanged in both modes

One code, stored # in the config's public_server block; the cookie's value is a # hash of the code, so regenerating the code invalidates every # previously accepted client at once. ACTIVE_BIND_HOST = "127.0.0.1" PUBLIC_COOKIE = "navi_public" PUBLIC_COOKIE_MAX_AGE = 31536000

def public_settings(cfg): ps = cfg.get("public_server") if isinstance(cfg, dict) else None if not isinstance(ps, dict): ps = {} restart = ps.get("restart") if isinstance(ps.get("restart"), dict) else {} return { "enabled": ps.get("enabled") is True, "access_code": str(ps.get("access_code") or "").strip(), "restart_status": str(restart.get("status") or "idle"), "restart_step": str(restart.get("step") or ""), "restart_message": str(restart.get("message") or ""), }

def set_public_restart(cfg, status, step, message): block = cfg.get("public_server") if isinstance(cfg.get("public_server"), dict) else {} block = dict(block) if "enabled" not in block: block["enabled"] = False block["restart"] = {"status": status, "step": step, "message": message} cfg["public_server"] = block save_config(cfg)

def schedule_bridge_restart(): # Exit 75 after the response has had a moment to flush: the # launcher's supervisor relaunches the bridge on 75, and the # new process binds per the saved Local server choice

If no # supervisor is listening (a bridge started by hand from a # since-closed terminal), the process simply stops and the # dashboard's confirmation polling names that failure and tells # the operator to relaunch Apex — a sentence, not a mystery. def _go(): time.sleep(0.6) os._exit(75) threading.Thread(target=_go, daemon=True).start()
def generate_access_code(): alphabet = "ABCDEFGHJKMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789" raw = "".join(secrets.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(8)) return raw[:4] + "-" + raw[4:]

def ensure_access_code(cfg): code = public_settings(cfg)["access_code"] if code: return code code = generate_access_code() block = cfg.get("public_server") if isinstance(cfg.get("public_server"), dict) else {} block = dict(block) block["access_code"] = code if "enabled" not in block: block["enabled"] = False cfg["public_server"] = block save_config(cfg) return code
def public_token(code): return hashlib.sha256(("navi-public:" + str(code)).encode()).hexdigest()

# --------------------------------------------------------------------- # Trusted devices (0.2.0e Build 2, #173): the door stops handing a # full session to anyone who types the code. The code now ASKS: # a device presenting it becomes a pending device (with a name the # visitor gives it), and an already-trusted session approves or # denies it in Settings -> System -> Door

An approved device gets # its OWN session token — 30 days, sliding while it stays in use — # and the operator's device list (name, first/last seen, expiry) # carries a per-device revoke, so one lost phone stops meaning # "change the code and re-let everyone in"

# # Bootstrap: while NO device is approved yet, the first device to # present the code approves ITSELF and receives its token on the # spot — a single-operator house is never locked out of its own # door waiting for an approver who does not exist yet. From the # first approval on, the shared-code cookie stops being accepted: # every device stands in the registry under its own name

# # The registry lives in the public_server block of the config, # beside the code it grew from. Session tokens are random, are # never shown in any payload (the Settings list carries names and # times only), and a device's cookie value IS its token. DOOR_DEVICE_TTL_SECONDS = 30 * 24 * 3600 DOOR_PENDING_TTL_SECONDS = 30 * 60

def door_devices(cfg): ps = cfg.get("public_server") if isinstance(cfg, dict) else None raw = ps.get("devices") if isinstance(ps, dict) else None out = [] if isinstance(raw, list): for d in raw: if isinstance(d, dict) and d.get("id") and d.get("status") in ("pending", "approved", "denied"): out.append(d) return out

def _door_save_devices(cfg, devices): block = cfg.get("public_server") if isinstance(cfg.get("public_server"), dict) else {} block = dict(block) block["devices"] = devices if "enabled" not in block: block["enabled"] = False cfg["public_server"] = block save_config(cfg)

def _door_prune(devices, now=None): now = now or time.time() kept = [] for d in devices: if d.get("status") in ("pending", "denied") and now - float(d.get("created_at") or 0) > DOOR_PENDING_TTL_SECONDS: continue kept.append(d) return kept
def door_approved_devices(cfg): return [d for d in door_devices(cfg) if d.get("status") == "approved"]

def door_device_for_token(cfg, token): if not token: return None now = time.time() for d in door_approved_devices(cfg): if d.get("token") and secrets.compare_digest(str(d["token"]), str(token)): if float(d.get("expires_at") or 0) > now: return d return None return None
def door_cookie_value(cookie_header): for part in (cookie_header or "").split(";"): part = part.strip() if part.startswith(PUBLIC_COOKIE + "="): return part[len(PUBLIC_COOKIE) + 1:] return ""

def door_gate_acceptance(cfg, cookie_value): # (accepted, device, legacy): a registered device token speaks # for itself; the shared-code cookie is honored only while no # device has ever been approved (pre-registry houses, and the # bootstrap moment itself)

if cookie_value: dev = door_device_for_token(cfg, cookie_value) if dev is not None: return True, dev, False code = public_settings(cfg)["access_code"] if code and not door_approved_devices(cfg) and secrets.compare_digest(cookie_value, public_token(code)): return True, None, True return False, None, False

def door_touch_device(cfg, device): # Last-seen, throttled, and the sliding renewal: a device in # active use never hits its 30 days mid-shift — using it while # valid renews it. Writes at most once an hour per device

now = time.time() if now - float(device.get("last_seen") or 0) < 3600: return devices = door_devices(cfg) for d in devices: if d.get("id") == device.get("id"): d["last_seen"] = int(now) if float(d.get("expires_at") or 0) - now < DOOR_DEVICE_TTL_SECONDS - 86400: d["expires_at"] = int(now) + DOOR_DEVICE_TTL_SECONDS break _door_save_devices(cfg, _door_prune(devices, now))

def _door_new_device(name, user_agent, status): now = int(time.time()) return { "id": secrets.token_hex(16), "name": (str(name or "").strip()[:60] or "Unnamed device"), "status": status, "token": None, "created_at": now, "approved_at": None, "first_seen": now, "last_seen": now, "expires_at": None, "user_agent": str(user_agent or "")[:120], }
def door_create_approved(cfg, name, user_agent): # The bootstrap act: mint an approved device with its own # token, on the strength of the code alone

devices = _door_prune(door_devices(cfg)) dev = _door_new_device(name, user_agent, "approved") dev["token"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32) dev["approved_at"] = dev["created_at"] dev["expires_at"] = dev["created_at"] + DOOR_DEVICE_TTL_SECONDS devices.append(dev) _door_save_devices(cfg, devices) return dev

def door_register_pending(cfg, name, user_agent): devices = _door_prune(door_devices(cfg)) dev = _door_new_device(name, user_agent, "pending") devices.append(dev) _door_save_devices(cfg, devices) return dev

def door_gate_outcome(cfg, name, user_agent, cookie_value): # The gate POST's decision, shared by both doors (the DHD # proxy and the bridge's own public bind): ("session", device) # when the visitor leaves with a token — a renewal, or the # bootstrap — and ("pending", device) when the device must # wait for an approval

ok, dev, _legacy = door_gate_acceptance(cfg, cookie_value) if ok and dev is not None: return "session", dev if not door_approved_devices(cfg): return "session", door_create_approved(cfg, name, user_agent) return "pending", door_register_pending(cfg, name, user_agent)

def door_pending_poll(cfg, device_id): # What a waiting device's poll learns: ("pending", None) while # it waits; ("approved", device) once a trusted session has # approved it — the device record carries the token the poll # response sets as its cookie; ("denied", None); ("gone", None) # when the wait expired or the record was revoked away

now = time.time() for d in door_devices(cfg): if d.get("id") == device_id: if d.get("status") == "approved" and float(d.get("expires_at") or 0) > now: return "approved", d if d.get("status") == "denied": return "denied", None if d.get("status") == "pending" and now - float(d.get("created_at") or 0) <= DOOR_PENDING_TTL_SECONDS: return "pending", None return "gone", None return "gone", None

def door_approve(cfg, device_id): devices = door_devices(cfg) now = int(time.time()) found = None for d in devices: if d.get("id") == device_id and d.get("status") == "pending": d["status"] = "approved" d["token"] = secrets.token_urlsafe(32) d["approved_at"] = now d["last_seen"] = now d["expires_at"] = now + DOOR_DEVICE_TTL_SECONDS found = d if found is not None: _door_save_devices(cfg, _door_prune(devices, now)) return found

def door_deny(cfg, device_id): devices = door_devices(cfg) found = False for d in devices: if d.get("id") == device_id and d.get("status") == "pending": d["status"] = "denied" d["token"] = None found = True if found: _door_save_devices(cfg, devices) return found

def door_revoke(cfg, device_id): devices = door_devices(cfg) kept = [d for d in devices if d.get("id") != device_id] if len(kept) != len(devices): _door_save_devices(cfg, kept) return True return False

def door_cookie_header(token): # A trusted device's cookie: its own token, for its own 30 # days — not the shared code's year. return (PUBLIC_COOKIE + "=" + str(token) + "; Max-Age=" + str(DOOR_DEVICE_TTL_SECONDS) + "; Path=/; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax")
def door_devices_payload(cfg): # The Settings -> Door list: names and times, never tokens

now = time.time() out = [] for d in _door_prune(door_devices(cfg), now): out.append({ "id": d.get("id"), "name": d.get("name") or "Unnamed device", "status": d.get("status"), "firstSeen": d.get("first_seen"), "lastSeen": d.get("last_seen"), "expiresAt": d.get("expires_at"), "expired": d.get("status") == "approved" and float(d.get("expires_at") or 0) <= now, "userAgent": d.get("user_agent") or "", }) return out

def lan_ipv4(): try: s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM) try: s.connect(("8.8.8.8", 80)) ip = s.getsockname()[0] finally: s.close() if ip and not ip.startswith("127."): return ip except Exception: pass try: ip = socket.gethostbyname(socket.gethostname()) if ip and not ip.startswith("127."): return ip except Exception: pass return "127.0.0.1"

# --- WAN detection (build .76, #59) --------------------------------- # The honest address model: a LAN address is never a public address. # The bridge learns this home's public (WAN) address with a small # HTTPS echo lookup - the same class of outbound call the update # check already makes - cached for five minutes, failure-tolerant: # any failure degrades to "undetected" and never blocks an enable

# APEX_DHD_WAN_IP is a diagnostics/test override only; unset in # normal operation. WAN_CACHE = {"ip": "", "state": "undetected", "at": 0.0} WAN_ECHO_URLS = ("https://api.ipify.org", "https://checkip.amazonaws.com", "https://icanhazip.com")

def _ip_is_private_or_cgnat(ip): try: addr = ipaddress.ip_address(str(ip or "").strip()) except Exception: return True if not isinstance(addr, ipaddress.IPv4Address): return True if addr.is_private or addr.is_loopback or addr.is_link_local or addr.is_reserved or addr.is_multicast: return True try: if addr in ipaddress.ip_network("100.64.0.0/10"): return True except Exception: pass return False

def wan_ipv4(force=False): # Returns (ip, state): state is "public" (a routable address was # seen), "behind-nat" (the echo answered with an RFC1918 or CGNAT # 100.64.0.0/10 address - this machine sits behind another router # or carrier NAT), or "undetected" (no echo answered)

now = time.time() if not force and WAN_CACHE["at"] and (now - WAN_CACHE["at"] < 300): return WAN_CACHE["ip"], WAN_CACHE["state"] override = str(os.environ.get("APEX_DHD_WAN_IP", "")).strip() found = "" if override: try: ipaddress.IPv4Address(override) found = override except Exception: found = "" else: for url in WAN_ECHO_URLS: try: req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"User-Agent": "Apex-DHD"}) with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=4) as resp: text = resp.read().decode("utf-8", "replace").strip() cand = text.split()[0].strip() if text.split() else "" ipaddress.IPv4Address(cand) found = cand break except Exception: continue if not found: ip, state = "", "undetected" elif _ip_is_private_or_cgnat(found): ip, state = found, "behind-nat" else: ip, state = found, "public" WAN_CACHE["ip"], WAN_CACHE["state"], WAN_CACHE["at"] = ip, state, now return ip, state

def _fedichat_rooms_path(fed_id): safe = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", "_", str(fed_id or "")) return os.path.join(FEDICHAT_DIR, safe + ".rooms.json")

def _fedichat_room_canonical(d): body = {k: d.get(k) for k in ("room", "fed", "name", "kind", "creator", "members", "ttlSeconds", "caseSlug", "created", "rev", "dissolved")} body["members"] = sorted(str(x) for x in (d.get("members") or [])) return json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()

def fedichat_room_id(fed_id, creator, name, created): seed = "|".join([str(fed_id or ""), str(creator or ""), str(name or ""), str(int(created or 0))]) return "r" + hashlib.sha256(seed.encode()).hexdigest()[:16]
def fedichat_dm_room_id(fed_id, a, b): pair = "|".join(sorted([str(a or ""), str(b or "")])) return "dm-" + hashlib.sha256( (str(fed_id or "") + "|" + pair).encode()).hexdigest()[:16]

def fedichat_general_room(fed): return {"room": "", "fed": fed["id"], "name": str(fed.get("name") or ""), "kind": "general", "creator": str(fed.get("gatewayNodeId") or ""), "members": [], "ttlSeconds": None, "caseSlug": "", "created": 0, "rev": 0, "dissolved": False, "sig": ""}

def _fedichat_room_sane(d): if not isinstance(d, dict): return None room = str(d.get("room") or "") kind = str(d.get("kind") or "") if not room or kind not in ("invite", "dm"): return None members = sorted({str(x) for x in (d.get("members") or []) if str(x)}) if kind == "dm" and len(members) != 2: return None if kind == "invite" and not members: return None ttl = d.get("ttlSeconds") ttl = int(ttl) if isinstance(ttl, (int, float)) and int(ttl) > 0 else None return {"room": room, "fed": str(d.get("fed") or ""), "name": str(d.get("name") or "")[:80], "kind": kind, "creator": str(d.get("creator") or ""), "members": members, "ttlSeconds": ttl, "caseSlug": str(d.get("caseSlug") or ""), "created": int(d.get("created") or 0), "rev": int(d.get("rev") or 0), "dissolved": d.get("dissolved") is True, "sig": str(d.get("sig") or "")}

def fedichat_rooms_load(fed): # [general] + the stored descriptors for this fedinet. out = [fedichat_general_room(fed)] try: with open(_fedichat_rooms_path(fed["id"]), encoding="utf-8") as f: data = json.load(f) for d in (data.get("rooms") if isinstance(data, dict) else []) or []: d = _fedichat_room_sane(d) if d is not None and d["fed"] == fed["id"]: out.append(d) except Exception: pass return out

def fedichat_rooms_save(fed_id, rooms): os.makedirs(FEDICHAT_DIR, exist_ok=True) path = _fedichat_rooms_path(fed_id) tmp = path + ".tmp" with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: json.dump({"rooms": [d for d in rooms if d.get("kind") != "general"]}, f, indent=1) os.replace(tmp, path)
def fedichat_room_find(fed, room_id): room_id = str(room_id or "") for d in fedichat_rooms_load(fed): if d["room"] == room_id: return d return None

def fedichat_room_members(fed, room): # The member set as node ids: the roster for the general # room, the descriptor's set for every other room. if room is None: return [] if room.get("kind") == "general": return [str(m.get("nodeId") or "") for m in _fed_roster_members(fed) if isinstance(m, dict)] return list(room.get("members") or [])

def fedichat_room_display(fed, room, op_names=None): if room is None: return _fedichat_room_name(fed) if room.get("kind") == "general": return _fedichat_room_name(fed) if room.get("kind") == "dm": return "DM — " + str(room.get("name") or "member") slug = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", str(room.get("name") or "room").lower()).strip("-") return "#" + (slug or "room")
def _fedichat_room_sign(d): d = dict(d) d["sig"] = mesh_sign(_fedichat_room_canonical(d)) return d

def _fedichat_room_refusal(fed, d): # Why an offered room descriptor is refused, in words, or # "" when it may land. The creator signs; nobody else can # mint or revise a room, and a descriptor for a room this # node does not belong to is not refused — it is simply # never materialized (the caller filters first: gossip # only carries rooms the receiver belongs to)

d = _fedichat_room_sane(d) if d is None: return "it is not a room descriptor — refused as malformed" if d["fed"] != fed["id"]: return "it belongs to a different fedinet — refused" members = {str(m.get("nodeId") or ""): m for m in _fed_roster_members(fed) if isinstance(m, dict)} creator = members.get(d["creator"]) if creator is None: return ("its creator (" + (d["creator"][:12] or "?") + ") is not on the current roster — refused") if d["kind"] == "invite" and d["creator"] not in d["members"]: return "its creator is not among its members — refused as malformed" if d["kind"] == "invite": rid = fedichat_room_id(d["fed"], d["creator"], d["name"], d["created"]) if rid != d["room"]: return "its id does not recompute from its facts — refused as tampered" if d["kind"] == "dm": rid = fedichat_dm_room_id(d["fed"], d["members"][0], d["members"][1]) if rid != d["room"]: return "its id does not recompute from its member pair — refused as tampered" pem = str(creator.get("publicKeyPem") or "") if not pem or not mesh_verify(pem, _fedichat_room_canonical(d), d["sig"]): return "its creator signature does not verify — refused as tampered" return ""

def fedichat_rooms_merge(fed, offered): # Converge offered descriptors into the local store. # Adoption is monotone: a new room lands; a higher rev # from the same creator replaces; an equal-rev conflict # keeps the descriptor whose creator... is the same by # construction — the tie breaks on the signature bytes so # every node settles identically. Returns # {accepted: [room ids], refusals: [{room, reason}]}

rooms = fedichat_rooms_load(fed) by_id = {d["room"]: d for d in rooms} accepted, refusals = [], [] changed = False for raw in (offered or []): d = _fedichat_room_sane(raw) if d is None: refusals.append({"room": str((raw or {}).get("room") or ""), "reason": "it is not a room descriptor — refused as malformed"}) continue reason = _fedichat_room_refusal(fed, d) if reason: refusals.append({"room": d["room"], "reason": reason}) continue held = by_id.get(d["room"]) if held is None: by_id[d["room"]] = d accepted.append(d["room"]) changed = True elif d["rev"] > held["rev"] or (d["rev"] == held["rev"] and d["sig"] > held["sig"] and _fedichat_room_canonical(d) != _fedichat_room_canonical(held)): by_id[d["room"]] = d accepted.append(d["room"]) changed = True if changed: fedichat_rooms_save(fed["id"], list(by_id.values())) return {"accepted": accepted, "refusals": refusals}

def fedichat_room_create(cfg, fed, name, kind, members, ttl=None, case_slug=""): # The creator's act (the dashboard door calls this): mint # a room, sign its descriptor, hold it locally, and let # the next exchange gossip it to its members. Returns # (descriptor, error)

ms = mesh_settings(cfg) own = mesh_node_id() or ms["nodeId"] if _fed_member(fed, own) is None: return None, "This node is not on that fedinet's roster — no roster entry, no room." kind = str(kind or "invite") if kind not in ("invite", "dm"): return None, "A room is an invite room or a direct message — the general room already stands." roster = {str(m.get("nodeId") or "") for m in _fed_roster_members(fed) if isinstance(m, dict)} members = sorted({str(x) for x in (members or []) if str(x)}) if kind == "dm": others = [x for x in members if x != own] if len(members) != 2 or own not in members or len(others) != 1: return None, "A direct message holds exactly two members — you and one other." if others[0] not in roster: return None, "That member is not on this fedinet's roster." room_id = fedichat_dm_room_id(fed["id"], members[0], members[1]) held = fedichat_room_find(fed, room_id) if held is not None: return held, None # idempotent per unordered pair other = _fed_member(fed, others[0]) d = {"room": room_id, "fed": fed["id"], "name": str((other or {}).get("name") or others[0][:12]), "kind": "dm", "creator": own, "members": members, "ttlSeconds": None, "caseSlug": "", "created": int(time.time()), "rev": 1, "dissolved": False} else: name = " ".join(str(name or "").split()).strip() if not name: return None, "An invite room needs a name." if own not in members: members = sorted(set(members) | {own}) strangers = [x for x in members if x not in roster] if strangers: return None, "Every member of an invite room stands on the fedinet's roster — one named member does not." created = int(time.time()) d = {"room": fedichat_room_id(fed["id"], own, name, created), "fed": fed["id"], "name": name, "kind": "invite", "creator": own, "members": members, "ttlSeconds": int(ttl) if ttl else None, "caseSlug": str(case_slug or ""), "created": created, "rev": 1, "dissolved": False} d = _fedichat_room_sign(d) rooms = fedichat_rooms_load(fed) rooms.append(d) fedichat_rooms_save(fed["id"], rooms) _fedichat_note_write(fed["id"]) return d, None

def fedichat_room_revise(cfg, fed, room_id, members=None, case_slug=None, dissolve=False): # A creator-signed revision: the member set, the case # tie, or the room's dissolution. Only the creator's node # can revise — the signature is the authority, and every # revision is auditable in the descriptor's rev chain

ms = mesh_settings(cfg) own = mesh_node_id() or ms["nodeId"] d = fedichat_room_find(fed, str(room_id or "")) if d is None or d.get("kind") == "general": return None, "No such room on this fedinet." if d["creator"] != own: return None, "Only the room's creator can change it — the descriptor is creator-signed, and this node is not the creator." d = dict(d) if members is not None: roster = {str(m.get("nodeId") or "") for m in _fed_roster_members(fed) if isinstance(m, dict)} members = sorted({str(x) for x in members if str(x)}) if d["creator"] not in members: members = sorted(set(members) | {d["creator"]}) strangers = [x for x in members if x not in roster] if strangers: return None, "Every member of an invite room stands on the fedinet's roster — one named member does not." if d["kind"] == "dm" and len(members) != 2: return None, "A direct message holds exactly two members — its set does not change." d["members"] = members if case_slug is not None: d["caseSlug"] = str(case_slug or "") if dissolve: d["dissolved"] = True d["rev"] = int(d.get("rev") or 0) + 1 d = _fedichat_room_sign(d) rooms = [d if x["room"] == d["room"] else x for x in fedichat_rooms_load(fed)] fedichat_rooms_save(fed["id"], rooms) _fedichat_note_write(fed["id"]) return d, None
# -- Build 2: media blobs + presence (memory only) ----------
def _fedichat_media_path(sha): return os.path.join(FEDICHAT_MEDIA_DIR, str(sha or ""))

def fedichat_media_store(data): sha = hashlib.sha256(data or b"").hexdigest() path = _fedichat_media_path(sha) if not os.path.isfile(path): os.makedirs(FEDICHAT_MEDIA_DIR, exist_ok=True) tmp = path + ".tmp" with open(tmp, "wb") as f: f.write(data or b"") os.replace(tmp, path) return sha

def fedichat_media_read(sha): if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", str(sha or "")): return None path = _fedichat_media_path(sha) if not os.path.isfile(path): return None try: with open(path, "rb") as f: data = f.read() except Exception: return None if hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest() != str(sha): return None # a blob that does not recompute is not served return data

def _fedichat_media_gc(fed): # Collect blobs no held line of this fedinet references # any more (a vanishing prune or a dissolution orphaned # them). Blobs are content-addressed and shared across # fedinets on this node, so the reference scan covers # every fedinet this node sits in — a blob another # fedinet still references is never collected here

try: referenced = set() for f2 in federation_settings(load_config()): for room in fedichat_rooms_load(f2): for m in fedichat_log_read(f2["id"], room["room"]): media = m.get("media") if isinstance(media, dict) and media.get("sha"): referenced.add(str(media["sha"])) if not os.path.isdir(FEDICHAT_MEDIA_DIR): return for name in os.listdir(FEDICHAT_MEDIA_DIR): if re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", name) and name not in referenced: try: os.remove(os.path.join(FEDICHAT_MEDIA_DIR, name)) except Exception: pass except Exception: pass

def _fedichat_presence_note(fed_id, room_id, author, state): key = (str(fed_id or ""), str(room_id or ""), str(author or "")) if state: _FEDICHAT_PRESENCE[key] = {"state": str(state)[:40], "at": int(time.time())} else: _FEDICHAT_PRESENCE.pop(key, None)

def _fedichat_presence_map(fed_id, room_id): now = int(time.time()) out = {} for (f, r, a), v in list(_FEDICHAT_PRESENCE.items()): if f == str(fed_id or "") and r == str(room_id or "") \ and v.get("state") and now - int(v.get("at") or 0) <= FEDICHAT_PRESENCE_TTL: out[a] = v["state"] return out
def _fedichat_path(fed_id): safe = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", "_", str(fed_id or "")) return os.path.join(FEDICHAT_DIR, safe + ".jsonl")

def _fedichat_canonical(msg): body = {k: msg.get(k) for k in ("fed", "prev", "author", "authorName", "n", "kind", "body", "ts", "replyTo", "target")} # Build 2 keys ride the canonical form ONLY when the line # carries them — a phase-1 line (and any general-room line # today) canonicalizes byte-identically to phase 1, so # every held id from the phase-1 log still recomputes
for k in ("room", "media", "quote", "ref", "navi"): if msg.get(k): body[k] = msg.get(k) return json.dumps(body, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
def _fedichat_id(msg): return hashlib.sha256(_fedichat_canonical(msg)).hexdigest()

def _fedichat_log_path(fed_id, room_id=""): if not str(room_id or ""): return _fedichat_path(fed_id) safe = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", "_", str(fed_id or "")) sroom = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9_-]", "_", str(room_id or "")) return os.path.join(FEDICHAT_DIR, safe + "--" + sroom + ".jsonl")

def fedichat_log_read(fed_id, room_id=""): path = _fedichat_log_path(fed_id, room_id) out = [] if os.path.isfile(path): try: with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f: for ln in f: ln = ln.strip() if not ln: continue try: rec = json.loads(ln) except Exception: continue if isinstance(rec, dict) and rec.get("id"): out.append(rec) except Exception: pass return out

def _fedichat_log_write(fed_id, msgs, room_id=""): os.makedirs(FEDICHAT_DIR, exist_ok=True) path = _fedichat_log_path(fed_id, room_id) tmp = path + ".tmp" with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f: for m in msgs: f.write(json.dumps(m) + "\n") os.replace(tmp, path)
def _fedichat_log_append(fed_id, msg, room_id=""): os.makedirs(FEDICHAT_DIR, exist_ok=True) with open(_fedichat_log_path(fed_id, room_id), "a", encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write(json.dumps(msg) + "\n")

def _fedichat_prune_floor(msgs, cutoff): # The phase-1 retention shape: lines older than the # cutoff are pruned, except the newest older line, which # stays as the floor — the chain verifies forward from # it, and its own parent is honestly absent

floor = None kept = [] for m in msgs: if int(m.get("ts") or 0) >= cutoff: kept.append(m) else: floor = m if floor is not None and (not kept or kept[0].get("id") != floor.get("id")): kept = [floor] + kept return kept, len(kept) != len(msgs)

def fedichat_log_current(cfg, fed_id, room_id=""): # The log as this node's laws hold it: the operator's # retention setting first (default keep prunes nothing), # then the room's own law — a vanishing room prunes lines # older than its TTL in the same floor shape, and a # dissolved room is pruned to its floor (its newest line # stands as the anchor; the room's face says the rest)

msgs = fedichat_log_read(fed_id, room_id) changed = False days = FEDICHAT_RETENTION_DAYS[fedichat_settings(cfg)["retention"]] if days and msgs: msgs, cut = _fedichat_prune_floor( msgs, int(time.time()) - days * 86400) changed = changed or cut room = None if str(room_id or ""): _idx, fed = _fed_find(federation_settings(cfg), fed_id) if fed is not None: room = fedichat_room_find(fed, room_id) if room is not None: if room.get("dissolved"): if len(msgs) > 1: msgs = msgs[-1:] changed = True elif room.get("ttlSeconds"): msgs, cut = _fedichat_prune_floor( msgs, int(time.time()) - int(room["ttlSeconds"])) changed = changed or cut if changed: try: _fedichat_log_write(fed_id, msgs, room_id) except Exception: pass if room is not None: _idx, fed = _fed_find(federation_settings(cfg), fed_id) if fed is not None: _fedichat_media_gc(fed) return msgs

def fedichat_chain_check(msgs): # The chain as held: every message's id recomputes from its # contents, and every parent (past the first held message — # the anchor, whose parent may be a pruned floor or the # genesis) is held before it. The first break is NAMED — # a broken chain is evidence, never silently healed

known = set() for i, m in enumerate(msgs or []): if _fedichat_id(m) != str(m.get("id") or ""): return {"ok": False, "at": str(m.get("id") or "")[:12], "reason": "a message's contents no longer match its id — the log has been altered at " + str(m.get("id") or "")[:12]} prev = str(m.get("prev") or "") if i > 0 and prev and prev not in known: return {"ok": False, "at": str(m.get("id") or "")[:12], "reason": "the chain breaks at " + str(m.get("id") or "")[:12] + " — its parent is not held here"} known.add(str(m.get("id") or "")) return {"ok": True, "at": "", "reason": ""}

def fedichat_operator_name(cfg): # This node's operator name — the operator card's name, # the #256 operator class's synced single value (the # bridge's config follows the converged name). "" when # the operator has not named themselves yet. return str((cfg or {}).get("operator_name") or "").strip()

def _fedichat_op_names(msgs): # The room's presence state as a log holds it: author # node id -> the operator name from that author's LATEST # presence line. Presence lines are signed like every # line, so a name in the room is bound to its author's # key — nobody wears another member's name
out = {} for m in (msgs or []): if m.get("kind") == "presence": name = str(m.get("body") or "").strip() if name: out[str(m.get("author") or "")] = name return out

def _fedichat_op_names_fed(fed): # Operator names across the whole fedinet: presence # lines live in whichever room they were posted in, but # a name is a fedinet-level fact — resolution, completion # and display all read the merged view. out = {} for room in fedichat_rooms_load(fed): for k, v in _fedichat_op_names( fedichat_log_read(fed["id"], room["room"])).items(): out[k] = v return out

def _fedichat_ensure_presence(cfg, fed, msgs, room_id=""): # Before this node speaks (a post, or Navi's answer), its # current operator name must stand in the log: if the # name is set and differs from this node's latest # presence line, a presence line is appended — signed, # chained, converged like any line. Returns the log as # it now stands (the caller's next line chains on it)
# An unnamed operator posts no presence and presents by # node name, exactly as phase 1 did

name = fedichat_operator_name(cfg) if not name: return msgs ms = mesh_settings(cfg) own = mesh_node_id() or ms["nodeId"] if _fedichat_op_names(msgs).get(own) == name: return msgs member = _fed_member(fed, own) if member is None: return msgs msg = { "fed": fed["id"], "prev": str(msgs[-1].get("id") or "") if msgs else "", "author": own, "authorName": str(member.get("name") or ms["nodeName"] or own[:12]), "n": int(member.get("n") or 0), "kind": "presence", "body": name, "ts": int(time.time()), "replyTo": "", "target": "", } if str(room_id or ""): msg["room"] = str(room_id) msg["id"] = _fedichat_id(msg) msg["sig"] = mesh_sign(_fedichat_canonical(msg)) _fedichat_log_append(fed["id"], msg, room_id) return list(msgs) + [msg]

def _fedichat_resolve_member(fed, ref): # A -<user> reference against the roster: a roster number, # a single-word node name, or the longest node name the # reference starts with (node names carry spaces — "Member # One" completes whole)

Since v0.5.4e the OPERATOR names # the room holds (presence) resolve too, on the same # longest-prefix terms — the address book grows, it never # swaps: node names and roster numbers keep working. # Returns (member, rest) or (None, ref)

members = [m for m in _fed_roster_members(fed) if isinstance(m, dict)] op_names = _fedichat_op_names_fed(fed) low = str(ref or "").lower() named = [] for m in members: named.append((str(m.get("name") or ""), m)) op = op_names.get(str(m.get("nodeId") or "")) if op: named.append((op, m)) for name, m in sorted(named, key=lambda x: -len(x[0])): if name and low.startswith(name.lower()): tail = str(ref)[len(name):] if tail == "" or tail.startswith(" "): return m, tail.strip() first, _sep, rest = str(ref or "").partition(" ") for m in members: if str(m.get("name") or "").lower() == first.lower() \ or op_names.get(str(m.get("nodeId") or ""), "").lower() == first.lower() \ or (first.isdigit() and int(first) == int(m.get("n") or 0)): return m, rest.strip() return None, str(ref or "")

# -- The door's knock ledger (0.2.0e Build 4, #143/#154) ------------ # The Mesh door can face the open internet now (a declared # public endpoint is exactly that), so it keeps count of failed # knocks per source: failed TLS handshakes at accept time, and # requests that fail signature authentication

Five failures # inside a minute close the door to that source — connections # are dropped at accept, before any handler runs — for a # backoff that doubles per repeat closing (60s, 120s, 240s, … # capped at 900s). Every knock and every closing is logged to # the bridge's stdout in words

A successful authentication # clears the source's failure slate: a paired peer's valid # signed traffic is never throttled, and whole requests are # not chatty, so no legitimate federation pattern can reach # five failures inside a minute. State is in-memory only: a # bridge restart reopens every door, which is the honest # failure direction for a lockout.
MESH_DOOR_KNOCK_FAILS = 5 MESH_DOOR_KNOCK_WINDOW = 60 MESH_DOOR_BLOCK_BASE = 60 MESH_DOOR_BLOCK_CAP = 900 _MESH_DOOR_LOCK = threading.Lock() _MESH_DOOR = {}
def _mesh_door_log(msg): print("Navi Mesh: " + msg, flush=True)
def mesh_door_blocked(ip): now = time.time() with _MESH_DOOR_LOCK: st = _MESH_DOOR.get(ip) return bool(st and st["blockedUntil"] > now)

def mesh_door_knock(ip, kind): # One failed knock from a source: a handshake that failed # at the door, or a request its signature did not carry. # Returns "counted", or "blocked" when this knock closed # the door (or the door was already closed)

def log_message(self, *args): pass

def _send(self, code, payload): body = json.dumps(payload).encode() try: self.send_response(code) self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json") self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body))) self.end_headers() self.wfile.write(body) except Exception: pass
def _body(self): length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0) return self.rfile.read(length) if length > 0 else b""

# # A session is born on first interactive need — the operator opens # it from the composer, or Navi drives one into existence with a # [[shell]] block — and then survives messages and window reloads # (it lives here, in the bridge, not in the page)

It ends when # someone closes it, when its shell exits, after 30 minutes # without input (the sweeper says so in the thread), or when the # bridge dies — and a bridge death is never papered over: the # events stay queryable as a tombstone until the bridge restarts, # and the persisted thread record shows a session with no closing # note, which the page names as a bridge restart

# # Everything a session does is an event on the chat's record: # inputs badged by author ("operator" / "navi"), output as it # streams. A program that takes the alternate screen is held on a # real grid (below) for the desktop's terminal pane; its output # does not pollute the streamed record, and entering/leaving the # alternate screen is itself noted in the thread

import codecs import fcntl import pty import signal import termios
SHELL_IDLE_SECONDS = 1800 # 30 minutes without input
def _strip_ansi(text): if not text: return "" return _ANSI_SEQ.sub("", text).replace("\r", "")

class _TermGrid: """A minimal VT grid — enough of xterm to hold a full-screen program's frame for the desktop pane: printable text with wrap, CR/LF/BS, cursor addressing, erases, insert/delete lines and chars, scrolling, and the alternate screen. SGR and friends are parsed and ignored. It is a faithful record of the frame, not a terminal emulator competing with xterm."""
def __init__(self, cols=80, rows=24): self.cols = max(20, int(cols or 80)) self.rows = max(5, int(rows or 24)) self.main = self._blank() self.alt = None self.cx = 0 self.cy = 0 self.in_alt = False
def _blank(self): return [[" "] * self.cols for _ in range(self.rows)]
@property def grid(self): return self.alt if self.in_alt else self.main
def lines(self): return ["".join(r).rstrip() for r in self.grid]

def resize(self, cols, rows): cols = max(20, int(cols or self.cols)) rows = max(5, int(rows or self.rows)) for name in ("main", "alt"): g = getattr(self, name) if g is None: continue ng = [[" "] * cols for _ in range(rows)] for y in range(min(rows, len(g))): for x in range(min(cols, len(g[y]))): ng[y][x] = g[y][x] setattr(self, name, ng) self.cols, self.rows = cols, rows self.cx = min(self.cx, cols - 1) self.cy = min(self.cy, rows - 1)
def _scroll_up(self, n=1): g = self.grid for _ in range(n): g.pop(0) g.append([" "] * self.cols)
def _scroll_down(self, n=1): g = self.grid for _ in range(n): g.pop() g.insert(0, [" "] * self.cols)
def _newline(self): self.cx = 0 self.cy += 1 if self.cy >= self.rows: self._scroll_up(1) self.cy = self.rows - 1
def _put(self, ch): self.grid[self.cy][self.cx] = ch self.cx += 1 if self.cx >= self.cols: self._newline()

def feed(self, text): i = 0 n = len(text) while i < n: ch = text[i] if ch == "\x1b": m = re.match(r"\x1b\[([0-9;?]*)([@-~])", text[i:]) if m: self._csi(m.group(1), m.group(2)) i += m.end() continue m = re.match(r"\x1b\][^\x07\x1b]*(?:\x07|\x1b\\)", text[i:]) if m: i += m.end() continue i += 2 if i + 1 < n else 1 continue if ch == "\n": self._newline() elif ch == "\r": self.cx = 0 elif ch == "\b": self.cx = max(0, self.cx - 1) elif ch == "\t": self.cx = min(self.cols - 1, (self.cx // 8 + 1) * 8) elif ch >= " ": self._put(ch) i += 1

def _csi(self, params, final): private = params.startswith("?") nums = [p for p in params.lstrip("?").split(";") if p != ""] def num(k, default): try: v = int(nums[k]) return v if v != 0 else default except Exception: return default g = self.grid if private: modes = [int(p) for p in nums if p.isdigit()] if any(m in (1049, 1047, 47) for m in modes): if final == "h" and not self.in_alt: self.alt = self._blank() self.in_alt = True elif final == "l" and self.in_alt: self.in_alt = False self.alt = None return if final in ("H", "f"): self.cy = max(0, min(self.rows - 1, num(0, 1) - 1)) self.cx = max(0, min(self.cols - 1, num(1, 1) - 1)) elif final == "A": self.cy = max(0, self.cy - num(0, 1)) elif final == "B": self.cy = min(self.rows - 1, self.cy + num(0, 1)) elif final == "C": self.cx = min(self.cols - 1, self.cx + num(0, 1)) elif final == "D": self.cx = max(0, self.cx - num(0, 1)) elif final == "G": self.cx = max(0, min(self.cols - 1, num(0, 1) - 1)) elif final == "d": self.cy = max(0, min(self.rows - 1, num(0, 1) - 1)) elif final == "J": mode = num(0, 0) if mode == 0: for x in range(self.cx, self.cols): g[self.cy][x] = " " for y in range(self.cy + 1, self.rows): g[y] = [" "] * self.cols elif mode == 1: for x in range(0, self.cx + 1): g[self.cy][x] = " " for y in range(0, self.cy): g[y] = [" "] * self.cols else: for y in range(self.rows): g[y] = [" "] * self.cols elif final == "K": mode = num(0, 0) if mode == 0: rng = range(self.cx, self.cols) elif mode == 1: rng = range(0, self.cx + 1) else: rng = range(0, self.cols) for x in rng: g[self.cy][x] = " " elif final == "L": for _ in range(num(0, 1)): g.insert(self.cy, [" "] * self.cols) g.pop() elif final == "M": for _ in range(num(0, 1)): g.pop(self.cy) g.append([" "] * self.cols) elif final == "P": row = g[self.cy] for _ in range(num(0, 1)): if self.cx < len(row): row.pop(self.cx) row.append(" ") elif final == "@": row = g[self.cy] for _ in range(num(0, 1)): row.insert(self.cx, " ") row.pop() elif final == "S": self._scroll_up(num(0, 1)) elif final == "T": self._scroll_down(num(0, 1)) # m (SGR), r, s, u, and everything else: parsed, ignored.
def _key_display(text): # How a raw key burst reads in the thread record: printable # runs kept, control characters named

out = [] for ch in text: if ch in ("\r", "\n"): out.append("⏎") elif ch == "\x03": out.append("^C") elif ch == "\x04": out.append("^D") elif ch == "\x1a": out.append("^Z") elif ch == "\x09": out.append("⇥") elif ch < " ": out.append("^" + chr(ord(ch) + 64)) else: out.append(ch) return "".join(out)
class ShellSession: """One chat's standing terminal. See the section header."""

def __init__(self, chat_id, cols=80, rows=24): self.chat_id = str(chat_id) self.grid = _TermGrid(cols, rows) self.events = [] self.seq = 0 self.lock = threading.Lock() self.created_at = time.time() self.last_input_at = time.time() self.alive = True self.close_reason = None self._pending = "" self._pending_at = 0.0 self._tail = "" self._was_alt = False self._decoder = codecs.getincrementaldecoder("utf-8")("replace") master, slave = pty.openpty() try: fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", self.grid.rows, self.grid.cols, 0, 0)) except Exception: pass env = dict(os.environ) env["TERM"] = "xterm-256color"
def _preexec(): os.setsid() try: fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSCTTY, 0) except Exception: pass

self.proc = subprocess.Popen( ["/bin/bash", "-i"], stdin=slave, stdout=slave, stderr=slave, cwd=shell_cwd(), env=env, preexec_fn=_preexec, close_fds=True) os.close(slave) self.master = master os.set_blocking(master, False) self._emit("note", None, "shell session opened") self._reader = threading.Thread(target=self._read_loop, daemon=True) self._reader.start()

# -- events --------------------------------------------------- def _emit(self, kind, author, text): with self.lock: self.seq += 1 self.events.append({ "seq": self.seq, "kind": kind, "author": author, "text": text, "ts": int(time.time())}) if len(self.events) > 400: del self.events[:len(self.events) - 400]
def events_since(self, since): with self.lock: return [dict(e) for e in self.events if e["seq"] > since]
def output_tail(self, limit=1200): with self.lock: return self._tail[-limit:]

def wait_settled(self, quiet=0.5, cap=4.0, floor=0.9): # A newborn session's startup output — the shell's # banner, the distro's welcome mat — lands over the # first moments of its life, while an input typed at # once is emitted into the record immediately and the # banner flushes in BEHIND it: the field shape that # buried an uptime answer under thirty lines of Bazzite # MOTD (v0.4.2e, #232)

Wait until the stream has been # quiet for `quiet` seconds — no new events, nothing # waiting to flush — at most `cap`, so the banner takes # its place at the session's opening, before any driven # line. The `floor` is the session's minimum age before # quiet counts at all: a banner still on its way (a # login script that sleeps before it prints) is silent # too, and silence that young proves nothing
Returns # True when the stream settled, False on the cap (the # caller types anyway; a slow shell is still a shell)

started = time.time() deadline = started + cap last_seq = -1 quiet_since = None while time.time() < deadline: with self.lock: seq = self.seq pending = bool(self._pending) if seq == last_seq and not pending: if quiet_since is None: quiet_since = time.time() elif time.time() - quiet_since >= quiet \ and time.time() - started >= floor: return True else: last_seq = seq quiet_since = None time.sleep(0.05) return False

# -- output path ------------------------------------------------ def _on_data(self, text): if not text: return with self.lock: self.grid.feed(text) alt = self.grid.in_alt if alt != self._was_alt: self._was_alt = alt if alt: self._flush_pending(force=True) self._emit("note", None, "a program took the full screen — on the " "desktop it renders in the terminal pane") else: self._emit("note", None, "the full-screen program exited — back " "to the streamed record") if not alt: self._pending += text if not self._pending_at: self._pending_at = time.time() self._flush_pending()

def _flush_pending(self, force=False): if not self._pending: return if not force and len(self._pending) < 8192 \ and time.time() - self._pending_at < 0.15: return raw, self._pending = self._pending, "" self._pending_at = 0.0 text = _strip_ansi(raw) if text.strip(): with self.lock: self._tail = (self._tail + text)[-8000:] self._emit("out", None, text.rstrip("\n"))

def _read_loop(self): while True: try: r, _, _ = select.select([self.master], [], [], 0.2) except Exception: break if r: try: chunk = os.read(self.master, 65536) except OSError: break if not chunk: break self._on_data(self._decoder.decode(chunk)) self._flush_pending() if self.proc.poll() is not None: try: while True: chunk = os.read(self.master, 65536) if not chunk: break self._on_data(self._decoder.decode(chunk)) except Exception: pass break self._flush_pending(force=True) code = self.proc.poll() with self.lock: was = self.alive self.alive = False if was: self._emit("note", None, "the shell exited" + ("" if code is None else " (exit " + str(code) + ")") + " — the session is closed") _shell_session_died(self)

# -- input path --------------------------------------------------- def input(self, text, author, raw=False): if not self.alive: return False try: os.write(self.master, text.encode("utf-8", "replace")) except OSError: return False self.last_input_at = time.time() shown = _key_display(text) if raw else text.rstrip("\r\n") if shown or not raw: self._emit("in", author, shown) return True

def resize(self, cols, rows): with self.lock: self.grid.resize(cols, rows) rows_now, cols_now = self.grid.rows, self.grid.cols try: fcntl.ioctl(self.master, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", rows_now, cols_now, 0, 0)) except Exception: pass

def kill(self, reason): with self.lock: was = self.alive self.alive = False self.close_reason = reason if was: self._flush_pending(force=True) self._emit("note", None, "session closed (" + reason + ")") try: os.killpg(self.proc.pid, signal.SIGTERM) except Exception: pass try: self.proc.wait(timeout=2) except Exception: try: os.killpg(self.proc.pid, signal.SIGKILL) except Exception: pass try: os.close(self.master) except Exception: pass

def shell_session_state(chat_id, since=0): key = str(chat_id) sess = _shell_sessions.get(key) if sess is not None and sess.alive: with sess.lock: alt = sess.grid.in_alt screen = sess.grid.lines() if alt else None cursor = [sess.grid.cx, sess.grid.cy] seq = sess.seq return { "ok": True, "live": True, "ended": False, "chatId": key, "altScreen": alt, "screen": screen, "cursor": cursor, "seq": seq, "events": sess.events_since(since), "idleFor": int(time.time() - sess.last_input_at), } tomb = _shell_tombstones.get(key) if tomb is not None: return { "ok": True, "live": False, "ended": True, "chatId": key, "altScreen": False, "screen": None, "cursor": None, "seq": tomb.seq, "events": tomb.events_since(since), "closeReason": tomb.close_reason or "the shell exited", } return {"ok": True, "live": False, "ended": False, "chatId": key, "altScreen": False, "screen": None, "cursor": None, "seq": 0, "events": []}

def installed_commands(): # What this machine actually has installed: every executable on # PATH. This is the list command autocomplete draws from in live # mode (plus the built-in default set the dashboard always offers)

names = set() for directory in os.environ.get("PATH", "").split(os.pathsep): if not directory: continue try: entries = os.listdir(directory) except Exception: continue for name in entries: if not re.match(r"^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9+._-]*$", name): continue path = os.path.join(directory, name) if os.path.isfile(path) and os.access(path, os.X_OK): names.add(name) return sorted(names)[:800]

# # Every GitHub failure Apex surfaces is classified into one of # three named kinds — auth (the credential itself is refused), # rate (a bucket is spent; the reset time rides along), abuse # (GitHub's secondary/abuse safeguard; Retry-After rides along and # Apex stops — nothing anywhere retries on its own) — and worded # as a sentence

No surface ever shows a bare "HTTP 403" again: # that silence is what made the field 403s (#172) undiagnosable. # # And the app reads — the Updater's checks, the NUR's topic # searches and repo reads, downloads — ride the operator's own # GitHub sign-in (Build 6, #173 phase 3: one credential for the # whole product; Build 2's separate Runtime PAT is retired)

# Signed out, they go unauthenticated and share that bucket — # 60 requests/hour per network address, 10/minute for search — # with everything else on the operator's network, and their # failures name those limits out loud.

class GithubHttpError(Exception): """A GitHub HTTP failure with its evidence attached: status, GitHub's own message, and the response headers (rate-limit and Retry-After facts live there). .code mirrors HTTPError's, so older callers that read it keep working."""

def __init__(self, status, message="", headers=None, url=""): super().__init__("HTTP " + str(status) + ((": " + message) if message else "")) self.status = status self.code = status self.message = message or "" self.headers = headers self.url = url
def _gh_header(headers, name): if headers is None: return None try: v = headers.get(name) except Exception: return None return str(v) if v is not None else None

# The last rate-limit buckets GitHub actually reported, keyed by # resource ("core" / "search"). Filled in from response headers # wherever a GitHub response provides them; the Settings → GitHub # identity panel reads them back. None until a response lands. _GITHUB_RATE = {"core": None, "search": None}

def _github_note_rate(headers, url=""): try: limit = _gh_header(headers, "x-ratelimit-limit") if limit is None: return resource = (_gh_header(headers, "x-ratelimit-resource") or "").strip().lower() if resource not in ("core", "search"): resource = "search" if "/search/" in (url or "") else "core" remaining = _gh_header(headers, "x-ratelimit-remaining") reset = _gh_header(headers, "x-ratelimit-reset") _GITHUB_RATE[resource] = { "limit": int(limit), "remaining": int(remaining) if remaining is not None else None, "reset": int(reset) if reset is not None else None, "at": int(time.time()), } except Exception: pass
def github_rate_state(): return {"core": _GITHUB_RATE.get("core"), "search": _GITHUB_RATE.get("search")}
def _gh_reset_phrase(reset_epoch): if not reset_epoch: return "" try: when = time.strftime("%H:%M", time.localtime(int(reset_epoch))) except Exception: return "" return " It resets at " + when + "."

def github_classify_error(status, headers=None, message="", authed=True): """Classify one GitHub failure and word it. Returns a dict: kind ("auth" | "rate" | "abuse" | "error"), the HTTP status, GitHub's own message where it sent one, the reset time and Retry-After where the headers carry them, and `text` — the full sentence a surface shows

# --------------------- Knowledge packs (RAG) --------------------- # Her knowledge, chip-style like her chips. A pack is a GitHub # repo carrying the "navi-rag" topic; its documents are the repo's # .md/.txt/.pdf files — a PDF's text is extracted at the door # (pdf_extract_text below, stdlib only) and only the text is ever # stored or indexed

Installing downloads the documents into # rag-packs/<slug>/, builds the pack's index there at install time, # and records the install in rag-packs/installed.json with an # active flag — only active packs feed retrieval in /api/chat, and # when a pack informs an answer, its sources ride the reply's "rag" # payload field and the dashboard draws them as pills under that # message — never as words in her reply

RAG Studio forges packs # from documents on # this machine into the same folder with local/ records. A pack # also exports back out as a GitHub-ready repo ZIP (README page, # navi-rag.json manifest, documents/, and the built index.json as # the pack's reference copy — installs rebuild the index locally # from the documents and skip a root README, so the page never # pollutes retrieval)

The index # is feature-hashed term vectors (RAG_EMBED_DIM buckets, signed, # L2-normalized): small local embeddings computed with the stdlib # alone — no model to download, a chunk embeds in well under a # millisecond, and at query time only the question gets embedded, # so retrieval stays fluid on CPU
Packs and their indexes sit on # the installers' persistence keep-list beside chips/ and # voice/models/, so updates and --fresh installs keep them.

RAG_PACKS_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "rag-packs") RAG_EXPORTS_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "rag-exports") CHIPS_EXPORTS_DIR = os.path.join(ROOT, "chips-exports") RAG_INSTALLS_PATH = os.path.join(RAG_PACKS_DIR, "installed.json") RAG_EMBED_DIM = 256 RAG_MIN_SCORE = 0.18 RAG_MAX_DOCS = 40 RAG_MAX_DOC_CHARS = 200000

def _rag_embed(text): # A feature-hashed term embedding: each word hashes into one of # RAG_EMBED_DIM buckets (a second bit of the hash picks the # sign, so unrelated words sharing a bucket tend to cancel # rather than reinforce), counts accumulate, and the vector is # L2-normalized so a dot product is a cosine

vec = [0.0] * RAG_EMBED_DIM for tok in re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", (text or "").lower()): if len(tok) < 3: continue h = zlib.crc32(tok.encode("utf-8")) vec[h % RAG_EMBED_DIM] += 1.0 if (h >> 9) & 1 else -1.0 norm = math.sqrt(sum(v * v for v in vec)) if norm: vec = [v / norm for v in vec] return vec

def _pdf_parse_cmap(content): # A ToUnicode CMap -> {code length: {code: unicode text}}, # from its beginbfchar / beginbfrange sections. maps = {}

def _pdf_decode_coded(raw, cmap): # Decodes one shown string's raw bytes through a font's # ToUnicode map (longest codes first); without a map — or for # a code the map does not know in a 1-byte font — the plain # byte decoding is the fallback

def pdf_extract_text(data): # The text layer of a PDF, stdlib only: every stream is # inflated (FlateDecode; a stream that does not inflate is # used raw) and the ones carrying text operators contribute # their strings in order, decoded through each font's # ToUnicode map when it carries one — the CID-font exports # Word and writing tools produce need exactly that, their # raw codes being font-internal numbers, not characters
