def build_rag_index(documents): # The index is built once, at install/forge time, and stored # with the pack; queries never re-embed the documents. docs = [] total = 0 for d in documents: chunks = [ {"text": c, "vector": _rag_embed(c)} for c in _rag_chunks(d.get("body") or "") ] total += len(chunks) docs.append({"title": d.get("title") or "document", "chunks": chunks}) return {"documents": docs, "chunkCount": total}

pdir = os.path.join(RAG_PACKS_DIR, slug) os.makedirs(pdir, exist_ok=True) for fn in os.listdir(pdir): if fn.lower().endswith((".md", ".txt", ".pdf")) or fn == "index.json": try: os.remove(os.path.join(pdir, fn)) except Exception: pass used = set() for d in documents: flat = (d.get("title") or "document").replace("/", "-") safe = re.sub(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]+", "-", flat).strip("-.") or "document" if safe.lower().endswith(".pdf"): # A PDF document's body is its extracted text, so on # disk it lives as a .txt file under its own name — # the pack never stores the binary

safe = safe[:-4] + ".txt" elif not safe.lower().endswith((".md", ".txt")): safe += ".md" stem, dot, ext = safe.rpartition(".") cand = safe n = 2 while cand in used: cand = (stem + "-" + str(n) + "." + ext) if dot else (safe + "-" + str(n)) n += 1 used.add(cand) with open(os.path.join(pdir, cand), "w") as f: f.write(d.get("body") or "") index = build_rag_index(documents) index["name"] = name index["description"] = description # Build 3 (#101): the pack's declared icon art lives on its # index record, the pack folder's metadata home — validated # here so a bad shape never reaches a face; the face falls # back to the book

# A tombstone yields to newer work: if the surviving copy carries # a stamp LATER than the deletion, the copy wins and the tombstone # is dropped — a thread genuinely continued after its deletion # elsewhere is not a resurrection. # -- Push-on-write (v0.5.1e, #257) -------------------------------- # Occasions (the button, app start, a DHD session, Mesh # contact) cannot meet a ten-second standard by construction: # a change waits for the other seat's next occasion

So a # WRITE on this seat asks for a round of its own: the note # coalesces a burst of writes into one round; the round rides # the Mesh when a peer's road is lit and the repo otherwise; # its landing is receipted like any other round's, with the # road and the measured duration on the bar. _SYNC_ROUND = {"depth": 0, "thread": None} _SYNC_PUSH = {"lock": threading.Lock(), "timer": None, "attempts": 0, "kinds": set()} _SYNC_PUSH_COALESCE = 1.25 _SYNC_PUSH_RETRY = 3.0

# -- Sync preemption (v0.6.3e, #317) ------------------------------ # The override's missing half, named in the field: the operator # chose Send and the card answered "Held — the running round's # verdict is the one that counts." An operator's word does not # queue behind machinery

The # chosen direction then runs at once

Machine triggers (push- # on-write, occasions) never note a preemption — the hold stays # theirs. A newer choice replaces an older one wholesale: the # newest direction is the one that runs, and a direction # superseded before it could run says so on its own receipt.

class _SyncSuperseded(Exception): # Raised inside a round at a phase boundary when a newer # operator direction outranks it. _SYNC_PREEMPT = {"lock": threading.Lock(), "seq": 0, "current": None, "doneSeq": 0, "doneDir": ""}

def _sync_preempt_note(direction, trigger): # The operator's choice, recorded. def _sync_superseded_result(direction, phase, own_direction=""): # The stopped round's verdict — on its return, its durable # record, and the card that reads them back. It names who # outranked it and where it stopped; the work it landed # before the boundary stands, and says so

def dossier_find_by_key(store, key_type, value): """The dossier that already holds this key, if any — the spine's lookup (#290)

An address or a name run from any door lands on the dossier that knows it, so the civil spine accretes on one person-shaped record instead of scattering across near-duplicate dossiers.""" v = str(value or "").strip().lower() if not v: return None for d in store["dossiers"]: for k in d.get("keys") or []: if k["type"] == key_type \ and str(k["value"]).strip().lower() == v: return d return None

Two families: names the dossier's own records named (association links not yet keys — a caption's other side, an officer of record), and shelves a standing key has not been run through (a person with no courts run)

The press — the page button, or the operator's ask in chat — is the go; nothing here fires anything.""" if d is None: return [] out, seen = [], set() keys = {(k["type"], str(k["value"]).strip().lower()) for k in d.get("keys") or []} ran = {(r.get("keyType"), str(r.get("key") or "").strip().lower()) for r in store["runs"] if r.get("dossierId") == d["id"]}
def add(kt, val, via): sig = (kt, str(val).strip().lower()) if sig in seen or sig in keys or sig in ran: return seen.add(sig) out.append({"keyType": kt, "value": val, "via": via})

for ln in d.get("links") or []: if ln.get("kind") == "association" \ and str(ln.get("to") or "").startswith("person:"): add("person", str(ln["to"])[len("person:"):], ln.get("label") or "named on a record") for k in d.get("keys") or []: if k["type"] == "person": add("courts", k["value"], "the courts shelf has not been run for this person") add("archive", k["value"], "the archive shelf has not been run for this person") if k["type"] == "business": add("courts", k["value"], "the courts shelf has not been run for this entity") return out[:6]

# -- Photo: EXIF, fully local, stdlib only ----------------------- def _exif_tiff(data, base): """A minimal TIFF reader: returns a dict of named facts or {} — enough for Make/Model/DateTime/Software/Artist/ Description and the GPS pair, nothing more.""" out = {} try: endian = data[base:base + 2] bo = "<" if endian == b"II" else ">" if endian == b"MM" else None if bo is None: return out def u16(o): return struct.unpack_from(bo + "H", data, o)[0] def u32(o): return struct.unpack_from(bo + "I", data, o)[0] def rat(o): n, dnm = struct.unpack_from(bo + "II", data, o) return (n / dnm) if dnm else 0.0 typesz = {1: 1, 2: 1, 3: 2, 4: 4, 5: 8, 7: 1, 9: 4, 10: 8} def read_ifd(off, wanted, gps=False): found = {} try: n = u16(base + off) for i in range(min(n, 64)): e = base + off + 2 + i * 12 tag, typ = u16(e), u16(e + 2) cnt = u32(e + 4) if tag not in wanted: continue sz = typesz.get(typ, 1) * cnt voff = (e + 8) if sz <= 4 else base + u32(e + 8) raw = data[voff:voff + sz] if typ == 2: found[tag] = raw.split(b"\x00")[0].decode( "utf-8", "replace") elif typ == 5: found[tag] = [rat(voff + j * 8) for j in range(min(cnt, 4))] elif typ == 3: found[tag] = [u16(voff + j * 2) for j in range(min(cnt, 4))] elif typ == 4: found[tag] = [u32(voff + j * 4) for j in range(min(cnt, 4))] else: found[tag] = raw nxt = u32(base + off + 2 + n * 12) return found, nxt except Exception: return found, 0 ifd0_off = u32(base + 4) facts, _ = read_ifd(ifd0_off, { 0x010F: "Make", 0x0110: "Model", 0x0132: "DateTime", 0x013B: "Artist", 0x010E: "Description", 0x0131: "Software", 0x8298: "Copyright", 0x8825: "GPSPointer"}) names = {0x010F: "Make", 0x0110: "Model", 0x0132: "DateTime", 0x013B: "Artist", 0x010E: "Description", 0x0131: "Software", 0x8298: "Copyright"} for tag, val in facts.items(): if tag in names and isinstance(val, str) and val.strip(): out[names[tag]] = val.strip() gps_ptr = facts.get(0x8825) if isinstance(gps_ptr, list) and gps_ptr: g, _ = read_ifd(gps_ptr[0], {1: 1, 2: 2, 3: 3, 4: 4}, gps=True) try: lat = g.get(2) or [] lon = g.get(4) or [] if len(lat) == 3 and len(lon) == 3: la = lat[0] + lat[1] / 60 + lat[2] / 3600 lo = lon[0] + lon[1] / 60 + lon[2] / 3600 if g.get(1) == "S": la = -la if g.get(3) == "W": lo = -lo out["GPS"] = "%.6f, %.6f" % (la, lo) except Exception: pass except Exception: pass return out

def dossier_exif(data): """(facts, kind) — kind is 'jpeg'/'png'/'' ; facts is {} when the file carries no embedded metadata.""" if data[:2] == b"\xff\xd8": i = 2 while i + 4 <= len(data): if data[i] != 0xFF: break marker = data[i + 1] ln = struct.unpack_from(">H", data, i + 2)[0] if marker == 0xE1 and data[i + 4:i + 10] == b"Exif\x00\x00": return _exif_tiff(data, i + 10), "jpeg" if marker in (0xDA, 0xD9) or ln < 2: break i += 2 + ln return {}, "jpeg" if data[:8] == b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n": facts, i = {}, 8 while i + 12 <= len(data): ln = struct.unpack_from(">I", data, i)[0] ctype = data[i + 4:i + 8] chunk = data[i + 8:i + 8 + ln] if ctype == b"eXIf": facts.update(_exif_tiff(chunk, 0)) elif ctype == b"tEXt": k, _, v = chunk.partition(b"\x00") facts[k.decode("utf-8", "replace")] = \ v.decode("utf-8", "replace") elif ctype == b"iTXt": parts = chunk.split(b"\x00", 5) if len(parts) == 6: facts[parts[0].decode("utf-8", "replace")] = \ parts[5].decode("utf-8", "replace") if ctype == b"IEND": break i += 12 + ln return facts, "png" return {}, ""

def seraph_hex_ip(hexs): try: raw = bytes.fromhex(hexs) except Exception: return "" if len(raw) == 4: return ".".join(str(b) for b in raw[::-1]) if len(raw) == 16: # /proc writes IPv6 as four little-endian 32-bit words. words = [raw[i:i + 4][::-1] for i in range(0, 16, 4)] raw = b"".join(words) import ipaddress return str(ipaddress.IPv6Address(raw)) return ""

def seraph_parse_conns(text, proto="tcp"): """/proc/net/{tcp,tcp6,udp,udp6} -> connection rows.""" out = [] for line in (text or "").splitlines()[1:]: parts = line.split() if len(parts) < 4: continue try: lip, lport = parts[1].rsplit(":", 1) rip, rport = parts[2].rsplit(":", 1) out.append({ "proto": proto, "localIp": seraph_hex_ip(lip), "localPort": int(lport, 16), "remoteIp": seraph_hex_ip(rip), "remotePort": int(rport, 16), "state": parts[3], }) except Exception: continue return out

SERAPH_MONTHS = {m: i + 1 for i, m in enumerate( ["Jan", "Feb", "Mar", "Apr", "May", "Jun", "Jul", "Aug", "Sep", "Oct", "Nov", "Dec"])} SERAPH_AUTH_RE = re.compile( r"^(\w{3})\s+(\d+)\s+(\d{2}):(\d{2}):(\d{2})\s+\S+\s+sshd\[\d+\]:\s+" r"(Failed|Accepted) password for (?:invalid user )?(\S+) from " r"(\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+)")

def seraph_parse_auth(lines, now=None): """sshd syslog lines -> [{ts, kind, user, src}].""" now = now or seraph_now() out = [] lt = time.localtime(now) for line in lines or []: m = SERAPH_AUTH_RE.match(line or "") if not m: continue mon = SERAPH_MONTHS.get(m.group(1)) if mon is None: continue year = lt.tm_year - (1 if mon > lt.tm_mon else 0) try: ts = int(time.mktime((year, mon, int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3)), int(m.group(4)), int(m.group(5)), 0, 0, -1))) except Exception: continue out.append({"ts": ts, "kind": "fail" if m.group(6) == "Failed" else "success", "user": m.group(7), "src": m.group(8)}) return out

def seraph_parse_leases(text): """dnsmasq-style leases -> [{ip, mac, name}] (best effort).""" out = [] for line in (text or "").splitlines(): parts = line.split() if len(parts) >= 4 and re.match(r"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+\.\d+$", parts[2]): out.append({"ip": parts[2], "mac": parts[1].lower(), "device": "", "name": parts[3]}) return out
def seraph_read_file(path): try: with open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace") as f: return f.read() except Exception: return ""

def seraph_collect(readers=None): """One collection pass -> a snapshot. `readers` may inject fixture text per source ({"arp":..., "tcp":..., "auth":..., "leases":...}); absent a reader, the live file is read. What a source cannot give is named in the snapshot's gaps — the vantage statement is part of the data, not a footnote.""" readers = readers or {}
def src(key, path): if key in readers: v = readers[key] return (v or ""), v is not None if not os.path.exists(path): return "", False return seraph_read_file(path), True

gaps = [] arp_text, ok = src("arp", "/proc/net/arp") if not ok: gaps.append("no ARP table readable — passive inventory is blind") assets = seraph_parse_arp(arp_text) leases_text, lok = src("leases", "/var/lib/misc/dnsmasq.leases") if lok: by_mac = {a["mac"]: a for a in assets} for lease in seraph_parse_leases(leases_text): if lease["mac"] in by_mac: if lease["name"] and lease["name"] != "*": by_mac[lease["mac"]]["name"] = lease["name"] else: assets.append(lease) conns = [] for key, proto in (("tcp", "tcp"), ("tcp6", "tcp6"), ("udp", "udp"), ("udp6", "udp6")): text, _ok = src(key, "/proc/net/" + key) conns.extend(seraph_parse_conns(text, proto)) if not conns: gaps.append("no connection table readable — flow picture is blind") auth_text, aok = src("auth", "/var/log/auth.log") if not aok: auth_text, aok = src("auth", "/var/log/secure") auth = seraph_parse_auth(auth_text.splitlines()[-2000:]) if aok else [] if not aok: gaps.append("no auth log readable — sign-in picture is blind") listeners = sorted({(c["localIp"], c["localPort"], c["proto"]) for c in conns if c["state"] == "0A"}) remotes = {} for c in conns: if c["state"] == "01" and c["remoteIp"] not in ("", "0.0.0.0", "::"): key = (c["remoteIp"], c["remotePort"]) remotes[key] = remotes.get(key, 0) + 1 return { "ts": seraph_now(), "assets": assets, "conns": conns, "listeners": [{"ip": ip, "port": p, "proto": pr} for ip, p, pr in listeners], "remotes": [{"ip": ip, "port": p, "count": n} for (ip, p), n in sorted(remotes.items())], "auth": auth, "gaps": gaps, }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- # Detection. Pure over (state, snapshot, settings): the same # inputs always give the same detections, which is what makes # the floor benchable and its alerts trustworthy.
def seraph_fired(state, key, now): last = state["lastFired"].get(key, 0) if now - last < SERAPH_DEDUPE_WINDOW: return True state["lastFired"][key] = now return False

def seraph_det(sid, kind, key, title, detail): return {"id": seraph_new_id("det"), "sensorId": sid, "kind": kind, "key": key, "title": title, "detail": detail, "ts": seraph_now(), "state": "open", "caseSlug": ""}

def seraph_in_sleep(ts, sleep_start, sleep_end): lt = time.localtime(ts) minutes = lt.tm_hour * 60 + lt.tm_min try: sh, sm = (int(x) for x in sleep_start.split(":")) eh, em = (int(x) for x in sleep_end.split(":")) except Exception: return False start, end = sh * 60 + sm, eh * 60 + em if start <= end: return start <= minutes < end return minutes >= start or minutes < end

def seraph_detect(state, snapshot, settings, watchlist): """Run the v1 detection set over one snapshot. Mutates state (inventory, listeners, samples, lastFired) — the caller saves. Returns the new detections.""" sid = settings.get("sensorId") or "" now = snapshot["ts"] out = [] terms = [str(t or "").strip().lower() for t in (watchlist or [])] terms = [t for t in terms if t]
# Watchlist matching — done HERE, on the sensor. The list is # an input to this function and is never written into any # snapshot, envelope or detection: matches travel, it doesn't

seen_values = set() for a in snapshot["assets"]: seen_values.add(a["ip"].lower()) if a.get("name"): seen_values.add(a["name"].lower()) for r in snapshot["remotes"]: seen_values.add(r["ip"].lower()) for term in terms: if term in seen_values and not seraph_fired(state, "watch:" + term, now): out.append(seraph_det(sid, "watchlist", term, "Watchlist match: " + term, "A watched value (" + term + ") is present " "on this segment or in its current traffic."))
# New face on the network

inventory = state["inventory"] for a in snapshot["assets"]: if a["mac"] not in inventory: inventory[a["mac"]] = {"ip": a["ip"], "name": a.get("name", ""), "firstSeen": now, "lastSeen": now} if not seraph_fired(state, "face:" + a["mac"], now): out.append(seraph_det( sid, "new-face", a["mac"], "New face on the network: " + (a.get("name") or a["ip"]), (a.get("name") or "An unnamed host") + " (" + a["ip"] + ", " + a["mac"] + ") is on the segment and was " "never in this sensor's inventory.")) else: inventory[a["mac"]]["lastSeen"] = now inventory[a["mac"]]["ip"] = a["ip"]
# Samples for beacon math: established outbound endpoints

for r in snapshot["remotes"]: state["samples"].append({"ts": now, "ip": r["ip"], "port": r["port"]}) state["samples"] = state["samples"][-SERAPH_SAMPLES_CAP:] by_endpoint = {} for s in state["samples"]: by_endpoint.setdefault((s["ip"], s["port"]), []).append(s["ts"]) for (ip, port), stamps in by_endpoint.items(): if len(stamps) < SERAPH_BEACON_MIN_SAMPLES: continue stamps = sorted(stamps) if stamps[-1] - stamps[0] < SERAPH_BEACON_MIN_SPAN: continue gaps = [b - a for a, b in zip(stamps, stamps[1:]) if b - a > 0] if len(gaps) < SERAPH_BEACON_MIN_SAMPLES - 1: continue mean = sum(gaps) / len(gaps) if mean <= 0: continue var = sum((g - mean) ** 2 for g in gaps) / len(gaps) cv = (var ** 0.5) / mean key = "beacon:" + ip + ":" + str(port) if cv < SERAPH_BEACON_CV_MAX and not seraph_fired(state, key, now): out.append(seraph_det( sid, "beacon", key, "Beaconing: " + ip + ":" + str(port), "Calls to " + ip + ":" + str(port) + " land on a " "metronome — about every " + str(int(mean)) + "s, " + str(len(stamps)) + " times in the window
Regular " "intervals are how implants phone home."))
# Impossible hours: a successful sign-in inside the sleep window

for ev in snapshot["auth"]: if ev["kind"] == "success" and seraph_in_sleep( ev["ts"], settings.get("sleepStart", "01:00"), settings.get("sleepEnd", "05:00")): key = "hours:" + ev["src"] + ":" + ev["user"] if not seraph_fired(state, key, now): out.append(seraph_det( sid, "impossible-hours", key, "Sign-in at an impossible hour: " + ev["user"], ev["user"] + " signed in from " + ev["src"] + " at " + time.strftime("%H:%M", time.localtime(ev["ts"])) + " — inside this network's sleep window."))
# Auth burst: one source, many failures, short window

fails = {} for ev in snapshot["auth"]: if ev["kind"] == "fail": fails.setdefault(ev["src"], []).append(ev["ts"]) for src_ip, stamps in fails.items(): stamps = sorted(stamps) hot = any(stamps[i + SERAPH_AUTH_BURST_MIN - 1] - stamps[i] <= SERAPH_AUTH_WINDOW for i in range(len(stamps) - SERAPH_AUTH_BURST_MIN + 1)) \ if len(stamps) >= SERAPH_AUTH_BURST_MIN else False key = "burst:" + src_ip if hot and not seraph_fired(state, key, now): out.append(seraph_det( sid, "auth-burst", key, "Failed sign-in burst from " + src_ip, str(len(stamps)) + " failed sign-ins from " + src_ip + " inside " + str(SERAPH_AUTH_WINDOW // 60) + " minutes — " "someone is trying doors."))
# Scan pattern: one source knocking on many ports (SYN_RECV)

knocks = {} for c in snapshot["conns"]: if c["state"] == "03": knocks.setdefault(c["remoteIp"], set()).add(c["localPort"]) for src_ip, ports in knocks.items(): key = "scan:" + src_ip if len(ports) >= SERAPH_SCAN_PORTS_MIN and not seraph_fired(state, key, now): out.append(seraph_det( sid, "scan", key, "Scan pattern from " + src_ip, src_ip + " has half-open knocks on " + str(len(ports)) + " distinct ports — someone is mapping this segment " "from the receiving end."))
# New listening service on a known host

current = {(l["ip"], l["port"], l["proto"]) for l in snapshot["listeners"]} known = {(l["ip"], l["port"], l["proto"]) for l in state["listeners"]} for ip, port, proto in sorted(current - known): key = "listen:" + ip + ":" + str(port) + ":" + proto if not seraph_fired(state, key, now): out.append(seraph_det( sid, "new-listener", key, "New listening service: " + str(port) + "/" + proto, ip + " is newly listening on " + str(port) + "/" + proto + " — a surface this sensor has not seen before.")) state["listeners"] = [{"ip": ip, "port": p, "proto": pr} for ip, p, pr in sorted(current)] state["lastSnapshot"] = { "ts": now, "assets": len(snapshot["assets"]), "conns": len(snapshot["conns"]), "listeners": len(snapshot["listeners"]), "remotes": snapshot["remotes"][:20], "gaps": snapshot["gaps"], "assetList": snapshot["assets"][:200], "listenerList": snapshot["listeners"], } return out

SERAPH_VOICE = { "watchlist": "A name on the watchlist just surfaced on {name}'s " "network — {detail}", "new-face": "New face on {name}'s network — {detail}", "beacon": "Something on {name}'s network is keeping time — {detail}", "impossible-hours": "A sign-in at an hour when {name}'s network " "should be asleep — {detail}", "auth-burst": "Someone is rattling doors on {name}'s network — " "{detail}", "scan": "Someone is mapping {name}'s network from the inside — " "{detail}", "new-listener": "A new door opened on {name}'s network — {detail}", }

def seraph_detection_voice(det, sensor_name): """The alert in Navi's voice (#319's discipline: she sends the alerts, not the system). One line, her flare, the fact.""" template = SERAPH_VOICE.get(det.get("kind"), "{detail}") return template.format(name=sensor_name or "the sensor", detail=det.get("detail") or det.get("title") or "")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- # Reporting. An envelope is one sensor's picture, whole: the # snapshot summary and the detections it raised. The sensor # spools it when the road home is dark; the console files it # under that sensor and nothing else.

def seraph_make_envelope(sensor_rec, snapshot, detections): return { "v": 1, "sensorId": sensor_rec["id"], "nodeId": sensor_rec.get("nodeId", ""), "name": sensor_rec.get("name", ""), "ts": snapshot["ts"], "snapshot": { "assets": snapshot["assets"], "remotes": snapshot["remotes"], "listeners": snapshot["listeners"], "gaps": snapshot["gaps"], "connCount": len(snapshot["conns"]), }, "detections": detections, }
def seraph_envelope_digest(env): blob = json.dumps(env, sort_keys=True).encode() return hashlib.sha256(blob).hexdigest()

def seraph_spool_write(root, env): name = str(env["ts"]) + "-" + seraph_envelope_digest(env)[:12] + ".json" path = os.path.join(root, "seraph", "spool", name) seraph_atomic_write(path, json.dumps(env, indent=1, sort_keys=True)) return name
def seraph_spool_list(root): path = os.path.join(root, "seraph", "spool") try: return sorted(os.listdir(path)) except Exception: return []
def seraph_spool_read(root, name): try: with open(os.path.join(root, "seraph", "spool", name), encoding="utf-8") as f: return json.load(f) except Exception: return None
def seraph_spool_drop(root, name): try: os.remove(os.path.join(root, "seraph", "spool", name)) except Exception: pass
def seraph_intake(root, env, sender_node): """File a report envelope under its sensor. Returns (ok, note)

Refusals are by name: unknown sensor, revoked sensor, a node claiming a sensor that is not its own.""" if not isinstance(env, dict) or env.get("v") != 1: return False, "bad-envelope" store = seraph_store_load(root) rec = store["sensors"].get(str(env.get("sensorId") or "")) if rec is None: return False, "unknown-sensor" if rec["state"] == "revoked": return False, "sensor-revoked" if rec.get("nodeId") and rec["nodeId"] != sender_node: return False, "sensor-node-mismatch" state = seraph_state_load(root, rec["id"]) snap = env.get("snapshot") or {} state["lastSnapshot"] = { "ts": env.get("ts") or seraph_now(), "assets": len(snap.get("assets") or []), "conns": snap.get("connCount") or 0, "listeners": len(snap.get("listeners") or []), "remotes": (snap.get("remotes") or [])[:20], "gaps": snap.get("gaps") or [], "assetList": (snap.get("assets") or [])[:200], "listenerList": snap.get("listeners") or [], } seraph_state_save(root, rec["id"], state) known = {d["id"] for d in store["detections"]} added = 0 for det in env.get("detections") or []: if isinstance(det, dict) and det.get("id") not in known: det["sensorId"] = rec["id"] det.setdefault("state", "open") det.setdefault("caseSlug", "") store["detections"].append(det) added += 1 store["detections"] = store["detections"][-SERAPH_DETECTIONS_CAP:] rec["lastSeen"] = seraph_now() seraph_store_save(root, store) return True, "filed:" + str(added)
def seraph_prune(root, retention_days, now=None): """Age out what the operator's retention says: samples past the window, and dismissed detections past the window

Open and filed detections never age out silently.""" now = now or seraph_now() horizon = now - max(1, int(retention_days)) * 86400 store = seraph_store_load(root) kept = [d for d in store["detections"] if d.get("state") == "open" or d.get("ts", now) >= horizon] changed = len(kept) != len(store["detections"]) store["detections"] = kept if changed: seraph_store_save(root, store) for sid in store["sensors"]: state = seraph_state_load(root, sid) samples = [s for s in state["samples"] if s["ts"] >= horizon] if len(samples) != len(state["samples"]): state["samples"] = samples seraph_state_save(root, sid, state)

def seraph_public_state(root, settings): """The console's picture, shaped for the page: registry, per-sensor last picture, open detections first.""" store = seraph_store_load(root) sensors = [] for rec in sorted(store["sensors"].values(), key=lambda r: r.get("added", 0)): state = seraph_state_load(root, rec["id"]) entry = dict(rec) entry["lastSnapshot"] = state.get("lastSnapshot") entry["openDetections"] = sum( 1 for d in store["detections"] if d["sensorId"] == rec["id"] and d["state"] == "open") sensors.append(entry) detections = sorted(store["detections"], key=lambda d: -d.get("ts", 0)) return {"ok": True, "settings": settings, "sensors": sensors, "detections": detections[:200], "watchlist": store.get("watchlist") or []}

def seraph_settings(cfg): # This seat's Seraph posture, from the config's "seraph" # slice. Role defaults to console: the suite is present and # manageable on every seat, and a seat starts watching its # own segment only when the operator says so. Retention # defaults to 30 days on-box; the sleep window is the # network's own quiet hours, operator-set
raw = {} try: s = (cfg or {}).get("seraph") if isinstance(s, dict): raw = s except Exception: raw = {}
def _int(key, default, lo, hi): try: v = int(raw.get(key)) except Exception: return default return max(lo, min(hi, v))

role = str(raw.get("role") or "console") if role not in ("console", "sensor", "both"): role = "console" return { "role": role, "retentionDays": _int("retentionDays", 30, 1, 365), "cycleSeconds": _int("cycleSeconds", 300, 60, 3600), "sleepStart": str(raw.get("sleepStart") or "01:00")[:5], "sleepEnd": str(raw.get("sleepEnd") or "05:00")[:5], "consoleNode": str(raw.get("consoleNode") or "").strip(), }
def _seraph_settings_save(cfg, patch): cur = seraph_settings(cfg) cur.update(patch) cfg["seraph"] = cur save_config(cfg) return cur

def seraph_watchlist_terms(): # The watchlist Seraph matches against: the Wire's declared # list (intel settings) plus any Seraph-local additions. The # merged list is used on THIS machine only — never written # into a snapshot, an envelope or a detection (#314)

terms = [] try: st = INTEL.settings() if isinstance(st, dict): terms.extend(st.get("watchlist") or []) except Exception: pass try: terms.extend(seraph_store_load(SERAPH_ROOT).get("watchlist") or []) except Exception: pass out, seen = [], set() for t in terms: t = str(t or "").strip() if t and t.lower() not in seen: seen.add(t.lower()) out.append(t) return out

def _seraph_self_sensor(cfg): # The seat's own sensor record, minted on first need: kind # "self", bound to this node's Mesh identity, named for the # machine. A shipped sensor's record (PIA first) is kind # "remote", minted at the Row — same registry, same shape

store = seraph_store_load(SERAPH_ROOT) for rec in store["sensors"].values(): if rec.get("kind") == "self": return rec import socket as _socket try: host = _socket.gethostname() or "This seat" except Exception: host = "This seat" return seraph_register_sensor( SERAPH_ROOT, host + " (this seat)", kind="self", address="this machine", ssh_user="", node_id=mesh_node_id() or "", vantage="the segment this seat is plugged into")
def _seraph_send(env, console_node): # One envelope home over the Mesh door. True only on the # console's own filed answer — anything else (no peer, dark # road, refusal) is a spool, never a shrug

cfg = load_config() ms = mesh_settings(cfg) peer = None for p in ms["borrow"]["peers"]: if p["nodeId"] == console_node: peer = p if peer is None: return False rid = env["sensorId"] + "-" + str(env["ts"]) body = json.dumps({"requestId": rid, "report": env}).encode() try: code, raw = _mesh_request(peer, "POST", "/mesh/seraph-report", body, rid, 30) payload = json.loads(raw.decode() or "{}") except Exception: return False return code == 200 and payload.get("ok") is True

def _seraph_drain_spool(settings): node = settings.get("consoleNode") or "" if not node: return for name in seraph_spool_list(SERAPH_ROOT): env = seraph_spool_read(SERAPH_ROOT, name) if env is not None and _seraph_send(env, node): seraph_spool_drop(SERAPH_ROOT, name)
def seraph_cycle(reason="cadence"): # One watch pass on this seat: collect, detect, file the # detections, report home (or spool), prune to retention

cfg = load_config() settings = seraph_settings(cfg) if settings["role"] not in ("sensor", "both"): return {"ok": True, "skipped": "this seat is not a sensor"} with _seraph_lock: rec = _seraph_self_sensor(cfg) snap = seraph_collect() state = seraph_state_load(SERAPH_ROOT, rec["id"]) dets = seraph_detect(state, snap, { "sensorId": rec["id"], "sleepStart": settings["sleepStart"], "sleepEnd": settings["sleepEnd"], }, seraph_watchlist_terms()) seraph_state_save(SERAPH_ROOT, rec["id"], state) store = seraph_store_load(SERAPH_ROOT) known = {d["id"] for d in store["detections"]} for d in dets: if d["id"] not in known: store["detections"].append(d) store["detections"] = store["detections"][-SERAPH_DETECTIONS_CAP:] seraph_store_save(SERAPH_ROOT, store) seraph_touch_sensor(SERAPH_ROOT, rec["id"]) env = seraph_make_envelope(rec, snap, dets) node = settings.get("consoleNode") or "" sent = False if node and node != (mesh_node_id() or ""): sent = _seraph_send(env, node) if not sent: seraph_spool_write(SERAPH_ROOT, env) else: _seraph_drain_spool(settings) seraph_prune(SERAPH_ROOT, settings["retentionDays"]) return {"ok": True, "sensor": rec["id"], "detections": len(dets), "reported": sent, "gaps": snap["gaps"]}

def seraph_start(): # The watch loop, started in __main__ beside the pulse's: # a first pass shortly after boot, then on the seat's own # cycle. A console-only seat's loop simply idles — the role # is re-read every pass, so a role flip needs no restart

def loop(): time.sleep(90) while True: try: seraph_cycle(reason="cadence") except Exception: pass try: secs = seraph_settings(load_config())["cycleSeconds"] except Exception: secs = 300 time.sleep(secs) threading.Thread(target=loop, daemon=True).start()

def mesh_handle_seraph_report(handler, body): # POST /mesh/seraph-report — a sensor reporting home. The # door is pairing-authenticated like the borrow door; the # registry is the second lock: the envelope's sensor must be # registered here, active, and bound to the authenticated # node. A client sensor's picture files under its own record # and nothing else — admission is never transitive sight

try: data = json.loads((body or b"").decode("utf-8", "replace")) except Exception: return 400, {"ok": False, "reason": "bad-request"} if not isinstance(data, dict): return 400, {"ok": False, "reason": "bad-request"} cfg = load_config() ms = mesh_settings(cfg) if not ms["enabled"]: return 200, {"ok": False, "reason": "mesh-off"} peer = mesh_authenticate(handler, body, str(data.get("requestId") or "")) if peer is None: return 401, {"ok": False, "reason": "unauthorized"} ok, note = seraph_intake(SERAPH_ROOT, data.get("report"), peer["nodeId"]) if not ok: return 200, {"ok": False, "reason": note} return 200, {"ok": True, "note": note}

def _notif_wanted_seraph(cfg): # Producer: Seraph's open detections — ONE record per # detection, in Navi's voice (#319: she sends the alerts). # The record retires when the detection leaves "open" # (filed into a case, or dismissed by the operator)

try: store = seraph_store_load(SERAPH_ROOT) except Exception: return [] names = {sid: rec.get("name") or "a sensor" for sid, rec in store["sensors"].items()} items = [] for d in store["detections"]: if d.get("state") != "open": continue items.append({ "id": d["id"], "kind": "seraph", "title": d.get("title") or "Seraph detection", "body": seraph_detection_voice( d, names.get(d.get("sensorId"), "a sensor"))[:600], "target": {"view": "Seraph", "sensor": d.get("sensorId")}, "count": 1, }) return items
def seraph_payload(): cfg = load_config() return seraph_public_state(SERAPH_ROOT, seraph_settings(cfg))
def seraph_act(action, data): # The DHD acts behind /api/seraph/act — every one an # operator act from the console's own door

Everything here # is the node's own work: the VAPID keypair is minted once by # this bridge and held in config/push.json (per-node, never # synced); payloads are encrypted end-to-end for the # subscription (RFC 8291) and signed (RFC 8292) with in-tree # cryptography — P-256, ECDSA, ECDH, HKDF, AES-128-GCM, # implemented below on the standard library alone and proved # against the RFCs' published test vectors in the build's # push1 bench (the RFC 8291 section 5 worked example # reproduces byte for byte)

The only parties a delivery ever # touches are the push services the platform itself runs — # the transport the Web Push standard is built on; there is # no relay, no account, and no third-party service of ours

# Parity is the law (Alex, 2026-11-17): whatever earns a # tray record earns the phone copy, the payload is the tray # record's own summary, the notification's tag is the tray # record's id, an ack on any seat clears the phone copy, and # the TTL is four hours. def _b64u_dec(text): if isinstance(text, str): text = text.encode("ascii") return base64.urlsafe_b64decode(text + b"=" * (-len(text) % 4))
def _ec_on_curve(pt): if pt is None: return False x, y = pt if not (0 <= x < _P256_P and 0 <= y < _P256_P): return False return (y * y - (x * x * x - 3 * x + _P256_B)) % _P256_P == 0

def _ec_add(p1, p2): if p1 is None: return p2 if p2 is None: return p1 x1, y1 = p1 x2, y2 = p2 if x1 == x2 and (y1 + y2) % _P256_P == 0: return None if p1 == p2: m = (3 * x1 * x1 - 3) * pow(2 * y1, -1, _P256_P) % _P256_P else: m = (y2 - y1) * pow(x2 - x1, -1, _P256_P) % _P256_P x3 = (m * m - x1 - x2) % _P256_P y3 = (m * (x1 - x3) - y1) % _P256_P return (x3, y3)

def _ec_mul(k, pt): # Scalar multiplication, double-and-add. k is reduced mod n; # the point at infinity is None. if pt is None or k % _P256_N == 0: return None k %= _P256_N out = None add = pt while k: if k & 1: out = _ec_add(out, add) add = _ec_add(add, add) k >>= 1 return out

ua_pub_raw = _b64u_dec(ua_pub_b64) auth_secret = _b64u_dec(auth_b64) if len(auth_secret) < 16 or _ec_pub_parse(ua_pub_raw) is None: return None if as_priv is None: as_priv, as_pt = _ec_keypair() else: as_pt = _ec_mul(as_priv, _P256_G) as_pub_raw = _ec_pub_bytes(as_pt) if salt is None: salt = secrets.token_bytes(16) keys = _webpush_keys_sender(auth_secret, ua_pub_raw, as_priv, as_pub_raw, salt) if keys is None: return None cek, nonce = keys[0], keys[1] rs = 4096 if len(plaintext) + 1 + 16 > rs: return None # one record only (RFC 8291 section 4) record = plaintext + b"\x02" body_ct = _aes128gcm_encrypt(cek, nonce, record) header = salt + rs.to_bytes(4, "big") + bytes([len(as_pub_raw)]) + as_pub_raw return header + body_ct

def _webpush_decrypt_with(keys, ct, rs): cek, base_nonce = keys[0], keys[1] out = b"" seq = 0 pos = 0 while pos < len(ct): chunk = ct[pos:pos + rs] pos += len(chunk) nonce = bytes(a ^ b for a, b in zip(base_nonce, seq.to_bytes(12, "big"))) rec = _aes128gcm_decrypt(cek, nonce, chunk) if rec is None: return None if not rec or rec[-1] not in (1, 2): return None out += rec[:-1].rstrip(b"\x00") seq += 1 return out

How Apex fits together, and how she starts.

" + "

The shape of her — dashboard, bridge, model

" + "

Apex is three pieces on your own machine:

    " + "
  • The dashboard is this page, served by the bridge at http://localhost:" + BRIDGE_PORT + ".
    • " + "
  • The bridge (bridge.py, in the install folder) does the real work: it serves the dashboard, runs shell commands, manages chips and workflows, holds sudo mode's on/off state (never a password), runs the chats' shell sessions, and carries your words to the model.
    • " + "
  • The model server is navi.llamafile, running ./navi.llamafile --server --v2 plus the flags from her hardware profile on port 8080 — at install, the installer profiled this machine (CPU, RAM, GPU) and chose the context size, threads, batch size, and GPU layers to fit it, so her settings come from your hardware, not the developer's; Settings shows what was detected and what was chosen, and the full log is hardware-profile.log; the model answers to the id navi, which the bridge reads from the server itself (/v1/models) rather than guessing.
" + "

Nothing leaves the machine on its own — the only network calls the bridge makes are to GitHub: when you open the chip or pack catalogs, check something for updates, or, once you have signed in and set it up, run a backup

The GitHub — issues & backups page in this wiki covers that whole side of her.

" + "

Two small details ride the frame: under the APEX wordmark sits her tagline — “Powered by Navi”, one static line; and at the top of the status column, her presence line starts at “Navi is here.” and cycles every few minutes through what she's up to — listening to the network breathe, arguing with a CAPTCHA, haunting Rockport's west end.

" + "

Starting her up

" + "

On Linux she lives in ~/.local/share/navi-apex — your own data home, where no corner of her tree needs root to exist
Launch her from the application menu or ./start.sh

Builds before the homecoming (Build 11) lived in /opt/navi-apex: the first Build 11 install migrates such a tree to the new home — every piece of state carried, the Mesh identity byte-for-byte — and parks the old tree in place with a marker (MIGRATED.txt) naming the new home and the one command that removes it when you are ready

Every launch is check-first: the launcher probes the model server, and if navi.llamafile is already running — from boot, an earlier launch, or started by hand — it leaves it alone and just runs the app; only when nothing answers does it start the server itself, with ./navi.llamafile --server --v2 and the hardware-profile flags from config/navi.config.json

The launcher starts the bridge, verifies the thing answering on port " + BRIDGE_PORT + " is really this build — naming whatever else it finds by its page title — and only then opens the dashboard. During install you chose when the model server starts: on app launch (the bridge starts navi.llamafile when you press Connect) or at system boot

Server output lands in navi.llamafile.log beside the app.

Chat and CLI access

" + "

Chat is CLI-first

Type a system command — anything whose first word is a command this machine has — and it runs immediately, no model call, no waiting on Navi to orchestrate it: the raw terminal output lands in the thread as a terminal block and becomes context she reasons over, so you can list a folder and then ask her about a file the listing showed
Everything else goes to Navi as conversation, including plain-language requests like “show me the contents of /home/name/”, where she runs the command and answers with the actual output attached

Under the composer sit two mode toggles — CLI and Navi: press one once and it latches, so every line you send goes that way until you press the other; the pill beside them shows which way the current line will go, and clicking the pill flips the latch

Since Build 4 the CLI latch is CLI Mode itself: latching CLI opens (or resumes) this chat's standing shell session and your lines type into it; latching Navi brings the conversation back while the session stays alive behind the toggle. A leading $ flips to a command, a leading > flips back to Navi — and either one re-latches the mode to match

Chips are untouched by the routing: they are her own purpose-built tools, run the same ways as ever.

" + "

Sending, and attaching files. There is no Send button — Enter sends, in every mode; beside the CLI | Navi toggle under the bar, plain words say so: Press enter to send. The whole composer — her chips on their slim shelf, the bar, the toggle row — sits in one dock at the foot of the chat, and the bar dresses for the latched mode: latched to CLI it takes the terminal green and command wording (Run a command — try: ls); latched to Navi it keeps her cyan
On a phone the dock's Call button is the phone glyph alone, so the bar keeps its room. The paperclip button beside the bar attaches a picture or a text file to this chat

The attachment stays in the thread where you uploaded it: a text file's contents ride with your next message as context she can reason over, and a picture is stored and referenced by name — her local model is text-only, so she does not see pictures, and nothing in the app claims she does

Every upload is also listed under the status column's Chats tab, in its Uploaded files, where you can find it later and delete it.

" + "

The composer works like a good shell: the line is colored as you type — the command word by whether the system knows it, flags, quoted strings, and paths each in their own color, the zsh-syntax-highlighting read — a dim ghost of the most recent matching command from this chat completes the line (Tab or → accepts it, in the zsh-autosuggestions way), and the command word autocompletes from what the system has installed, the same set that decides the CLI route

The terminal blocks in the thread keep the same coloring, so the history reads like a real shell session. Her replies render as markdown: code arrives as code blocks, not literal backticks. When navi.llamafile is disconnected, chat drops to a plain command line until you reconnect from the status column; chips still run in that mode

Above every view sits her presence bar — her picture (her own portrait, the lamp-post key art that ships with the app), her name, her dot, and what she is doing: here (the same living line the status column carries), in a call with you, or away when her model is stopped

(Since v0.4.1e the bar carries no typing indicator — while she thinks, the living line simply stands.) The bar is part of the frame, not of any one page: it stays over Chat, Settings, Docs — everywhere — and at its top right sits the status column's pane button, wearing the panel glyph

Every message in the thread wears its author's face in the gutter, their name, and the time it was sent — hers, yours (the name from your profile), and the call transcript in Settings → Voice reads the same way, spoken marker kept. The status column's doors are the frame's own now: the pane button at the presence bar's top right — on every page, at every width — and the panel button in the phone's top bar
Those are the only two doors; every one drives the one column state and raises the rail in place wherever you are; the phone's top bar itself is pinned, so the doors are there at any scroll depth

Conversations are saved as known chats — switch from the status column's Chats tab (the status pane's second tab, beside Status), without leaving this page.

" + "

Her window. Apex opens in her own standalone window — the Tauri shell — and closing the window quits the app. There is no tray icon and no login autostart: she runs when you launch her from the application menu, and not before

Her window binary is verified, never assumed: installers stamp it with a hash of the shell sources, a failed rebuild retires the previous binary (navi-apex-shell.stale) instead of leaving it to be run, and the launchers refuse to run a binary the stamp doesn't cover — an older shell is a different app wearing this build's name.

" + "

Sudo mode (v0.3.0e — Build 3)

" + "

Sudo mode lets the commands Navi runs execute as root — and since Build 3 it runs on sudo's own credential timestamp, not on anything Apex holds

You arm it in Settings → System: flip the switch and a masked prompt appears on that same card; the password is fed once to sudo -v and then forgotten by the page and the bridge alike — never stored, logged or synced, anywhere. What persists is one on/off flag in the config and sudo's own timestamp

While the timestamp lives, her elevated commands run as sudo -n (never prompting); when it lapses, the status column and the Settings card read Expired, and elevated commands refuse honestly — naming the expiry — until you re-warm. Disarming (from Settings or the status column) flips the flag and kills the timestamp with sudo -k: instant and total

The status column no longer owns the switch; it reads the state — Armed or Expired while the feature is on, and absent entirely while it is off. Every elevated command Navi runs is on the record: an append-only audit (config/sudo-audit.jsonl — timestamp, the command as run, the chat it served, its exit status), viewable read-only on the Settings card

The audit deliberately does not ride Sync. One honest cost: on a machine whose sudo asks a fingerprint reader before the password, each fresh sudo -n still runs PAM — but it fails fast instead of waiting the reader out, and the arm's one sudo -v pays the full conversation once per timestamp window

The DHD prerequisite installer rides the same timestamp now: arm sudo mode first if a DHD step needs root.

" + "

Shell sessions — the full shell (CLI Mode, Build 3)

" + "

One-shot commands are half the story. Each chat can hold one standing interactive session — a real shell on a real terminal (a PTY), living in the bridge, keyed to the chat

Open one by latching the composer's CLI toggle (the old >_ button retired in Build 4 — the toggle is the door, and the composer's lines type into the session while it is latched); it survives messages and window reloads, and everything it does streams into the thread as a terminal record: lines typed are badged by author — OPERATOR or NAVI — because Navi can drive the same session
When a step needs a stateful shell (answering a prompt, a REPL, an interactive tool), she types into it herself and sees its output on her next turn

The shell is a tool in her hand, never her voice (v0.4.2e, #232): conversation is answered in conversation, when she does drive she says what she is running and why in the same reply, and a turn that would otherwise come back as nothing but terminal output is re-asked once so you always get an answer in words — with the result spoken, not the session's banner

A program that takes the full screen (an editor, a monitor) renders on a real terminal grid in a pane above the composer on the desktop — click the pane and type to the program. On a phone there is no pane: the session streams into the thread instead, and the session header says so — an honest degradation, named, not a squeezed pretend-terminal

Since Build 5 there is exactly one input: the composer — the session's live status and its Close live in a header above the composer (or in the pane's head while a program holds the screen), and latching CLI always brings the session forward — the thread scrolled to its record, the composer focused — however long it sat behind the Navi latch

Sessions end when you close them, when the shell exits, or after 30 minutes without input — the thread notes the closing and its reason either way. If the bridge restarts, the session is gone and the record says exactly that; nothing fakes continuity
Elevation never rides the session: it runs under its own session id, so sudo inside it prompts in-terminal like any terminal, and sudo mode's timestamp does not leak into it

Sessions are local to the seat whose bridge holds them — a reply borrowed over the Mesh does not move your shell.

" + "

When the shell wakes (v0.4.6e, #240). Her driving is gated by the bridge, not just by her judgment: a shell block in her reply is executed only on a machine-directed turn — the composer latched to CLI, a session already open in the chat and mid-flow, or your message itself asking for machine work (files, processes, services, the state of the box, in whatever natural words)

On a conversation turn — a general question, a remark — a block is simply not run: no session is born, nothing is typed, and she answers in words. The gate is deliberately easy to pass with a real machine ask; it exists so conversation never reaches the terminal

Lines that do drive are checked as they are typed: a copied prompt prefix ($ ) is stripped, and a line that reads as a sentence rather than a command is refused and named in the session record instead of being typed into bash
And when a drive leaves her reply empty and she is re-asked, the re-ask shows her the session's actual output — she narrates only what the terminal showed, and if nothing ran, that is what she says

The same rules bind a reply borrowed over the Mesh exactly as they bind a local one.

" + "

Her measured vitals (v0.4.6e, #187). Navi cannot feel her own speed — so the bridge times every generation she makes on this machine (tokens, tokens per second, time to first token, the whole request) and shows her the recent figures in her context, beside the Guardian brief
Ask her how fast she is and she answers from those measurements — or tells you plainly that she has none

She never invents a speed, a benchmark, or a stress test: a number about herself is either measured by the bridge or not said.

" + "

Output cards — the thread folds itself

" + "

When the conversation moves on, the bulky parts of earlier exchanges fold into small cards so the thread stays readable: a terminal block folds into a card whose line shows the command in its colors, how it ended (like exit 0), and the first line of its output; a long reply from Navi — 500 characters or more, eight lines or more, or one containing a code block — folds into a card labeled Navi reply with its first line and its size

Click a card to open it and read the whole thing; click again to fold it. The card you are still in — everything from your last message onward — never folds. Folding is only about looks: nothing is deleted, the whole history stays in the thread and on disk, and Navi still sees the full output as her context, exactly as before

Clearing the chat clears the cards with it.

" + "

Your command shows once

" + "

A command you run shows exactly once in the thread: in your own line, in its colors. The terminal block under it carries the output only — no repeated command line inside the block

A small line under the block says how the command ended (like exit 0) when that is known.

" + "

Colors for commands

" + "

Command lines are colored the same way everywhere — while you type in the chat bar, in your sent line in the thread, and on a folded card: the command word is one color when the system knows it and another when it does not, and flags, quoted words, file paths, numbers, operators like |, and $VARIABLES each get their own
After a pipe, the next word is colored as a command again, because it is one. Every theme tunes these colors for its own surfaces, so they stay readable in all twelve themes

Ordinary sentences to Navi stay plain — only lines that read as commands get the colors.

" + "

The shell remembers — recall, search, completion, and shortcuts

" + "

Your command history is kept in one place, like a shell's history file: it survives switching chats, clearing a chat, and closing the page, and it holds up to 200 commands
With the suggestion list closed, press the Up arrow to walk back through commands you have run and the Down arrow to walk forward again — going past the newest brings back what you had typed

Press Ctrl+R to search the history: type some letters and the newest matching command shows; press Ctrl+R or the arrow keys to step through matches, Enter or Tab to put the match in the bar (it does not run yet), and Escape to cancel and get your typed line back

As you type a command, the list now completes more than the first word: file and folder paths complete from the real filesystem (a folder completes with a slash and opens its contents), known flags and subcommands for common commands like git and ls are offered, and arguments you have used with that command before are offered too, marked as used before

The editing shortcuts from the shell work as well: Ctrl+A and Ctrl+E jump to the start and end of the line, Ctrl+U cuts everything before the cursor, Ctrl+K cuts everything after it, Ctrl+W cuts the word before the cursor, and Ctrl+Y pastes back what a cut took

History shortcuts like !! (the last command), !$ (its last argument), and !3 (the third command in the history) never run silently: the first Enter rewrites the bar with the expanded command and asks you to check it — press Enter again to run exactly what you see.

" + "

Raw terminal work — Chat's CLI mode

" + "

There is no separate terminal view: Chat's CLI mode is the terminal

Press the composer's CLI toggle once and it latches — every line you send runs as a command and the raw output lands in the thread as a terminal block, with nothing of Navi in the loop until you press Navi (or start a line with >) to latch back

The same installed commands decide what counts as a command, the same autocomplete finishes the command word as you type, and sudo mode — armed in Settings → System — covers the commands you run this way while its timestamp lives

One command is the composer's own, in either mode: type /cls (or /clear) and send it to clear the current chat — the thread empties and its folded cards reset, exactly what the old Clear chat button did before it retired; the line itself is never sent, never run, and never enters the history.

" + "

Chats live on the server now

" + "

Your chats are kept by the bridge, not by this browser window: plain files in config/chats/ on the machine Apex runs on, one per thread

Open Apex from the desktop, through DHD, or from a second browser on the same install and you are looking at the same conversations — sign in on your server from work and the thread you left on the laptop is simply there

The browser keeps a local copy as a cache and an offline fallback, and the first time a browser with older chats meets an empty server store, its chats are imported as the seed — never discarded. Your uploads index rides with the chats

Chats are also the ninth backup essential: tick Chats in Settings → GitHub & Backup and the threads ride the ready-to-fly backup; a restore converges them — newest wins per thread, and where both machines moved the same thread on, both versions survive, the incoming one as a dated sibling. Nothing is ever merged away silently

The one exception is the main thread: it is a single thread on every machine, so its copies merge by message rather than surviving side by side (v0.4.10e, #251).

" + "

The phone composer \u2014 the Chat tools list (v0.4.7e, #246)

" + "

On a phone the composer bar is two things: the input and a \u2630 Chat tools button at its end, in the slot the Call button used to hold

Three tools live in the list that button opens \u2014 New case, Attach and Call \u2014 each a full-width row with its icon and its name. Picking one closes the list and does the thing, exactly as the old bar buttons did \u2014 the same handlers, the same form, the same picker, the same call

There is no composer mic on a phone at all \u2014 not in the bar, not in the list: dictation into the composer is a desktop affordance. On a phone, voice is a call: while a call is live, the call card's own Push to talk is the voice control, and it is untouched by any of this

The CLI/Navi latch and the route pill beneath the bar are state, not tools, and stay exactly where they were, with the list open or closed.

" + "

What stayed out of the list is what is state, not tools: the CLI | Navi latch and the route pill under the bar never moved, because they say how your next line will travel and must stay visible while you type

Above phone widths nothing changes at all: the four tools sit in the bar itself, and there is no \u2630 button.

" + "

Context awareness \u2014 she knows the Row (v0.4.9e, #248)

" + "

Apex and nocturnerow.com are one ecosystem, and Navi reads the Row's half of it

The bridge fetches the site's public record \u2014 the Dispatches, the Roadmap chapters, the Apex and Navi pages, and the release signals \u2014 and caches it on this machine (config/row-feed.json), refreshing on a cadence and naming the fetch time wherever the record is used

Ask her for news from the Row and she summarizes the latest Dispatch in her own words and names its date; ask what's new with you and she answers from the release signals and her own running build; ask what can you do and she answers from this documentation \u2014 the corpus that shipped with the build
She speaks from the record or says she doesn't have it: if the Row can't be reached, the last good cache serves and she says when it's from; with neither, she says so

No invented posts, releases, or capabilities.

" + "

Her measured pace rides the same road: when her recent generations on this hardware average slow, she may say she's sluggish \u2014 and name the remedy, borrowing through the Mesh or joining the federation, offering to walk you through the gate's seven steps. An offer, once per conversation, never an act and never a nag

Her presence line draws from the same well: alongside the canned pool, the bridge may compose a line from safe, named state only \u2014 her version, a waiting update, the bell's counts, Mesh and federation state \u2014 template-made by the bridge, never model-written, and never from your cases, chats, or private detail.

" + "

The living greeting (v0.5.13e, #288)

" + "

Home's Brief opens with her greeting, and the greeting is alive: Good <part of day>, <your name> — the name from your operator profile, the part of day from this seat's clock with a real night band (the operator's day starts at midnight, so the small hours read as night, not as a stretched evening)

Under it, one line of hers — a statement, a quip, a nod — composed by the bridge from her actual statuses: the Mesh's state, the tray's unread count, the wire's health, her watches, this seat's build. Every fact in the line is one the bridge measured; the play is in the framing, never in invented facts, and the line rotates rather than repeating itself back-to-back

Then the brief continues — and your Pulse digest rides in it, naming only the watches with something new.

" }, { id: "chips-guide", title: "Chips development guide", related: ["navi-functions", "chips-publishing"], html: "

Chips — chips, the catalog, and the Studio

" + "

A chip is a small Python module shipped as a chip: a .png whose entire codebase rides inside the image
A loadable chip declares command, use, aliases and params, and defines run(arguments)
Chips reach Navi through navi_internal.navi_instance — print_message(text) to speak, llm_chat(message) to ask her model, process_message(text) for her full pipeline

Every method is written up in full on this wiki's Navi Chip Functions page — the documentation is their home.

" + "

Navi User Repo (NUR) searches GitHub for repos tagged navi-chips — that topic is the whole store

The Saints Sec Chips and Community Chips tabs are where you find and install chips: a card there shows whether you already have the chip, and that is all it does with it. A chip that is already on this machine — installed from its repo, or forged in Chip Studio under the same name — reads INSTALLED on its catalog card and its Install button sits grayed out: there is no second install over the copy you have

Install tracks the latest release; a newer release offers an update, which you take from the chip's card on the Local Chips tab. Chip Studio is where chips are written: a full code editor with highlighting, find, templates, and a live structure check

To publish: public repo, the navi-chips topic, a release tag as the version.

" + "

Editing a chip you already have. Local Chips is where you manage the chips you have — its card carries every management action: Run, Download .png, Edit in Studio, Edit README, Export for GitHub, Publish to GitHub, Check for updates / Update, and Delete

Uninstalling is not fenced into that one card anymore: an installed chip's catalog card carries Uninstall too, and so does its sleeve in ChipDeck — cartridge and install record go together from any of them, and a chip with local edits asks before it goes

Any chip in the folder can go back to the Studio — press Edit in Studio on its card in Navi User Repo (NUR) → Local Chips, or pick it in the Studio's Open a chip list: forged chips, GitHub installs, and chips you once exported and installed again all open with their whole file set, root.py and modules together. Saving re-forges the chip with your changes inside

If the chip came from GitHub, saving marks it edited locally: the app says plainly that your copy no longer matches the published one, and an Update will refuse rather than quietly overwrite your edits. To share your version, use Export for GitHub in Navi User Repo (NUR) and cut a new release

Knowledge packs work the same way: Edit in RAG Studio on the RAG tab reopens any pack — documents in or out, name and description adjusted — and saving rebuilds its index on your machine.

" + "

Installs prove themselves. When a chip installs, the bridge re-scans the chips folder before it answers: if the cartridge landed on disk but does not list, the answer says so, and why — an install is never reported done on faith
A cartridge whose payload will not parse is listed in Local Chips as couldn't be read — visible and deletable, but it cannot run, and the runners skip it

Older chips still run: installing walks the repo's folders recursively, so a chip laid out as a package keeps its relative paths and its imports resolve at run time; a repo's chip-requirements.txt is read and the chip's card shows the declared dependencies plainly — they are not installed automatically; and every chip sandbox carries the legacy navi.py shim (get_parameters, old semantics) unless the chip ships its own.

" + "

A chip's face is a card, drawn at card grade. New forges wear the family shell — black body, coral notched bands top and bottom as the cartridge's contacts (coral is the chip family's color — knowledge cartridges wear green, Mesh pairing cards blue) — with the chip's own story on it like a Mesh card's: the family header, its art large in its window, then the chip's name, what it does, and in small print its version and its output kind

The window itself is textured now: a dim QR-style tile field, seeded from the chip's name, and over it the art renders as a solid silhouette with a shade offset — the built-in glyphs (a key for cryptex, a hash mark for a hasher, a terminal for a shell tool) were redrawn as filled objects on the field's own 20-by-20 grid, so each reads at sleeve size without its name
The glyph is named in the chip's manifest (glyph in navi-chip.json); with no glyph named, a keyword read of the chip's name and description picks one

Better still, draw your own: a manifest icon — 20 rows of 20 characters, # for the accent, o for its shade, . for empty — outranks the built-in glyph and rides inside the picture like the glyph does; art in the wrong shape is refused in plain words at forge time, and a picture whose art arrives damaged simply falls back to its glyph

A chip no art claims keeps the older name-seeded pattern in the window as a fallback. The version itself also rides inside the picture now, so the cartridge states its own version wherever it travels — on the face, in the install receipt, and on its ChipDeck sleeve

Faces are drawn at forge time — installed and published pictures keep the faces they were forged with until they are re-forged.

" + "

Running chips from chat, and Workflows

" + "

Any loaded chip runs from the conversation: ./<name> — the way you run a program — with its arguments after it (./navi-cryptex hex -e -t \"Hello world!\"); a short name resolves (./cryptex finds navi-cryptex), a bare ./ answers with the shelf itself, and typing ./ in the composer offers the chips' names as you type

/chip <name> remains as the long-form alias, alongside “run the <name> chip” and its name alone — its output lands in the thread. Under the CLI latch ($), ./ is the shell's own again: the latch decides, never a guess

There is no pill row above the composer anymore — the shelf lives in ChipDeck now, and running lives at the keyboard. The bridge genuinely runs it: code defining run() executes with a working navi_internal; a chip that only declares an output shows that instead

Workflows chain chips in order — each chip's output becomes the next chip's input, and the last output is the result.

" + "

Writing a chip, step by step

" + "

A chip is a small Python program Navi can run
A chip is a set of files: root.py — the main file, the one Navi runs; every chip has exactly one — and helper files like helpers.py, extra Python files root.py brings in with import helpers

The rules root.py follows (the Studio checks them and underlines what is missing):

    " + "
  1. It brings in Navi with import navi_internal and takes hold of her with navi_instance = navi_internal.navi_instance.
    2. " + "
  2. It says its name with command — the word people type to run it.
    3. " + "
  3. It says what it does with use — one short line.
    4. " + "
  4. It can list other names in aliases and describe its inputs in params (what -help shows).
    5. " + "
  5. It defines run(arguments) — the part Navi calls; arguments.text is the words typed after the chip's name.
" + "

Through navi_instance a chip can print_message(text) (show a line), llm_chat(text) (ask her model), process_message(text) (hand text to Navi as if typed), get_user()/set_user(name), clear_terminal(), and chat_with_navi()

Every one of those functions is explained in full — what it takes, what it gives back, and when to reach for it — on this wiki's Navi Chip Functions page, in the sidebar. Making one:

  1. Chips tab → Chip Studio.
  2. Name it.
  3. Write root.py.
  4. Add helper files in the file list.
  5. Forge chip.

The whole file set packs into the chip picture

The editor colors code, guides indents, folds blocks, finds words in every file, saves on its own, underlines missing pieces, and takes focus mode — the app's one expand idiom, the Vault's — which puts everything but the editor away; its toolbar holds the rest (command palette, outline, zoom, wrap)

On a phone the Studio works one pane at a time — Face, Code, Test under a full-width switch — with the face as a collapsible strip, a snippet shelf and autocomplete over the keyboard, and Run, Forge and Save pinned to the thumb

The writing desk itself has its own page in the sidebar: The Chip Studio editor.

" }, { id: "navi-functions", title: "Navi Chip Functions", related: ["chips-guide", "studio-editor"], html: "

Navi Chip Functions — what a chip can call

" + "

A chip does not run off on its own — it runs inside Navi, and everything it does with her goes through one doorway: navi_internal, her own chip API

At the top of root.py the chip brings her in and takes hold of the live instance:

    " + "
  • import navi_internal — brings Navi's chip API into the chip.
    • " + "
  • navi_instance = navi_internal.navi_instance — the live Navi herself

Every function below is called on this instance; take hold of it first, at the top of run() or at module level." + "

Talking and thinking. The three functions a chip reaches for most:

    " + "
  • print_message(text, include_ai_name=True) — prints a message to Navi's terminal, with her name in front of it unless you pass include_ai_name=False

This is the main way a chip talks: results, progress, errors — if the operator should see it, it goes through here." + "
  • llm_chat(user_message, called_from_app=False) — sends a message to Navi's model and returns its response, so a chip can ask her to think and then work with what she says

The published navi-nmap chip uses it to turn raw scan output into a summary a person can read." + "
  • process_message(user_message) — runs a message through Navi's full pipeline — command detection and all — exactly as if the operator had typed it

Reach for it when the chip wants Navi herself to handle something, not just her model." + "

The difference between the last two matters: llm_chat is a question and an answer; process_message is handing her the keyboard.

" + "

The operator, the terminal, and the session

" + "

Who she is working for:

    " + "
  • get_user() — returns the current operator's name: the name selected in Settings, the one her greetings use.
    • " + "
  • set_user(sys_user) — sets the current operator's name.
" + "

The screen and the session:

    " + "
  • clear_terminal() — clears the terminal screen and reprints the Navi banner

A chip that is about to draw something full-screen starts here." + "
  • chat_with_navi() — opens an interactive chat session with Navi, dropping the operator into conversation with her from inside the chip.
    • " + "
  • setup_history() — initializes the history for prompt sessions, so a chip that runs its own prompts keeps them navigable.
    • " + "
  • setup_navi_vocab() — registers commands and aliases with Navi's vocabulary (the spaCy entity ruler), so her command detection learns the words the chip brought with it.
    • " + "

    This page is their home. The full method list lives here in the documentation, complete and kept current — Chip Studio carries no method panels of its own, so the list is written once and read while you write
Upstream, the project's chip-developer wiki page, Developing Chips — Indepth, documents navi_internal.py's NaviApp class — the source this page follows

New to chips entirely? Start with the Chips development guide, in the sidebar.

" }, { id: "studio-editor", title: "The Chip Studio editor", related: ["chips-guide", "glossary"], html: "

The Chip Studio editor, button by button

" + "

The editor is the writing desk inside Chip Studio — the place chip code gets written

It looks plain on purpose: everything it does is one click or one key away, and this page names each thing in the order you will meet it.

" + "

These pages live in the Docs view. This wiki's home is the Docs view — the main documentation window

Press Pop out at the top of the Docs view and the wiki detaches into its own window, open at the page you were reading, so you can keep it beside the editor or the chat while you work. Pop back in — in the popped window or in the Docs view holding its place — returns it to the Docs view, same page

The pop-out is always another window entirely — the app's own second window — never a panel inside this one; if a window host ever blocks it, the Docs view says so and offers a direct link that opens the wiki in a new window instead.

" + "

The file list. On the left is the list of the chip's files. root.py sits at the top — the main file, the one Navi runs

Click any file to open it. Buttons under the list add a new file, rename the open one, or delete it (root.py cannot be deleted — every chip needs its main file). A dot beside a file's name means “changed, not saved yet”

Everything in the list travels with the chip: forge the chip and all the files go inside the picture.

" + "

Focus mode. The button in the toolbar with the four corners puts everything but the editor away — the rail, the status column, the Studio's own header rows — room to think on a big chip. It is the same expand idiom the Vault uses; the app has exactly one
Press it again, or press Esc, to bring the room back

Your place in the code does not move either way.

" + "

On a phone the Studio works one pane at a time — Face, Code, Test under a full-width switch — the face art as a collapsible strip, and Run, Forge and Save pinned in a bar at the thumb that reserves its own height in the layout, so nothing ever slides under it

A snippet shelf and an autocomplete row sit over the keyboard as the primary input aids. No desktop feature is cut to make room.

" + "

Reading the code. The editor colors the code — names, words, and numbers each get their own color, so the shape of a line is visible at a glance. Thin vertical lines (indent guides) show where a block starts and ends

Click the small arrow beside a block to fold it away; click again to bring it back. Folding is only for your eyes — a save always keeps the whole file.

" + "

Finding things. Find searches the open file, and can replace what it finds. Find in all files searches every file in the chip and lists the hits as file and line — click a hit to jump straight there

The Outline list names every function and class in the file; pick one to jump to it. The command palette also has go to line for when you know the number.

" + "

The red squiggles. A wavy red line under code means the chip is missing something it needs — a file with no run(), say. The bar under the editor says what is wrong, in words

Fix the words and the line goes away.

" + "

More than one cursor. Hold Alt and click to plant another cursor. Type once and every cursor types at once — handy for renaming a word in ten places. The palette's “clear extra cursors” puts you back to one.

" + "

The command palette. The Commands button opens one box that lists everything the editor can do

Type a few letters of the thing you want, press Enter, and it happens. If you forget where a button lives, the palette knows.

" + "

Minimap, zoom, wrap. The thin strip on the right is a tiny picture of the whole file — click it to jump. Zoom makes the letters bigger or smaller

Wrap folds long lines onto the screen instead of letting them run off the side.

" + "

Saving. On a chip that already exists, the editor saves by itself while you work — watch the dot beside the file's name disappear. Ctrl+S saves right now

On a brand-new chip, Forge chip is the save.

" + "

The face art box. Under the description sits a box for the chip's own face art: 20 rows of 20 characters — # draws in the accent, o in its shade, . leaves a cell empty
It is the chip's icon in its manifest: your art outranks the built-in glyph on the forged face, and it travels inside the picture. Leave the box empty and the chip wears its glyph

Art in the wrong shape — the wrong number of rows, a row of the wrong length, a character outside the three — is refused in plain words when you save, never silently dropped.

" }, { id: "chips-publishing", title: "Publishing chips", related: ["chips-guide", "rag"], html: "

Publishing a chip on GitHub

" + "

Publishing means putting your chip on GitHub (a website that holds code) so any Navi can find and install it

The export builds the whole package — you never copy files by hand:

    " + "
  1. Forge the chip in Chip Studio first.
    2. " + "
  2. Open Chips → Navi User Repo (NUR) → Local Chips and find your chip — installed chips under Installed, your own makes under Forged.
    3. " + "
  3. Type a version like 0.1.0 (a version is just a label: this is the first one) and press Export for GitHub, then download the ZIP (one file holding many files).
    4. " + "
  4. On GitHub, make a new public repository (one project's folder on GitHub; public means everyone can see it) and unzip the export at its top.
    5. " + "
  5. On the repo page, open the About gear and add the topic navi-chips — a topic is a label, and this label is how Navi finds chips.
    6. " + "
  6. Publish a release (GitHub's way of saying: this exact version, ready to download) — the version tag is created with that publish, so tag it with the same version.
" + "

Signed in to GitHub? Skip the ZIP: Publish to GitHub on the chip's card does the middle steps for you — it creates the public repo (an existing one is updated, and she says so), sets the navi-chips topic on its own, and uploads the same files the export builds

The repo name is pre-filled from the chip's name and yours to edit before anything uploads. And Publish finishes the job: it creates the version tag and publishes the release itself, with the chip picture attached. If that version is already released, Publish refuses and says so — bump the version in the manifest instead of overwriting a release

And the README page is yours too: Edit README on the chip's card edits the generated page; your text is kept inside the chip and ships in the export and the upload alike, with a restore back to the generated page.

" + "

Inside the export: root.py and the helper files (install downloads every Python file in the repo recursively, keeping folder paths, so package layouts survive — root.py, or the entry named in the manifest, is the chip; the rest are its modules; a chip-requirements.txt at the repo top is read and shown on the chip's card as declared dependencies, never installed automatically); navi-chip.json, a small card with the name, description, version, and entry file; the chip .png; and a generated README.md page
Installs and updates: Navi User Repo (NUR) searches GitHub for the navi-chips topic; Install brings the whole file set down as a chip; a release with a bigger tag offers every install an update

Knowledge packs publish the same way — see the RAG page.

" }, { id: "chipdeck", title: "ChipDeck — the binder", related: ["chips-guide", "rag", "mesh"], html: "

One binder for everything that rides a picture.

" + "

What lives in the binder

" + "

ChipDeck (in the menu, under Chips) is a gallery of sleeves, one per picture-riding thing on this machine: every installed chip, every Apex | Mesh pairing card on file in config/mesh/cards/, and every knowledge pack, drawn as its cartridge

Each sleeve shows the actual picture — the cartridge's real bytes, not an icon for it — with the thing's state at a glance (installed from where, edited locally, paired, active) and its actions gathered underneath: chips run (straight into chat, as ./<name>), download their picture, open in Chip Studio, and uninstall; Mesh cards download and unpair; packs activate, deactivate, download their cartridge, and remove.

" + "

Drop a picture on the Deck and it slots in. The data inside the picture says what it is — chip, knowledge cartridge, or Mesh card — and each kind installs through its own door, with its own checks
The receipt names the version the picture itself carries, and a chip's sleeve states it too — a picture forged before versions rode inside simply shows none, and nothing guesses one for it

Cases, findings, evidence, timeline

Mark one case open and it becomes the case Navi works: ask her in chat to “file that as a finding” and she files the exchange into the open case and tells you she did — out loud, naming the case and the file, never silently

The latest terminal or chip output from chat can be filed as a finding from the case page, too.

" + "

The case chat, her own findings, and the open case (Build 15)

" + "

Every case has its own chat, made the first time the case is opened and returned to ever after — one case, one canonical thread, riding the same server-side store as every other chat (it survives machines the way chats now do)
It is listed on the Chats tab with a CASE tag, and Open the case chat on the case page walks you straight into it

The chat is a reference, not a container: the case's content stays in the Vault's plain files.

" + "

While a case is open, Navi can file her own findings into it — conclusions she reaches, in her own words, filed under her own name (the finding's frontmatter says so, the case page marks it FILED BY NAVI, and a line lands in the timeline)
It is never silent: the filing happens in the thread where she reached the conclusion, and the receipt — the finding's title and its path — hangs on her message there

She files nothing from unrelated chats and nothing without that receipt.

The open case is visible: the status column carries it (CASE, in the stats), and in the case's own chat a chip above the thread names it — tap it to jump to the case
