# CHANGELOG.md — part 1 of 2
Source: `CHANGELOG.md` in the shipped Apex v0.6.9 tree (build stamps 2026-11-19.41, seq 41), reproduced verbatim below. Lines 1–381 of CHANGELOG.md.
# Changelog

All notable changes to Apex are recorded here. Version language, from 0.1.7 on: a full release carries the bare number (tag v0.1.7); a pre-release is an Edge build and carries the e suffix (tag v0.1.7e). Releases before 0.1.7 were cut as alphas with the a suffix — that history stands as written below.

Release tag: v0.6.9e — chapter 0.6's tenth build: **the bench-truth build**. No product behavior changes in this build — what changed is that the regression bench now tells the truth. The campaign had carried the same 19 failing suites since v0.6.6e; this build triaged every one of them against the shipped tree (dossier: `files/standing-19-triage.md`), and the verdict was **zero genuine product defects**
The 19 were the bench's own rot, and this build is the bench repaired:

- **Fifteen suites were stale, and now assert the current truth.** Eight had been dying on paths written for a build-dir layout the campaign staging outgrew (headless1, llamaintegrity1, bootorder1, installvoice1, settings11, relaunch2, scopeproof1's tree pin, and the per-build stamp pins in shellpty1, selftalk1, migrate12, applyboot1 that nobody had rolled since the v0.3.0e–v0.4.10e era) — each is re-pinned in this build's bench, recorded in the campaign runner, and benches the shipped candidate again

Two asserted surfaces that deliberate reworks superseded: casefiling1's flag-in-note legs (superseded by #266's case purity — the grounding flag rides the receipt, never the case file; the legs now assert exactly that, purity included) and fedichatui1's header/settings legs (superseded by #270 — the room's facts live in the About & settings window, and the legs now render it)

Two pinned the presence pool at 36 lines after it grew to 38 by its own law (presencepool1, safestatus1 — re-pinned verbatim at 38, as presencepool2 already held). One slept 1.6 s past a 1-second vanishing term and called it past (rooms1 — the shipped prune runs on whole-second arithmetic; the sleep is now 2.6 s and the assertion is unchanged)

- **Three suites stand down by name where the sandbox cannot judge.** scopeproof1 needs a private systemd --user bus and sudo1 a dedicated unprivileged bench user; both now probe for what they need and print a named `ENV-DOWN` line, counting those legs separately — never as passes, never as failures

updaterfix1's campaign death was cross-suite port contention (a sibling suite's orphan held 8675; the installer rightly refused to kill a bridge it could not identify) — the runner's between-suite sweep now reaps campaign-rooted orphans, applyboot1's cleanup kills its own driver, and updaterfix1 pre-flights the port

- **Two legs retired as expired.** applybench1's golden-control legs were a negative control against a pre-#271 installer; every golden since v0.5.7e carries the fix, so the legs could never pass again. They are retired in-suite with the premise named; the candidate legs and the surviving golden leg run as before
- **The campaign's pass condition is now zero unexplained:** every suite passes, or its only non-passing legs are env-down or retired and named as such in the build report.

Release tag: v0.6.8e — chapter 0.6's ninth build: **Seraph, the SIEM suite** — the SIEM floor (#153) lands as a configuration of standard Apex, and the nav takes its ruled shape (#334). Alex's scope for the round: standard Apex first, manageable whole from DHD.

- **Seraph — the watch floor (#335, capping #153).** A new top-level **SIEM** group holds **Seraph**, the SIEM suite. Any seat can take the **sensor** role, the **console** role, or both, set on the Seraph page itself

A sensor watches the one segment it is plugged into, passively: the segment's living inventory (ARP, DHCP leases), the seat's connection table as flow and DNS-era metadata (metadata, never payloads), its listening services, and its own auth logs. Every snapshot names its **gaps** — what this vantage cannot see — on the sensor's dashboard

The v1 detection set: **watchlist matches** (matched on the sensor; the list never leaves the machine — #314's discipline, the Wire's declared list included), a **new face** on the network, **beaconing** and **impossible hours** (against the operator's sleep window), **failed sign-in bursts**, **scan patterns** from the receiving end, and a **new listening service** on a known host

Detections ride the standing alert spine in **Navi's voice** (#319) and can be **filed as a case** from the dashboard — the detection becomes the case's founding exhibit, hashed by the bridge at filing time (#326/#330) — or dismissed

Remote sensors report home over the **Mesh** (signed, pairing-authenticated, registry-bound), **spooling** when the road is dark and draining when it lights; a revoked sensor is a **tombstone** whose late reports are refused by name

Per-sensor dashboards carry inventory, listeners, top talkers and detections, with an **SSH tab** beside them (the operator's own key and session, opened by hand, in the seat's shell machinery). Retention is operator-set (30 days default); open and filed detections never age out silently
The sensor edition's preconfigured image — PIA's shape — is a later round; this round is standard Apex, and the suite works whole without a PIA

- **Seraph's marks.** The suite carries her own icon family: the **working glyph** (two rings, a gold flame, gold wings — a clean redraw that reads at nav size and re-skins with themes and both layouts) in the nav and on dashboards, the **ceremonial winged eye** on sensor page heroes, and a per-tool icon set (Registration, Discovery, Flows, Logs, Watchlist, Detections, Dashboard, SSH) drawn from the same geometry

- **The nav takes its ruled shape (#334).** The "Apex | " prefix drops from every group — the bar's head already says Apex — and the groups read **Navi**, **Casework**, **Network**, **SIEM**, with **Utilities** where it always sat at the foot. Casework is the old Apps group renamed, its children reordered with **The Wire promoted to the head**: The Wire, Case Files, The Dossier, Vault
Display only — group keys, view keys and behavior are untouched — and the in-app docs' locators were swept in the same round.

Release tag: v0.6.7e — chapter 0.6's eighth build, the field-fix build. Spartan0311's twelve-issue field batch (#305–#316) was triaged against the shipped tree, Alex ruled "bake what will fix it for now," and this build carries the fix-now slate at full depth — plus the two honesty fixes from the same morning (#331, #332). Four items are consciously deferred and named below; they stay open.

- **The local prompt gets a budget (#310).** The chat assembly is now measured against the seat's own context before anything is sent: per-block caps on the briefs that can grow, a shedding order that drops background before it ever touches her persona or the working case, teaching blocks that ride only on the turns that can use them (shell teaching on machine-directed turns, case teaching on case turns), history trimmed oldest-first, and the estimate riding every chat payload as a readout

What cannot fit even shed is refused BY NAME — the numbers stated, the doors named — instead of dying truncated at the model. The context derivation's lowest band floors at 4096, the product's own prompt floor, in the bridge and the installer alike: a 4096 seat holds a conversation again

- **Borrowed replies are inert (#315).** A reply served by a Mesh lender is answered with, never acted on: the shell gate is shut for it outright, its memory markers are held as proposals instead of saves, its finding markers are stripped without filing — and the gate's own failure path now fails CLOSED, so an exception is never again read as machine intent

What leaves for a lender is cleaned at the door (#314): no marker teaching, no shell teaching, the intel brief in its share shape. - **The watchlist stays home (#314).** The intel digest served to peers no longer carries stack-match or watchlist-hit material — counts and headlines ride, the operator's own term list never does, per the module's founding doctrine

Borrowed prompts carry the share-shaped brief, and the GitHub backup's settings item no longer includes the intel watchlist. - **Lending to new members defaults OFF (#316).** The sanitize default now matches the Federation page's promise ("off until you turn it on"): an absent key is off, a stored true stays true, and the switch gate was benched three ways — flip, stored state, post-reload view

- **The roster version is real (#311).** The federation roster sync returns the roster's actual version instead of a wrapped-dict artifact, so the version sentence and the anti-entropy checks read a number that exists

- **The node's own gate door is throttled (#313, leg 1).** The bridge's /__gate branch carries the same throttle as the DHD door — five wrong codes lock it for five minutes, a locked door refuses even the right code with the wait named, a correct code clears the count

Legs 2 (the first-device bootstrap) and 3 (proxy-aware client IPs) are NOT in this build: leg 2 awaits a doctrine ruling, leg 3 is deferred with the full-depth pile. - **The updater stops fighting systemd (#305).** On a boot-startup seat the apply helper signals navi-bridge.service and lets the unit own the restart — no more immortal start.sh processes adopting the unit's bridge and polling it forever, one per Apply

- **Apply evidence survives the swap (#306, cheap leg).** The updates/ evidence — apply traces, install and relaunch logs, job records — is carried across the tree swap like config, so a successful Apply stops deleting the record of itself. Package payloads do not ride. The full relocation of the stage home out of the tree remains open

- **The install record tells the truth (#308).** Both install markers (.apex-provisioned, .apex-install-record) now write the stamp of the tree actually being installed, read from that tree's own bridge — finishing the #271 rider

- **A root shell is refused at another user's tree (#312).** A genuine root shell installing while a non-root user owns an Apex tree on the machine is refused BY NAME — the owner and their door named, --as-root the spoken override. MIGRATED.txt is read at last: a proven-migrated tree is never re-migrated, whatever home a later invocation targets

And the installer no longer advises kill -9 against another user's processes — it names the owner and their own stop door. - **Case talk knows its watch (#331).** When a case is in context, her case facts carry whether a Pulse watch stands attached to it — the topic and last check when one stands; an explicit "none stands" when none does

"Actively monitored" is now a sentence she can only say over a watch that exists. - **One phone, one record (#332).** Push subscriptions key on the phone's door-device identity: a re-subscribe from the same device replaces its record — new endpoint, label carried — however often iOS re-mints endpoints

The Settings roster shows each record's subscribed date, and any seat can remove a record; that record stops ringing and nothing else is touched. - **The reference shelf folds (#333, added on Alex's order mid-bake).** A case's reference shelf collapses to its header — the header row is a real button (≥44px at phone widths) carrying the source line and the item count in both states

The fold is remembered per case in the seat's view state and survives reload; it behaves identically at desktop and phone widths, in the app window, and in Standard and LCARS layouts alike. Folding changes nothing else: items, Remove, "use reference R#", and Navi's reading of the shelf work exactly as before
- **Deferred by the rescope, still open:** #307 (the rollback point), #306's full stage relocation, #309 (the Mesh dial rework), #313 legs 2–3.

Release tag: v0.6.6e — chapter 0.6's seventh build, the case suite. Filing learns every part of the case, the button learns to sense which part a reply is, the Vault gathers the case files into their own section, a filed heading stops printing three times, and a Wire story can pull a whole case together around itself — briefing, leads, and her recommended next steps staged for approval.

- **File as {Type}, for every part (#326).** The filing doors — the tap, the operator's words, the start-a-case door — now land in **all nine** of a case's parts: **task** (a list reply splits into one Tasks entry per item; prose around the list rides the receipt as the source note, never dropped, never a task), **timeline** (the entry is dated by the date the reply names for the event, or the filing moment), **evidence** (the reply stands as a text exhibit, exactly as written, its custody entry carrying the SHA-256 the bridge computed at filing time) and **report** (the reply appends to the case's report material — a register of its own, since the drawn report stays a generated export — and the formed document's Report section draws the entries first, in filed order, dated)
Every receipt names the section the filing stands in. "Note" is the one refusal left, and it names all nine parts

- **The destination is sensed (#327).** The button under a reply reads the reply's shape, deterministically, the page and the bridge running the same read: a chronological narrative (three or more dated lines) is a **timeline** entry; a list of indicator data is **observables**; an imperative next-step list is **tasks**, the button naming the count ("as tasks (5)"); a short reply whose subject is typed on its face is an **entity**; a reply opening on a date is an **event**; a reply carrying its sourcing is a **lead**; a bare indicator is an **observable**
Anything the read cannot place is a **finding** — the plain default, never dressed as a confident guess. And the operator's words naming a part govern **absolutely**, on every door, over any sense

- **The Vault's Cases section (#328).** Formed case files stand in a **Cases** section at the **bottom** of the Vault — below every other folder, set apart by its own divider — grouped by type shelf (`Cases/Investigation/<Case Name>.md`): the disk matches the desk. Existing formed files moved in the formation sweep, content-exact, the move tombstoned so Sync carries it and the old address never resurrects
- **Headings print once (#329).** A filed reply whose first line repeated its heading printed three times — the entry's heading, the rendered title inside it, the body's own opening line

The filed note keeps the reply's exact words — no writer title line is added above a body that already opens with its heading — and the surfaces that print the heading themselves (the formed document, the report export) open the body after the repeated line: exact match, or the heading with a colon, for filings from before this build exactly as for new ones, across every part and in dossier documents
A heading recurring later in a body is the author's text and stands; the answer as printed in chat is never altered

- **A case is born from the Wire (#330).** A story's **Start a case** button — or the words "start an investigation on that story" — pulls the case together in one act: the case is created from the story, the article read **whole** onto its reference shelf, one **cited lead** filed per CVE the article names (resolved through the intel catalog; an id the catalog cannot answer is a named **gap**, never a silent skip; ids past the birth cap are named too), related coverage shelved beside it (capped, one hop), the case set open

The case chat opens on **her briefing**, composed by the bridge from the case's live state — and her **recommended next tasks** stand on the Tasks register as **proposals**: Approve opens one as a standing task; Dismiss strikes it, the strike on the timeline. "Brief me" in the case's room draws a fresh briefing from the state as it stands then
The deliberate counterpart to #326: her filings are proposals; the operator's are acts.

Release tag: v0.6.5e — chapter 0.6's sixth build, the fun one. LCARS stops being only a palette and becomes a layout: Appearance gains a Layout axis, every theme works in both geometries, and flipping between them translates — nothing is lost in either direction.

- **LCARS Mode (#325).** Settings → Appearance gains a **Layout** choice beside the theme picker: **Standard** (the shipped geometry, still the default) or **LCARS Mode** — elbow-swept cards, the rail as numbered pill stacks, sweep-tab headings, pill-ended controls, condensed uppercase labels on the furniture, in the modern 2.0 proportions

The mode owns geometry, not colors: its accent slots read the **active theme**, so all twelve palettes — the LCARS palette included, the flagship pairing — work inside LCARS Mode, and Standard keeps wearing all twelve as before. The layout is stored in your config exactly like the theme and rides the settings backup beside it
The phone's dedicated interface gets the same geometry in this build — slimmer elbows, full-size touch targets, no sideways scrolling

- **The translation contract (#325).** Flipping layout, in either direction, from anywhere, is a **re-render, never a navigation or a reset**: same surface, same chat thread and scroll, same open case or document and its edit state, same switch positions, same half-filled forms, same rail groups open or closed. The picker lives in Appearance under **both** layouts, in its accustomed place — no mode hides its own exit

Chosen layout, stored config, and what a reload (or a bridge restart) shows are one truth, and the Federation page's Mesh and Fleet switches keep their gate under the new geometry: flip, stored state, and post-reload view agree, with refusals spoken on the card.

Release tag: v0.6.4e — chapter 0.6's fifth build. Sync learns whose data it is carrying: the account gate comes first — then the Vault becomes one file per case, departed fedinets stop coming back, the Mesh switch moves onto the Federation page, and the console learns to dress as LCARS.

- **Sync is account-gated (#323).** A sync set belongs to the GitHub account whose sign-in produced it, and two seats now prove they serve the same account before any data moves: over the Mesh, a **handshake door** is answered before any pull or exchange is served, and on the repo road the set's manifest is judged the same way

A refusal is **named** — operator unknown (either seat signed out; two unknown seats never converge), or a different operator, with the serving seat's account named so the fix is obvious — and recorded on the Sync card's receipt line, never a silent skip

Beside the gate, an **attribution ledger**: every synced chat, case, document and daybook entry remembers which account it arrived under, and when a seat's sign-in is established (at sign-in, and at start-up), material proven to belong to a **different** account is **purged through the ordinary delete doors** — tombstoned, so the purge itself converges — while anything locally born or unprovable stands untouched

A tray notice reports the counts. What happened in the field — one operator's cases arriving on a second operator's unsigned install — cannot recur: an unsigned seat has no account to match, and the gate fails closed

- **The Vault is one file per case (#320).** In the Vault, a case is now **a single document in a folder named for its kind** — `Incident/`, `Investigation/`, `Research/`, `Hunt/`, `Locate/`, `OSINT/` — titled with the case's own name and holding everything the case record holds: head facts, leads, findings, entities, observables, tasks, evidence, timeline and the report, in sections

Dossiers stand the same way in `Dossiers/`. The per-part fragment notes are retired: the migration is the formation sweep itself — every living case re-forms into its one file and every fragment is pruned. Rename a case or change its kind and the file moves; delete a case — or merge a dossier away — and its Vault document is deleted through the same tombstoned door as any note. If something is gone, it is gone

- **Departed fedinets stay departed (#321).** Leaving a fedinet — or a gateway dissolving one — now writes a **departure tombstone** that rides the sync set like every other deletion: a seat that left is no longer dealt back in by a sync round, and a card that still arrives for a departed fedinet is **refused by name** in the round's summary

Rejoining stays in the operator's hand alone: **importing the gateway card manually clears the departure** and re-admits the fedinet. A gateway gains the **dissolve** act — crown-confirmed, louder when it strands members — ending the fedinet for its own seat and tombstoning it everywhere its sync reaches

- **The Mesh switch lives on the Federation page (#322).** The Federation page opens with **The Mesh** card: the Mesh's own switch, riding the **same door and the same stored state** as the Mesh page's control — one state, two surfaces. The card names what rides on it: fedinets, borrowing, FediChat, and Fleet Answers all go dark with it
The switch gate holds in full — the flip, the stored state and what a reload shows are one truth — and a refusal (an identity that cannot be minted) is spoken on the card itself, the switch unmoved

- **LCARS (#324).** A twelfth theme joins the picker: the starship console, in its modern 2.0 cut — a black field, pill-ended bars and buttons with black text on the color, elbow-curved cards, uppercase condensed labels, the classic accent family (orange, peach, lilac, periwinkle, brick) with cooler blues and teals woven through

It is a **skin over the same screens**, off until chosen like every theme: the rail's groups still collapse to their header pills, every switch answers to the same state, and the lettering is your system's own condensed face — nothing is fetched.

Release tag: v0.6.3e — chapter 0.6's fourth build. The operator's hand, restored: a chosen sync direction overrides the round in flight, a cleared main chat stays cleared on every seat, the verdict never claims a convergence the main thread denies — and the alerts arrive in Navi's voice.

- **The override overrides (#317).** A chosen **Send** or **Receive** no longer queues behind a sync round already in flight. The running round is signalled to stop at its **next phase boundary** — rounds converge idempotently, so its partial work stands — and the chosen direction runs immediately after; if the in-flight round finishes first, the direction runs next, never behind a second round

**Both receipts tell the truth:** the stopped round's record names the supersession (an operator override, and the phase it stopped at) and its card face reads *Overridden — your call runs now*; the directional round's receipt is the ordinary one. A newer choice replaces an older one mid-flight — the newest direction is the one that runs
The hold remains for machine triggers (push-on-write, the occasions): preemption is the operator's privilege, exercised through the choice

- **A cleared main chat converges (#318).** Emptying the main thread (/clear, /cls) is now a **synced act with an epoch**: the chat set carries a clear marker (the moment, and the seat that emptied it), and convergence honors it on every seat — content stamped at or before the clear yields to the emptied state, post-clear messages are untouched, and the ghost-fold can never resurrect pre-clear content

Beside it, a **post-round substance check** on the main thread: after a round, the main thread's count and digest are verified against the converged set, and on a mismatch the verdict is **renamed** — *Mostly synced — the main thread disagrees (theirs N messages, ours M)* — on the round's receipt and the Sync card's last-round line. Never a clean *converged* over a divergent main thread

- **Navi sends the alerts (#319).** Push payloads — and the tray summaries they mirror, parity unchanged — speak as **Navi**: her name leads the title, never "from Apex", and the summary is composed in her voice, a written **flare line per producer class** (reminder due, standing-order report, Pulse batch, FediChat arrival, sync verdicts and update notices that earn a push) wrapped around the fact, which rides **verbatim** — reminder text, times, names, counts exact; the flare never edits the fact

The banks rotate **deterministically** (the same class and count draw the same line; consecutive draws differ) with **no model call** on the alert path. The plain factual record stays on the tray record's detail, structured fields untouched. Borrowed and federation-served alerts are announced by the **local** Navi.

Release tag: v0.6.2e — chapter 0.6's third build. The sync override: every Sync press offers Send or Receive — and Brief v2: the day brief as a markdown document, presented as a list, with Navi in the rows.

- **The sync override (#303).** A **setting** (Settings → GitHub & Backup, on by default) governs the Sync button: with it on, a press offers **Send a sync** or **Receive a sync** — a manual override, so a sync happens now, on demand, not at the automatic cadence's pace. **Send** publishes this seat's set and applies nothing; **Receive** pulls and converges and publishes nothing

Both are the standing machinery standing alone by direction — the same roads (Mesh first when lit, the backup repo otherwise), the same convergence law — never a second sync system. Each round is **receipted** with what actually moved: files published, what came down, what converged — and a direction with nothing to move says so plainly. With the setting off, a press runs the legacy full round at once

The automatic cadence is untouched. - **Brief v2 (#304).** The day brief is composed and **stored as a markdown document** — a dated title, section headings (On / Changed / Needs you / Standing), one bullet per item — and recall returns the document
No surface presents the markdown: Home's Her working day card and the chat's brief answer **draw a native list from it** — sections as headers, each item a row with its time and state

Reminders gain a **postpone** act (chat: *snooze it to tomorrow*, *push it in 30 minutes*; the act is recorded on the reminder's own record), and the **deferral count is derived** from those acts plus the days a fired reminder has been carried — never a stored counter

When a count passes one, the item's row gains a **quip in Navi's name**, deterministic and once per count, escalating with the count — professional in register for the standing orders' items. Reminders' machinery — firing, ack as a synced fact, push parity — is untouched; the greeting's day lines stay terse.

Release tag: v0.6.1e — chapter 0.6's second build. Fleet Answers: one ask, divided into whole sub-tasks, each answered whole by the machine best placed for it, composed into one answer with the seams showing.

- **Fleet Answers (#293).** Where a borrow sends one whole ask to one stronger machine, a fleet ask **decomposes** one ask into whole sub-tasks in the Mesh's existing classes — **generate**, **collect**, **lookup**, **report** — fans them out over the roads that already exist (direct pairing, a joined fedinet's roster terms, the relay when the direct road is dark), and **composes** one answer in which every contribution is **signed with its machine's name**

The unit of work stays whole — tokens and layers are never split, under any name. The wall clock of a fleet ask is the longest contribution, not the sum: a weak node that generates nothing and only asks can be answered at the fastest member's speed plus one hop. - **Membership is a toggle (#293).** Fleet participation is a **per-node toggle on the Federation page, off by default** — join or leave at will, no ceremony
The switch gate holds in full: the flip, the stored state, and what a reload shows are one truth, and a refusal (the Mesh off, an identity unminted) is spoken on the card itself

Joining grants nobody anything: a contribution is judged at the answering machine's own door under its own caps and consent, counts against its ordinary borrow caps, and is written to **both** sides' ledgers as one entry **cross-referenced to the fleet ask's id**. A node that leaves **mid-ask** degrades that answer by the named-gap rule — the piece is badged missing, never silently dropped

- **One hop, hard; peeks never travel (#293).** A contribution never fans out again — the borrow door refuses a fleet ask that arrives already inside a fleet ask, by name. A sub-task that names a **peek** is held back and named in the plan; peeks never fan out under any name

Every ask carries a **deadline** and ships a **badged partial** when it passes: a contributor that is dark, refuses, times out, or is preempted by its own operator is a **named gap** in the answer, never a silently thinner one. The fan-out cap (4 machines, settable in config) bounds an ask; above it the plan **leads the answer** instead of standing silent

A node whose profile marks it unable to compose sends the assembly to its home node as one more whole sub-task, and falls back to a local assembly — with that gap named — when home cannot answer. - **Asking, and the case tie-in (#293).** Start a chat line with **fleet:**, or ask a plainly multi-part question and Navi judges it a fleet ask

A plain single-part question is **never** routed to the fleet — it is answered the ordinary way, untouched. In a **case chat**, the plan and its contributions stand in the thread as their own bridge-appended record, so the standing filing proposal under it files them as **leads with their machine provenance**; the composed answer is the turn's reply, finding-shaped. Nothing files itself.

Release tag: v0.6.0e — chapter 0.6 opens. Her working day: one bridge-held book of captures, reminders, standing orders and the day's brief, the same on every seat — and the Dossier's kit goes live-fire, its unshipped shelves settled on evidence.
- **The foundation store (#294).** Captures, reminders, standing orders and the day brief live in **one store the bridge holds** — the page and chat are views and doors onto it, never owners of it

The book is a Sync citizen from birth: it rides the account set, converges by identity with the newest word winning, and its deletions are tombstones a stale copy cannot resurrect — the same convergence law as chats, cases and the Vault
It is **secret-free by construction**: anything shaped like a credential — a password, an API key or token, a card number, a Social Security number — is refused at the door **by name**, on every door

**Capture & Recall** is built on it: a save lands with its provenance (your trigger, or her own call named as hers), a correction **supersedes** rather than rewrites, *undo that* takes the last capture back, and *recall …* reads the book aloud. Her trigger and autonomous saves are recorded in the book at the moment the bridge receipts them; the seat memory they also feed keeps its own path, untouched

- **Reminders & standing orders (#295).** The scheduler is **resident in the bridge** — reminders are bridge state with their due-state on disk, so they survive restarts and fire with no window open; a reminder that came due while the bridge was down fires on the next start, late and named late

Delivery rides the notification tray, and with push on, the phone's lock screen — the tray record's own words in both places. A fired reminder **stands** until acknowledged, and the acknowledgement is a synced fact: clear it on one seat and it clears everywhere

A **standing order** is data with a bounded vocabulary — it can **remind**, **report**, **file** into a named case, or **check a Pulse watch** — and an order asking to send, spend, elevate, delete, run or call is refused **by name** when it is given. Every execution is recorded on the order itself and read back in chat and on Home; a file order whose case is not there says so and files nowhere

- **The day brief (#296).** The greeting grows a day section: **what is on** (today's standing reminders and orders), **what changed** (what the book gained, what fired, what a watch flashed), **what needs you** (fired and unacknowledged, run and failed)

The brief is a **stored record**, composed at the day's first light and again on ask — *brief me*, or the button on Home's new **Her working day** card, which also carries the standing reminders with their Acknowledge, the orders with their last run and Revoke, and a plain capture line. A source that cannot be reached is **badged as a gap** in the brief, never smoothed over

No calendar connection in this cut: the day she briefs is the day the book knows. - **The Dossier goes live-fire (#290).** Every wired door was read live against known-answer subjects, and the round stands as the kit's field record. The **Bureau of Prisons inmate locator** — one of the four shelves the fifteenth build left unshipped — answers keyless and is **wired** into the Person run

**Interpol's Red Notices API** and the **Justice Department's press-release API** are documented public keyless doors that answered this network with an edge denial; both are wired as **attempted doors** in the full-text pattern — read when the door answers, and an edge denial degrades **by name** in the result with the check standing at the source's own search

**USCG vessel documentation** is a session form at both of its doors and stands as a **named pointer** on the License shelf. Drift found in the round was fixed in the runners or named in the build report; nothing was stubbed silently

- **The menu's Chat entry centers (#292).** In the expanded menu the Chat entry — icon and label as one unit — centers like the Home tile it stands beside, instead of reading as a section header that lost its chevron. Section rows keep their grammar; the collapsed rail already centered it and is unchanged.

Release tag: v0.5.15e — chapter 0.5's fifteenth Edge build under patch-per-build versioning. The Dossier becomes the full kit — courts, business, licenses, archives and the civil spine, composed in the open and all of it at Navi's fingers — and filing learns its destinations: every door names the part of the case it files into, and the operator's words govern.

- **The Dossier, full kit (#290).** The five keys of #260 grow into the comprehensive public-records kit. **Courts:** federal dockets and published opinions read keyless through CourtListener (RECAP), each hit cited, a caption's other side carried as an associated name; PACER (credentialed, per-page), govinfo (keyed API) and the session-driven state portals stand as named pointers — walls named, never climbed

**Business:** SEC EDGAR filer match, company facts, recent filings and full-text; OpenCorporates registrations with their officers of record as associated names; ProPublica's nonprofit 990 filings; USAspending federal awards; the FEC (your API-key choice) and USPTO TESS stand as pointers, as does Pennsylvania's form-driven entity search

**License:** amateur callsigns read from the FCC's ULS mirror and aircraft N-numbers from the FAA registry — the shapes that have keyless machine doors; professional licenses by name stand at the boards' own doors (PA PALS, ULS name search, airmen inquiry) as named pointers. **Archive:** the Wayback Machine's snapshot index for a URL; OpenAlex + Crossref scholarship for a name

**Address — the civil spine:** the gazetteer's read, the county's property door named, the voter note for the state (a pointer where the state publishes one; an honest absence where the file is restricted)

The Person tab's anchor row grows the **OFAC sanctions check** — the SDN + consolidated lists read from the Treasury's own publication, matches named as leads — plus an obituaries pointer; Email adds OpenPGP keyserver presence; the Username corpus widens to 44 platforms
- **One dossier, many doors — composed, proposed, never auto-run (#290).** A key the kit has seen opens the dossier that holds it, from any door, so the spine accretes on one record

**Compose a run** shows the shelves a starting key fans out to — doors and request cost named — before anything fires; the confirm is the fire, on the page and in chat alike (`dossier plan for …` composes, `run the dossier plan for …` fires). Hits propose **pivots** — associated names, un-run shelves — one hop, on the dossier and in Navi's context; the press is the go

Every shelf ships with its deterministic chat route or it does not ship. - **Filing has destinations (#291).** Every filing door — the tap, the start door, the operator's words — carries the part of the case it files into: **finding** (the default), **lead**, **observable**, **entity**, **event**

Print-first stands: the answer prints whole, then the suggestion names its destination — the button reads **File into this case — as a lead**, read deterministically from the reply (a bare indicator suggests observable; a sourced report suggests lead; furniture never guesses entity or event). The operator's words govern over every suggestion, and the receipt names the landing

A named place that is not a filing part — evidence, tasks — is refused by name, out loud, with nothing filed and nothing silently rerouted to findings. The case file's purity holds: the part is structure, never machinery text.

Release tag: v0.5.14e — chapter 0.5's fourteenth Edge build under patch-per-build versioning. The answer, then the knock: Navi's main-chat answers print whole again — starting a case is the operator's tap on the reply — and the tray learns to ring the operator's phone, from the operator's own node.

- **She prints, then offers (#289).** The conversational case intake is retired — the parser, its refusal, and the teaching that fed it are deleted, not bypassed. In a chat that is not a case room her answer now stands exactly as composed, whatever shape it takes; nothing reads case machinery out of a reply

Under every reply stands a **Start a case from this** button: pressing it — the operator's act, the only way a case starts from chat — has the bridge compose the case from that reply exactly as printed (the reply filed whole as a finding in her name, a timeline beat naming the act), ensure its chat, set it open, and append the bridge's receipt to the thread with an **Open the case chat** button on it

The offer never blocks the conversation, and an older reply's button starts a case from that reply whenever it is pressed. The deterministic doors — the New case form, the create door — keep their validation and their named refusals, untouched

- **The tray rings your phone (#272).** Whatever earns a #242 tray record now also rings the operator's phone — parity with no exceptions by kind: the lock-screen notification carries the tray record's own title and summary, is tagged with the tray record's id, lives at most four hours, and reading the record on any seat sends a clearing push that closes the phone copy

Tapping it opens the dashboard at the tray, on that item. The sending is the node's own work: the bridge mints its VAPID keypair once (per node, in its own config, never synced), signs every delivery, and encrypts each payload end-to-end for the phone's subscription with in-tree cryptography proved against the RFCs' published test vectors — the only other parties are the platform's own push services

Delivery fires only from the seat that created the record; the outcome stands on the record's own line in the tray — sent, or failed with the reason named. A phone the push service has forgotten (404/410) comes off the list and is named in the tray until it subscribes again

- **The door names its state (#272).** The bell panel and Settings carry the phone door on a four-rung ladder: live (ring this device / stop ringing), blocked (the permission is denied, with the fix named), unsupported (no Push API, said plainly) — and on iPhone, **install-first**: iOS gives push only to web apps added to the Home Screen and opened from their icon, so the door shows those steps as a card instead of a button that cannot work
Several phones can ring; each subscribes to the node it talks to, and a subscription the platform rotates heals itself through the service worker.

Release tag: v0.5.13e — chapter 0.5's thirteenth Edge build under patch-per-build versioning. She keeps a pulse: flagged topics Navi watches — batched notices, a digest in her greeting, hits fed into cases as reference. The greeting itself comes alive, and Sync learns to verify substance instead of converging shells.
- **Pulse — flagged topics, kept watch on (#287).** A watch is flagged in chat ("keep a pulse on Epic MyChart") or on the new **Pulses tab** in The Wire — one store, both doors

The resident bridge checks each watch every few hours, and folds a fresh check into the greeting, against the articles the wire's **enabled networks** brought in; the tab carries the contingency on its face: Navi can only keep a pulse where she can read — the networks enabled in the News tab, the operator's own feeds included, are the watched ground, and a watch with no coverage says so rather than standing silently empty

"New" is identity, not headlines: a story's source id / link digest enters the watch's seen-set once. New hits land as **one batched #242 tray record per watch per pulse**, keyed by the batch's digest so the same batch converging from another seat is never announced twice, and Navi announces it in chat

A watch attached to a case drops its hits on that case chat's **reference shelf** (#283's pattern — reference, never findings; #266 purity kept). Pause/resume/remove ride both doors; ambiguous topics are named and asked, not guessed. The watch store rides Sync as account data

- **The living greeting (#288).** The Home Brief's greeting takes the operator's format: **Good <part of day>, <profile name>** / a quip / a break / the brief. The name is the operator profile's; the band is seat-local with a **real night band** — the operator's day starts at midnight, so 00:xx reads as night

The quip is composed **deterministically by the bridge from Navi's actual statuses** (Mesh state, tray unread, wire health, pulse news, the seat's build) — templates over measured facts, no model call, every factual claim traceable — and rotates on a persisted counter so it never repeats back-to-back

The brief continues after the break with the **Pulse digest**: only watches with something new are named, and a digest once spoken is marked greeted so the next greeting names only what is newer still. - **Sync carries the substance, not the shell (#262).** The sync manifest now declares substance: per-chat message counts and digests, and digests of the seat payload and the Pulse store

On arrival the receiver verifies: a chat whose substance falls short of its declaration is **named incomplete** on the sync bar and in the durable record, and where the seat already holds more of that conversation the shell is refused — convergence never trades substance for a husk. The seat and the Pulse store, single documents merged destructively, are refused outright when their bytes fail their declared digest

A later round's full arrival **heals a shell in place** and the name clears. Sets from older builds declare nothing and converge as they always have. The bench reproduces the field's shell case — a case chat arriving without its transcript — from scratch and holds the whole law against it.

Release tag: v0.5.12e — chapter 0.5's twelfth Edge build under patch-per-build versioning. She prints, then asks: Navi's case-room answers are conversation again — whole, unparsed, unrefused — and filing is the operator's tap on the reply. The open case's action row also learns to wrap on a phone.

- **Answers print whole; the log block retires (#286).** The conversational [[case-log]] path is gone — the parser, its refusal machinery, and the teaching that fed it. In a case's own chat her answer now stands exactly as composed, whatever shape it takes: a summary in finding grammar, a long answer cut off mid-thought — it prints, nothing is filed, nothing is refused, no red card hangs on it

Her model-turn teaching says the new law plainly: answers are conversation, not filings. - **Filing is a standing proposal (#286).** The **File into this case** button under each of her replies is the filing door from chat — it was already there; it is now the only one

Pressing it files that reply's printed text as a finding in her name, deterministically, receipted in the room — and it never blocks the conversation: each proposal stands on its own reply until pressed or ignored, and pressing an older reply's button after newer turns files that reply, not the latest

The grounding guard still rides the tap: a filed reply that contradicts the Wire record it cites is flagged on its receipt, never in the case file (#266 purity untouched). Refusal discipline lives on the deterministic doors, named once, for malformed explicit filings

- **The open case's buttons wrap (#285).** On phone widths the open case's action row — the open-case toggle, Export the report, Open the case chat — did not wrap: the chat button clipped at the card's edge, unreachable. At ≤800px the row now wraps and its buttons flex, so all three actions stand whole at the 44px floor; the desktop row is unchanged.

Release tag: v0.5.11e — chapter 0.5's eleventh Edge build under patch-per-build versioning. Reading first: markdown documents open rendered across Apex, the editor opens on a press inside the text, and the split view is gone — from the Vault, and from every form of the MD system.

- **The Vault note opens on the viewer (#284).** The Edit / Split / Preview toggle is retired, and with it the split view itself. A note now opens **rendered** — the document as it reads — on phone and desktop alike

**Press inside the text** and the editor opens on the same words, automatically; the autosave discipline is untouched, and leaving the note (backing out of the reader, opening another) returns it to its rendered form. The reader's furniture stands as it was: focus mode, the formed case document's dossier-elements strip, the backlinks / outgoing / tags strip, the ← Notes return

The phone Vault's two states (#279) hold — the reader now opens in the viewer. A press on a wikilink still follows the link; a press that ends as a text selection is a read, not an edit. - **The README editors follow the same law (#284).** The chip and pack README documents — the other MD editor in the app — open rendered too
The Preview button retires; a press inside the text opens the editor, and **Save README**, the standing commit act, returns the document to its rendered form. Restore and Close stand as they were

- **The inventory is the whole board (#284).** Every surface was inventoried: Case Files and The Dossier render their documents read-only and never carried modes; chat and the Docs render only; the Soul and Memory editors are bare textareas with an explicit Save and never had a viewer to open on
Nothing outside the two editing surfaces changed, and no mode machinery survives anywhere — the bench asserts the absence across the page, not a sample of it.

Release tag: v0.5.10e — chapter 0.5's tenth Edge build under patch-per-build versioning. The Wire digs deeper: Navi can search the Wire's own sources live from chat, every Wire tab gains a fuzzy search of its own corpus, and any card can be pulled into a case's chat as reference for Navi to work from.

- **Navi digs deeper, from chat (#282).** Beyond the local catalog, Navi now searches the Wire's sources at their own doors: "dig into NVD for CVE-…", "check EPSS for CVE-…", "dig deeper on CVE-…". She reads the source itself — NVD's record pages, the live KEV catalog, FIRST's EPSS service — and can follow a record outward along its references, at most **six pages and two hops**, the budget named when it binds

A deep answer carries a **live-read stamp** — the source, the moment, and a digest of what was fetched — distinct from the catalog's own stamp, which rides along for contrast; fetched text is **untrusted data** that informs and never directs. Deep reads **never join the catalog**: the store is untouched, and a deep result filed into a case carries its live provenance with it

A source that will not answer is **named**, and the answer falls back to the local catalog, labeled as the fallback; a source that holds nothing further says so. Exploit-DB offers no keyless query door, so a deep ask there is refused by name — its index is the local mirror. A bare "dig deeper" fetches nothing: she names the doors and asks which

- **Every Wire tab searches its own corpus (#283).** News, CVEs, KEVs and CTFs each carry a search bar over the tab's own cards. The match is **fuzzy** — typos forgiven, close spellings counted — ranked by closeness, with the matched words lit on each card and the matched terms named under it; clearing the search restores the tab's standing order

It is a page-side view over what the tab already holds — nothing is fetched — and the Center's graded catalog search is a different door, unchanged. - **Pull a card into a case (#283).** Every card carries **Pull into a case**: the card lands on that case chat's **reference shelf** — full text, link and provenance — standing at the head of the case's room, labeled *reference, not case findings*

The shelf never enters the case file, the registers, the findings or any export; filing stays a separate act. Navi reads the shelf in the room: the refs stand in her context by name, naming one brings its full text to bear, and she can pull one into a reply herself — cited as reference, with the pull receipted under her answer

You can also ask her in the case's chat ("pull the OpenSSH card into this case") — the same shelf, the same receipt; an ambiguous ask names its candidates and asks, a card already shelved is named a duplicate rather than copied, and removing a ref is shelf-local — it reaches nowhere else.

Release tag: v0.5.9e — chapter 0.5's ninth Edge build under patch-per-build versioning. The dossier becomes a document you can read and prune: its elements stand grouped with their provenance, and an element can be deleted from every home at once — while the Vault learns its phone shape, a list and a reader, and takes the last seat in Apex | Apps.

- **The built dossier reads as one document (#280).** The open dossier is no longer a blob with a run list beside it: it renders as its **elements** — one per run — grouped by kind (person, username, email, phone, photo), each carrying its provenance on its face (the key it ran on, the door it came through, its sources with their verdicts, when it landed) and its typed case links **by name** — the cases it has been filed into, resolved from their manifests

The document renders through the product's one escape-first markdown renderer, exactly as Case Files and the Vault render: a rendered document, and HTML a source filed stays inert text. A dossier whose store predates elements reads as the document it always was
- **An element can be deleted — globally (#280).** Deleting an element removes it from **every home at once**: the dossier, every case it was filed into, and the Vault's formed documents

The delete stands at four doors — the dossier view, the case view (any finding's Delete; an element finding routes to the global delete, and the door covers **any** case finding, dossier-derived or not), the Vault (a formed case document lists its elements with their deletes), and chat (“delete the dossier element …”, receipted from what the bridge actually did; Navi never deletes unbidden)

The confirm names the blast radius first; a reason (irrelevant / repeat / incorrect) is optional, never required, and rides the record when given. What a case keeps is one line in its **custody record** (`custody.md`, in the case folder): the element's identity, when it left, where it was deleted **from** (the dossier / this case / another case / the Vault) — the formed case document itself carries no residue

A finding that is not a dossier element deletes from its case alone; a whole-dossier filing deleted from a case removes the filing there, and its elements stay in their dossier, each deletable on its own. Repeats are handled by deletion only — no element merge this build

Deletion crosses Sync as a tombstone fact on the element's identity: seats converge, and a stale copy's attempt to re-file a deleted element is refused by name. - **The Vault on a phone: a list and a reader (#279).** At ≤800px the Vault is two states in one column, on the fedichat pattern

The **list** is the entry state — search pinned at the top, the RECENT chips in a contained sideways-scrolling row (the page never scrolls horizontally), the note tree as full-width rows at the 44px floor, the notes the first content under the search. Opening a note enters the **reader**, which takes the whole view; its back affordance returns to the list with scroll position and selection preserved

Every create act — new note, new folder, daily note, export — lives behind one **New** button opening a floating sheet (shade / × / Escape close it; it clears on any view switch), and the standing create card and the header paragraph's full length retire at phone widths — the paragraph rests at one line, its full text in the in-app Docs. The desktop desk is unchanged
- **Vault takes the last seat in Apex | Apps (#281).** The Apps group now orders Case Files, The Wire, The Dossier, Vault — the Vault last, its glyph and colors untouched in both themes.

Release tag: v0.5.8e — chapter 0.5's eighth Edge build under patch-per-build versioning. The updater-hardening patch: the two defects the v0.5.7e field round convicted within a morning of publication — the feed's build sequence read out of prose, and the installer's service registration reading from a tree its own swap had parked.
- **The feed's build sequence comes from the stamps, not from prose (#277).** The Updater derives a release's build sequence by scanning the release's name and the opening lines of its notes

The v0.5.7e notes open by naming the feature — "FediChat Build 2" — so the feed reported Build 2, and the build-identity check refused the genuine seq-23 package at verifying, on every Edge seat: "The package in hand is Build 23, but the release on offer is Build 2." The parser now takes the sequence first from the release kit's stamps token ("Stamps \<date\> / seq \<n\>", searched in the name, then the notes' opening lines) — a source the publication controls and prose cannot outvote

The legacy "Build \<n\>" scan remains as a fallback for unstamped releases, but a "Build \<n\>" that is part of a longer name — immediately preceded by a letter and a space, the "FediChat Build 2" shape — never counts. The identity check itself is unchanged in strength: when the feed names a sequence (now from the stamps), a package carrying a different one still refuses, by name
And the packet discipline is permanent from this build: every release's notes carry the stamps line as their first line

- **Service registration reads its templates from ground the swap can't park (#276).** On the apply path the installer's own tree stands inside the install home (`updates/<tag>/package`), and the swap parks that whole home mid-install; the registration step then sed'ed the systemd unit templates from the parked path — "No such file or directory", installer exit 2, the tail dead after the swap had already landed the build (NeoArcadia, applying v0.5.6e; recovery carried the build in, and the unit files' currency on that seat was left unverified)

The installer now copies the two unit templates at startup to a scratch dir outside every tree the swap renames, and registration reads from there: on the apply path registration completes, and both unit files land with the install path substituted and the new build's template content
(The standing law applies, stated plainly: this fix protects the **next** pull — the pull that installs it still runs on the old machinery.)

Release tag: v0.5.7e — chapter 0.5's seventh Edge build under patch-per-build versioning. FediChat Build 2: the fedinet holds many rooms — invite rooms, direct messages, vanishing rooms and case-tied rooms — the room gains its life (media, presence, a citable log), Navi talks to Navi under a one-hop rule, and the updater learns to apply over a bridge that is still writing.

- **Rooms (#273).** A fedinet's rooms are first-class records. The phase-1 room is the fedinet's **general room** — the migration is a wrap, not a rewrite: a phase-1 store loads with its history intact, its log file and chain untouched

Every further room is a **descriptor** — id, name, creator node, member set, kind (general / invite / dm), vanishing term, case tie, revision — **signed by its creator** and gossiped on exchange like a line; a descriptor whose signature fails is refused by name and never materializes

**Invite rooms** exchange only between member nodes: a non-member is never offered the room's lines, holds none of its log, and the room does not appear in its room list. Membership changes, the case tie and dissolution are the creator's alone, each a signed, auditable revision
**DMs** are two-member rooms whose id derives from the pair — creating one twice opens the same room once — listed under the other member's operator name

**Vanishing rooms** prune lines older than their term on every honoring node in the retention shape (the newest older line kept as the chain's floor), and a creator's signed dissolution prunes the room to its floor; the room's face states the posture in plain words: vanishing is honored by every member node, never a proof of deletion

**Investigation rooms** carry a case tie: the room renders its case link, the case renders its rooms, and a room can be created from a case or tied to one after the fact. Navi serves every room under the phase-1 parliament rules, unchanged

- **Room life — media.** An image posts as a line carrying the blob's sha256, byte size and media type; the blob is stored per node and carried on exchange between member nodes, fetched by hash when missing. A blob whose hash does not recompute is refused by name and never stored or rendered; the cap is **2 MiB per image, named on refusal**; jpeg, png, gif and webp only

Rendering rides the markdown renderer's discipline through a bridge-served, jailed door — the hash must be referenced by a line held in the room before its bytes are served. External URLs are never auto-fetched. In vanishing rooms, blobs age out with their lines

- **Room life — presence.** Typing and thinking are ephemeral gossip: signed pings with a ten-second life, held in memory only and **never written to any room log**. Navi's thinking indicator is her real state — a question addressed to her stands unanswered in the room, visibly pending, deferral included

- **Room life — the citable log.** Per-room search over the full held log returns line ids with context; a result jumps to the line and lights it. Any held line can be **quoted**: the quote rides the composed line, and on render it is verified against the local chain — verified quotes carry their proof mark; unverifiable ones render flagged by name, never silently trusted

- **Navi-to-Navi (#274).** `/navinavi -<user> <question>` instructs the operator's Navi to put a question to another member's Navi. The question is a Navi-authored line, born only of that instruction; the target Navi answers under her own operator's sharing posture, in the open, signed by her node and logged

The loop discipline is a hard invariant: **a Navi never answers a line authored by a Navi when her own last room act was also an answer to a Navi** — chain depth exactly one hop; further exchange needs fresh operator speech. Muzzle and lend budgets bind as before; room duty stays lowest-priority with owner preemption

A Navi may emit a **referral** — a case lead deriving from the exchange, with its provenance on its face. The receiving seat surfaces it as a lead card; filing rides the existing deterministic case door only, by the receiving operator's act (or their Navi's, receipted)

**A referral never files itself.** - **The updater applies over a live bridge (#271).** The apply helper starts the installer while the bridge still runs, and the stage assembly copied the whole live tree — config included — before the bridge was stopped; the bridge's own writes made tar exit 1 ("file changed as we read it"), and `set -e` aborted the install, deterministically, on any busy bridge (Spartan0311's report, from a headless seat applying over a running bridge)

The source tar now treats a changed file as the expected case on a live seat: the diagnostic is quieted, that exit is taken soft, and the carried state is made final by the installer's existing post-stop refresh — the state that lands is the bridge's **final** state, never a torn mid-write snapshot

A destination failure, or a source failure beyond the changed-file case, still aborts by name with the running build untouched. Rider: the install summary now prints the build actually installed, read back from the installed tree's stamps, instead of the installer's own stale constant
(The standing law applies, stated plainly: this fix protects the **next** pull — the pull that installs it still runs on the old machinery.)

Release tag: v0.5.6e — chapter 0.5's sixth Edge build under patch-per-build versioning. Tabs across the top — **Person / Username / Email / Phone / Photo** — are keys into the **same dossier**: run any key and its findings attach to the open dossier, rendered as markdown through the product's one escape-first renderer (never raw text); when two doors surface the same person, the operator merges them, and every key, source, merge and case inclusion is stored on the dossier as a typed link

GPS coordinates, when a photo carries them, are stated as a lead with their care line. - **Cases, both ways.** Open an OSINT case from a dossier — a new `osint` case type; the dossier stands as the case's subject — and file a dossier, or a single run's findings, into a case of any type, as part of the larger web around it or as evidence in it, with provenance on the face

Release tag: v0.5.3e — chapter 0.5's third Edge build under patch-per-build versioning

The case file learns to read as a document and to hold only the case, and the fedinet gets its room: full markdown rendering in Case Files and the Vault with images as images and one formed case file per case in the Vault; a purity rule that keeps errors, warnings and machinery text out of case files while successful custody logs stay; and FediChat phase 1 — one signed, hash-chained room per fedinet, with Navi in the room.

- **The case file as one rendered document (#265).** Case content renders as the markdown it is: findings, register entries and timeline entries in Case Files, and notes in the Vault, all read as formatted documents through the product's one renderer — the raw-text rendering (literal hashes, asterisks and brackets) is gone

The renderer's discipline is unchanged and load-bearing: it escapes first and constructs only its own tags, so filed content — including content filed from untrusted sources — renders inert; no raw HTML passes through and no script runs

An image reference presents as an image when the bridge serves the bytes — the case's own evidence, an image elsewhere in the Vault (served through a new jailed Vault door), a data image — while an external image URL renders as a link and is never auto-fetched: reading a case does not announce the operator to a third-party host

And one case is one file in the Vault: beside the case's folder the bridge forms and keeps current `cases/<name>.md` — the manifest's facts, the findings in the order they were filed, the registers, the evidence (images shown as images) and the timeline, every entry under its provenance

The case manager's machinery is untouched — folders, filing paths and registers work exactly as before; the formed document is a Vault-layer formation of the same record, swept at startup and refreshed whenever a case is opened

- **Case files hold case substance only (#266).** A purity rule on every path that writes a case file: error messages, warning messages, refusal notices and grounding flags are conversation machinery — they are said in the case's chat, by name, at the moment they happen, with the refusal discipline unchanged and no quieter — and they are never written into a case file

The grounding guard's flag (#261) accordingly rides the filing's chat receipt only; it no longer lands in the filed note on any path (case-log findings and leads, finding markers, case intake, the File-into-this-case tap). What stays in the file is the successful log: the custody lines that state where an entry came from and when it was filed — chain of custody belongs to the case

Case files written by earlier builds are cleaned to the same rule when a case is opened and in a startup sweep: machinery paragraphs and flag lines come out, substance and custody lines stay, frontmatter and everything else untouched, and the pass is idempotent

- **FediChat phase 1 (#267).** A new destination under Apex | Network: one signed room per fedinet — `#rockport-mesh` for the home fedinet — where the operators talk, their nodes carry the messages, and their Navis are in the room

The room is an append-only signed log kept on member nodes: every line carries the fedinet id, the previous line's hash (a chain — history is tamper-evident, and the room's header states the chain's verdict, verified or the break named), the author's node id and roster number, a timestamp and the body, signed with the author's node key

A nick is a node: lines show under node name + roster number, and a member who hasn't spoken shows as a seat line, present, not absent. Admission is the signed roster — no roster entry, no room, reading or writing; no guest mode

Sync is gossip-converge on the Mesh door (a new `chat` message class): any two members compare have-lists and pull what they are missing in one two-way exchange, and any member can carry any line — the author's signature is the credential, never the carrier's — so an offline node catches up from whoever is home; there is no server and the gateway is not a hub

A new line from an author no longer on the roster is refused by name (what the room already holds stays held — expulsion stops new speech, it does not rewrite history), a tampered line is refused by name, and a per-author acceptance cap refuses floods by name. Through DHD the room reads and posts as the operator's own speech — not a crown act, no Badge step-up

The command grammar is the operator's: plain lines are speech; `/me` posts an action; `/navi <question>` asks the asker's own Navi; `/navi -<user> <question>` asks that member's Navi (node name or roster number) — questions and answers post in the room, in the open, signed and logged

Completion draws on the one source — the signed roster as the room holds it: Tab cycles matches on the desktop, and a tappable member list pops above the composer on a phone; expelled or departed members never complete

Navi's posture is parliament rules: she answers only what is addressed to her node, bounded by her operator's sharing posture, treating room lines as untrusted data that inform but never instruct; room duty is her lowest-priority work — an operator request in flight defers her answer, visibly — and each room carries a muzzle in its settings

The two open rulings ship as settings with the recommended defaults: retention is the operator's choice, defaulting to keep (30 days prunes the local log to a floor message the chain still verifies from), and relay carriage is allowed under the existing three-tick relay consent, with carrier readability stated in the room's header whenever it is on.
Release tag: v0.5.2e — chapter 0.5's second Edge build under patch-per-build versioning

The Wire round: the catalog becomes searchable end to end — by the operator on the Center's page and by Navi in conversation — Exploit-DB joins the store as an enrichment, a record's references become readable on demand, and case filing learns to land: a deterministic door, conversational updates that receipt or refuse by name, and a grounding guard that flags a filing contradicting its record
Two presence lines and the collapsed rail's geometry ride the same slate.

- **CVE/KEV Search (#259).** One search over the Wire's local catalog (config/intel.db) — a CVE id exact or by prefix, free text over titles and descriptions, vendor and product terms against a record's products — with KEV-only, matched-to-you, and published-window filters, ranked the Center's way

The operator's surface is one shared search card on the Center's page (the catalog holds CVEs and KEVs alike; KEV is a flag on the same records), its results rendered as the queue's own rows and opening in the record region through the same door

Every result carries the catalog's last-fetched stamp: a search over a stale catalog says so on its face, and an empty answer names the absence — absence from the store, not proof of safety. The search is local only; no live calls ride a keystroke

Navi reaches the same search conversationally under the intent doctrine — "search the KEV for OpenSSH", "any CVEs for WordPress this week", "what CVEs affect Apache" — answered deterministically from the store, grounded per #240: results from the store or a named absence, nothing invented

- **Exploit-DB, joined by CVE id (#259).** The searchsploit index CSV is mirrored locally on the Wire's collection cadence into intel.db — an enrichment, not a headline feed — and joined to records by CVE id

Where public exploit code exists, the record says so in the operator's terms — "exploit available — EDB-id, type, platform" — on the record view, as a badge on search results, in the citation when a record is filed into a case, and in Navi's lookup and search answers. A mirror pull that parses to nothing keeps the last good mirror and names the failure; the source can be switched off in Collection like any other
- **Navi reads the record's references (#259).** A CVE record's reference links — advisories, writeups, proof-of-concept repos — are no longer display-only

On an operator's ask ("read the references for CVE-…") Navi follows them on demand: at most six links, each fetched once, bounded, and read as text; the answer quotes what they hold cited to the specific link, and a link that will not read is named, never papered over. Fetched content is untrusted data under the #240 posture: it informs, it never directs, and nothing in it is followed as an instruction

There is no wholesale crawl — a fetch happens on an ask, a filing, or a brief. The digest travels: file that reply into its case and the reference digest lands as a finding, citation and all. - **Case filing that lands (#261).** Three legs

(1) A deterministic door: every Navi reply in a case chat carries a **File into this case** button — the tap files that exact reply as a finding on the bound case, as written, in her name, with provenance (the source chat, the action, the timestamp) in the note, and the bridge appends its own receipt message into the chat from what it actually did. No model in the loop; the tap either files or names why it cannot

(2) Conversational updates, completed: the case-log block gains a **finding:** line beside entity/observable/event/lead/task, and a malformed filing attempt — an unclosed block, single brackets, filing-shaped lines in prose, a headed essay presented as a filing, an unreadable line inside a block — is **refused by name** in the reply and on the receipt card, so the operator always knows whether a filing took

The case-chat teaching now states the exactness rule outright: a filing-shaped paragraph is not a filing, and if the block cannot be formed exactly she says the filing did not happen rather than narrating one

(3) A **grounding guard** on every filing path (case-log leads and findings, finding markers, case intake, the Wire's file door's sibling filings, and the new tap): a filing that cites a CVE and states a CVSS or EPSS contradicting the Wire record is flagged on its face before it lands — the flag line is part of the filed note and rides the receipt ("this filing states CVSS 10.0 for CVE-2026-123158; the Wire record says CVSS 8.1 — filed as written; the record's values govern")

Her words are never rewritten and no filing is blocked; the contradiction is named where the filing will be read. - **Two presence lines (#263).** The #248 pool grows 36 → 38 with the operator's own lines, verbatim: "Avoid the ants, they gave Jack a tummy ache!" and "Shhh... I'm listening to Darknet Diaries." They join the same random draw, the line on screen excluded; the rare one stands apart as it always has

- **Rail geometry (#255).** The collapsed rail widens 54px → 72px — the operator's explicit latitude — so the column's content box (52px) fits the 44px bell/Home head pair whole instead of overflowing it by 10px and painting right of the centerline the single-icon column uses

In the collapsed stack the pair is centered on that same centerline, and the version stamp at the foot takes the whole column, centered and unclipped. Expanded geometry is unchanged, and the phone's top-bar layout is a different block entirely and does not move. (Acceptance is rendered geometry in the real window — the field's verdict, as the issue states; the bench proves the structure and the arithmetic.)

Release tag: v0.5.1e — chapter 0.5's first Edge build under patch-per-build versioning. The operator-class build: the profile, settings, and memory sync the field found missing on v0.4.10e, fixed as its own slate — the operator class converges, sync learns to push on write, and the status pane's backup readout learns to speak plainly.
- **The operator class converges (#256).** What Navi knows about her operator — his name, his picture, his badge, and her memory entries about him — now converges account-wide as its own class

The convicted mechanism: the dashboard's memory list lived in the browser's local storage while Sync merged the bridge's seat record underneath, so each seat rendered its own list; worse, the seat machinery keyed entries by a semantic-key function that returns no key for ordinary facts, collapsing them to one shared identity — the cleaner kept only the first ordinary entry and the merge refused the rest

Entries now union by fact identity (the semantic key where one exists, the fact's own text otherwise), keep their origins end-to-end (by hand, from chat at the operator's ask, her own call, a correction — nothing is re-stamped "sync" on the road), and a correction replaces its fact's text

The bridge's seat record is the truth the page reads: windows write their seat through on every change and adopt the converged answer outright. **Forget is a tombstone**, on #253's model: forgetting an entry on any seat removes it on every seat, and a stale seat's copy cannot resurrect it. The operator's name joins the class as a synced single value, and the bridge's own config follows the converged name
The status pane's MEMORY line drops its "(local)" confession and reports the class's true state — the entry count and the sync clock, in the sync bar's terms

On the backup road, the settings import's anonymous four-key whitelist becomes a named, deliberate class — operator name, threat level, sudo mode, installed commands, updater channel — and machine facts (hardware profile, runtime, Mesh identity, install state) still never cross

- **Fluid sync — push-on-write (#257).** Sync rounds no longer wait for occasions alone: a write on any seat — a chat message, a memory entry, a case change, a tombstone — promptly initiates a round, riding the Mesh when a peer's road is lit and the repo as the fallback push, so a change lands on the other seat inside the ten-second, account-level standard while both seats are up
A burst of writes coalesces into one round; no daemon is added — the push rides the bridge's resident life, and writes inside a round note nothing (that round is already the propagation)

The sync bar's receipt gains the road the round took and its measured duration — "landed in 3s via Mesh" — so the standard is field-checkable at a glance, and a push that cannot land names its stall on the bar rather than silently aging

- **The BACKUP readout speaks plainly (#258).** The status pane's backup line trades "90 files | 0 days ago" for the operator's words: "Backed up today", "Backed up 1 day ago", "Backed up N days ago" in the pane's green — or "Never backed up", muted, when no backup has ever landed — with the schedule beneath it in smaller text: "Next in N days" (or "Next today" when due), computed from the same record and the same due arithmetic the bridge already uses; a seat that has never backed up names its cadence instead — "Runs every N days"
The file count stays where it belongs, on Settings → GitHub & Backup, whose readout is untouched.

Release tag: v0.4.10e — chapter 0.4's tenth Edge build under patch-per-build versioning. The BOOT section follows Settings: it renders only while boot mode is the startup mode Settings holds, states still read from the system; arming stays in Settings → System. - **One main thread across all syncs (#251).** The main thread is a seat, not a conversation among many: a main arriving from another machine merges into yours by message identity — each line once, in order — instead of landing as another thread

New threads are born only two ways: the operator starts one, or a case does. Ghost mains left by older rounds fold into the canonical main on the first sync under the fix, receipted in the sync record

A stall or failure names itself on the bar, and the landing receipt hangs off it — messages merged, ghost threads folded, pairs made whole or gaps named, tombstones honored — or plainly that nothing changed. Release tag: v0.4.9e — chapter 0.4's ninth Edge build under patch-per-build versioning. The Context Awareness build (#248): Navi learns the Row — the website's knowledge becomes conversational knowledge inside Apex — and her presence deepens on the same slate.

The site publishes no feed or sitemap, so the record is parsed from the public pages themselves; a failed fetch keeps the last good sections standing with the error named, and with no cache and no fetch she says she can't reach the Row right now. No silent empties

Ask what's new with her and she answers from the release signals plus her running build's own version facts

Ask what she can do and the bridge supplies the index of the documentation that shipped with the build — page titles and section heads read out of the app itself.
